# Implementation design

This document maps [`docs/protocol.md`](protocol.md) (version 1.4) onto code for the whole first
release of §29: the Quint model, the pure Rust core with executable invariants, the Kani harnesses,
the MCP shell over SQLite, and the tests. It is the contract that the implementation agents share:
every type, enum variant, field, event, and function signature that crosses a work-package boundary
is spelled out here. The specification wins on any conflict. A conflict is a bug in this document;
it is fixed here, or, where the specification itself is ambiguous or contradictory, it is listed in
D.14 for a decision, and accepted amendments land in `docs/protocol.md` before any code relies on
them (AGENTS.md: "Specification first, code second"): the G0 items in 1.2, and the items found
after 1.2 was written (D.14.2) in 1.2 too, because they were accepted before 1.2 was released.
Version 1.3 adds next calls to every response (§20.9): the design implements them as a pure query
(D.8.26), and the choices behind them were confirmed on 2026-10-02 (D.14.3). Version 1.4 carries
the decisions on the first usability test of 1.3: responses that say what a call did, new branches
of the next calls, a few changed rules, and fixes of defects the test found; D.14.4 maps each
recommendation to the place that implements it.

Section numbers of the form §N refer to the specification. Section numbers of the form D.N refer to
this document. Items of the form A-N are the ambiguities of D.14.

Contents: D.0 principles and gate · D.1 crates and trusted computing base · D.2 primitive types ·
D.3 parameters · D.4 state · D.5 context and commands · D.6 results and the core API · D.7 events and
`evolve` · D.8 algorithms · D.9 invariants · D.10 Quint model · D.11 shell · D.12 tests ·
D.13 implementation plan · D.14 ambiguities and amendments (D.14.4: 1.4) · D.15 scale, tenancy,
and autonomy · D.16 next calls in the examples · Appendix A traceability · Appendix B entity
transitions to events · Appendix C parameters to uses.

## D.0 Principles and the specification gate

### D.0.1 Gate G0: the specification comes first

No work package of D.13 starts until every item that D.14 marks **Amend** (behaviour or contract
changes) or **Decide** has been decided, and WP-S has written the decisions into
`docs/protocol.md` 1.2, with a row in "What changed", in one commit, before WP-0. Every item of the
scale review that changes behaviour, D-1 to D-4 and D-6 included, is **Amend**.

**G0 was decided on 2026-10-02** (D.14.1). Every Amend item and every **Clarify** item was accepted.
Every Decide item follows its recommendation, except A-23, A-61, and A-63, where the alternative was
chosen; those three now change what agents see, and 1.2 states them. 1.2 is written on the
analysts' quantitative models, and the year simulation is built later, as a regression check before
the release (G0-c). No item was declined, so D.14's "If declined" column applies nowhere; it stays as
the rationale.

Items found after 1.2 was written are listed in D.14.2. All six (A-113 to A-118) were accepted as
proposed, also on 2026-10-02. 1.2 was not yet released, so they are written into 1.2 itself, with
"What changed" rows, and not into a 1.3; the design implements them. Writing them into 1.2 added a
few details that the proposals did not contain; D.14.2 lists them apart, confirmed on 2026-10-02,
and does not count them as accepted.

**Version 1.3** (response guidance, §20.9) was written on 2026-10-02, after 1.2, from a proposal
that ties each rule to the slip it prevents. It follows the recommendation of each of its ten
choices, and all ten were confirmed on 2026-10-02 (D.14.3). The guidance adds no base state,
event, entity, or refusal: it amends WP-D1 (the types of D.8.26), WP-D2 (four derived indices,
D.4.10), and WP-D5b (one reply field, D.6.2, and the shared helper `conversation_holder`,
D.8.26), and the query, its check, its model, and its rendering are packages of their own (WP-D7,
WP-A5, WP-E3, D.13.2).

1.3 also records the decisions taken on 2026-10-02 while wave 1 was built. A `said` answers
only the earlier requests of its own conversation (§9.4, D.8.8, D.14.3): `Request` keeps the
conversation key that `Appended(Request)` already carries, and `NodeItems::unanswered` is indexed
by it. This amends WP-D1 (`Request::conv`), WP-D2 (`evolve`'s filing, the index, and Settled's
state check), WP-D4 (the merge's crediting, D.8.20), and WP-D5b (`said`'s answers, D.8.15), and in
the model WP-A1 (`Request.conv` and `CSaid`'s `where`, D.10.3), WP-A2 (`act_request` and
`act_said`, D.10.4), and WP-A3 (the `people` slice, D.10.7). WP-A1 merged before this decision, so
its part lands in a follow-up. Likewise, a `said` fulfils only the open commitments of its own
conversation (§9.2, D.8.15, D.14.3), which was decided after reviewing 1.3's decisions. A
commitment already keeps the conversation key that `CommitmentOpened` carries, `Commitment::conv`,
so no type, event, or index changes. This amends WP-D4 (C1's step check, D.9.2), WP-D5b (`said`'s
commitment events, D.8.15), and WP-D7 (rule 9's status replies, D.8.26), and in the model WP-A2
(`act_said`, D.10.4), WP-A3 (`step_C1`, D.10.7), and WP-A5 (rule 9 in `guide.qnt`). The cron rules
and search window (§12, D.11.10, D.8.18) are written as `forum-cron` implements them, and the
version 1 key rules (§7, D.11.14) as they were decided in three rounds, all of which
`forum-keys` implements.

**Version 1.4** (the usability round, D.14.4) was written on 2026-10-02 from the decisions on the
first usability test of 1.3, whose recommendations are R1 to R27 of the test's report. R1 to R6, R8
to R21, R24, R25, and R27 were accepted, and R7, R22, and R23 deferred. 1.4 adds no entity,
no error code, and no new kind of refusal: `invalid(NoIntent)` now also covers a release's
`intent_done` with no intent open (§25 Intent), and an argument of another form of `ask` is an
unknown argument, a plain parameter error. It removes one refusal (a decision's basis naming its
own node is now dropped with a warning, R14) and strengthens one invariant (H2: a session is never
silent while a hold it took is live, R27). It adds two base fields, `Hold::reopened` (R4) and
`Session::told` (R13), one command argument, `hold release {intent_done}` (R15), and one firing
effect, the copy of a series' fields when its occurrence becomes available (R10), and it moves the
Silence deadline of a holder to the end of its last lease (R27). The rest is response shapes,
warnings, next-call branches, and the shell's text.
WP-D1 is being written when 1.4 lands, so the types it freezes are 1.4's; every later package
builds its 1.4 part with the rest, and the merged model packages get follow-ups (D.13.1).

Everything below follows these decisions. Each place that depends on an item names it, for example
"(A-10)", each place that 1.3 adds names its rule or §20.9, and each place that 1.4 changes says
"1.4" and names its R item (D.14.4).

### D.0.2 Design principles

1. **Base state and derived indices are separate.** `State` has a base part (the facts, mirrored one
   to one by the Quint model), a history part (statistics and candidate ages, which depend on the
   order of events), and an `ix` part (flags, rollups, key and name lookups, the candidate index,
   and the deadline queue). Every index has a full-recount function. R1, F, and T4 reduce to "index
   equals recount". The base and history parts are what the shell keeps in its SQLite state tables,
   the source of truth (D.11.6, FQ-2); the indices are recounted from them at startup (D.11.8).
2. **One event, one transition.** Each event is one §25 transition of one entity, one creation, or
   one field change of one node, plus the bookkeeping owned by that one node (its holds, wait,
   intent, tags, marks, counters). `evolve` rejects a transition from a state that §25 does not allow
   by counting an anomaly (D.7.5). Events carry every derived value: ids, `seq`, `at`, lease ends,
   deadline times.
3. **Time is a predicate where the specification says so.** Leases, waits, pauses, refusal liveness,
   session silence, and archiving are pure functions of `(S, now)` (T3, AR). Deadlines exist to apply
   §25 transitions and to re-materialise flags at the instant a predicate changes; they never decide
   a predicate's value.
4. **The deadline queue is a function of the base state.** Every deadline owner has a pure
   `deadline_of`, which returns `None` once the deadline has fired (its transition happened, or its
   owner's one-shot marker is set). A cancelled deadline is one whose owner changed; it is no longer
   in the recount, so it cannot fire (T4).
5. **Validate, then execute.** A command is checked against the state first; only the check can fail.
   Execution cannot fail: it emits events and applies each one with `evolve` immediately, so later
   steps of the same command see their own effects and the next free ids ("plan by doing").
6. **Node content is in the core; feed texts are not.** Title, body, fields, files, status, digest,
   and agreements are in the core state, so that `version` increases exactly when content changes
   (O2). The texts of feed entries travel in commands and are recorded once, in the events of the
   history, so the history is complete; the shell renders and indexes them from there (D.11.6,
   D.11.12), and the core never holds them.
7. **Every loop is bounded** by a parameter or by the size of a collection, so that Kani can unwind
   it and Verus can later give it a decreasing measure.
8. **No feature without a failure it prevents** (AGENTS.md). Where the specification describes
   something that has no observable effect in the first release (`expects`, `learnings`, the
   evidence kinds, the external notification relay), it is accepted and stored, or left out, and
   listed in D.14. The basis of a decision is stored as references from the first release on,
   because a basis recorded as prose could never feed a later check (CS-22).
9. **The core's memory follows what is live, not the history** (CS-8, CS-17, D-5). Sessions retire,
   `op_id` records, addressed notes, and agent questions expire, and feed metadata is kept only for
   entries that an entity or the `moved` warning needs; the rest is in the history (D.11.6).
   Finished entities (a settled request, an answered question, a confirmed `said`, a superseded
   decision) leave memory `FINISHED_RETAIN` after they finish; their rows stay in the state tables,
   from which the shell reads them and a command that names one restores it (D.4.12).

### D.0.3 Verification scope (decided on 2026-10-02)

Only the **key invariants** are checked formally: H1 to H6 (holds and fencing), O1 and O2 (retries and
versions), K1, K3, K4, K5, and T5 (keys, the tree, merges, and waits without cycles), T1 to T4 (time),
and the totality of `evolve` (no panic on any event), with the determinism guard rails of D.1.3.
For them the Quint model (the `holds`, `keys`, and time parts, checked with TLC, and with Apalache only
where it reaches) and Kani harnesses stay. Every other invariant keeps its executable check in
`check_invariants` or `check_step` and is exercised by unit tests, property tests (with the checks
after every step), and scenario tests, but gets no Quint or Kani work. Verus proofs are a later,
optional step for the key invariants only.

This overrides every other part of this document: where D.9.2, D.10, D.12.5, or a row of D.13.2 asks
for a Kani harness, a Quint invariant, a model slice, a model action, or a Verus TODO for an invariant
outside the key set, it is no longer required, and a package need not build it. WP-A5 (next calls in
the model) is dropped; WP-A3 covers the key invariants only; WP-F1 replays traces of the key parts
only. The registry (D.9.4) records "tests" as the level for the other invariants.

## D.1 Crate layout, dependency graph, and trusted computing base

### D.1.1 Workspace

```
Cargo.toml                 [workspace] resolver = "3", members = ["crates/*"]
                           [workspace.package] edition = "2024", rust-version = "1.94", license = "MIT"
rust-toolchain.toml        channel = "1.94", components = ["clippy", "rustfmt"]
clippy.toml                disallowed-types and disallowed-methods (D.1.3)
crates/
  forum-cron/              pure, no_std + alloc: civil calendar, frozen time-zone tables, 5-field
                           cron, next_slot
  forum-keys/              pure (std): versioned key normalisers; used by the shell only
  forum-core/              pure, no_std + alloc: types, apply/decide, settle, evolve, queries,
                           executable invariants, invariant registry, Kani harnesses
  forum-server/            the shell: MCP streamable HTTP, sessions, SQLite log, rendering, search,
                           masking, configuration
  forum-conformance/       test-only (publish = false): Quint trace replay
  swarm-sim/               test-only (publish = false): the load driver of the scale gates (D.12.8,
                           D.15): simulated agents over MCP HTTP
model/                     the Quint model (package.json pins @informalsystems/quint 0.33.0)
scripts/verify.sh          runs every check and prints which ran (D.12.9)
usability/                 1.3: the usability test with live agents (WP-U), run only with
                           `verify.sh --usability`
docs/protocol.md           the specification
docs/design.md             this document
docs/verification.md       generated invariant registry, Verus TODOs, traceability (WP-F3)
```

There is no `sim/` crate in the first release. The year simulation stays planned (README). 1.2 is
written on the analysts' quantitative models, and the year simulation is built later, outside this
repository, as work package WP-Y: it runs with the profiles of D.15.4 before the release, as a
regression check, and is not a gate for 1.2 (G0-c, CS-23, D.13.2).

### D.1.2 Dependency graph

```
forum-cron ──────► forum-core ──────► forum-server ◄────── forum-keys
    │                  │                  ▲               (url, unicode-normalization)
    │                  │                  │
    └──────────────────┼──────────────────┘   (the shell parses cron itself)
                       │
                       └──► forum-conformance (dev only: quint-connect, itf, serde_json;
                                               also uses forum-cron)
```

| Crate | Normal dependencies | `no_std` | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `forum-cron` | `serde` (optional, feature `serde`, `derive` + `alloc`) | yes (`alloc`) | Pure arithmetic over a frozen time-zone table supplied as data. Never reads a tz database. Inside the verified boundary |
| `forum-keys` | `url` 2.5, `unicode-normalization` 0.1 | no | Shell-side, pure, idempotent, property-tested. Not a dependency of the core (§24) |
| `forum-core` | `forum-cron`; `serde` (optional, feature `serde` enables `forum-cron/serde`) | yes (`alloc`), except under `test` and `kani` | The verified core. Two test-only features add code and change nothing else, except that `conformance` gives the two durations of the next calls the model's ticks: `testkit` (`World`, D.12.1) and `conformance` (`apply_with` and `TieBreak`, D.6.1; `query::guide_items`, D.8.26); the server enables neither |
| `forum-server` | `forum-core[serde]`, `forum-cron[serde]`, `forum-keys`, `rmcp` 3.5 (`server`, `transport-streamable-http-server`), `axum` 0.8, `tokio` 1, `rusqlite` 0.40 (`bundled`, `hooks`, `backup`), `zstd` 0.14, `jiff` 0.2 (`default-features = false`, `std`, `tzdb-bundle-always`), `jiff-tzdb` 0.1, `sha2` 0.11, `serde`, `serde_json`, `toml` 1, `regex` 1, `tracing`, `tracing-subscriber` | no | The shell. Dev: `rmcp` feature `transport-streamable-http-client-reqwest`, `proptest` 1.11 |
| `forum-conformance` | `forum-core[serde, conformance]`, `forum-cron[serde]`, `quint-connect` 0.1.2, `itf` 0.4, `serde`, `serde_json` | no | Never linked into the server |
| `swarm-sim` | `reqwest` 0.13 (default features off), `tokio`, `serde`, `serde_json` | no | A load driver for the scale gates (D.12.8, D.15); it speaks MCP over streamable HTTP like any client, with a minimal JSON-RPC client of its own rather than `rmcp`'s, so that it controls when each call is sent (latency is measured from a call's intended time, without coordinated omission) and keeps one connection per simulated agent; it links no forum crate |

`forum-core` and `forum-cron` start with `#![cfg_attr(not(any(test, kani)), no_std)]` and
`extern crate alloc;`. `no_std` makes the most important exclusions structural: there is no
`std::collections::HashMap`, no `std::time`, no `std::fs`, no threads, and no environment in `alloc`.
Collections are `alloc::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet}` and `alloc::vec::Vec` only.

The core never sees a time-zone database or a normaliser: the shell turns an IANA zone name into a
`TzTable` (a list of UTC offset transitions, D.11.10) and keys into normalised strings with their
normaliser version, both before the command is built. Both travel inside the command and are recorded
in its events and the state, so neither loading the state nor replaying the history ever consults
`jiff` or `forum-keys`, and a tzdb update changes only series created or updated afterwards.

### D.1.3 Lints that enforce determinism

`crates/forum-core/src/lib.rs` and `crates/forum-cron/src/lib.rs` start with:

```rust
#![cfg_attr(not(any(test, kani)), no_std)]
#![forbid(unsafe_code)]
#![deny(
    clippy::float_arithmetic,
    clippy::float_cmp,
    clippy::arithmetic_side_effects,   // only checked_*, saturating_*, wrapping_* (FNV)
    clippy::indexing_slicing,
    clippy::unwrap_used,
    clippy::expect_used,
    clippy::panic,
    clippy::unreachable,
    clippy::todo,
    clippy::unimplemented,
    clippy::as_conversions,            // casts go through From/TryFrom
    clippy::iter_over_hash_type,
    clippy::disallowed_types,
    clippy::disallowed_methods,
    clippy::wildcard_enum_match_arm,   // every match names every variant
)]
```

`clippy.toml` at the workspace root (it applies to every crate; the shell needs no hash map in this
design, so it carries no exemption):

```toml
disallowed-types = [
  { path = "std::collections::HashMap", reason = "iteration order is not deterministic" },
  { path = "std::collections::HashSet", reason = "iteration order is not deterministic" },
  { path = "std::time::SystemTime",     reason = "time enters the core through Ctx only" },
  { path = "std::time::Instant",        reason = "time enters the core through Ctx only" },
]
disallowed-methods = [
  { path = "std::time::SystemTime::now", reason = "only forum_server::clock::now_ms reads the clock" },
  { path = "std::time::Instant::now",    reason = "only the shell's long poll measures time" },
  { path = "std::env::var",              reason = "configuration is read once, in forum_server::config" },
]
```

The shell reads the wall clock in exactly one function, `forum_server::clock::now_ms()`, and measures
the `talk wait` timeout in `forum_server::wait`; both carry a local `#[allow]` with a comment.

`scripts/verify.sh` adds three guard rails that lints cannot express:
- `cargo tree -p forum-core -e normal --prefix none --features serde` must list only `forum-core`,
  `forum-cron`, `serde`, `serde_core` (a dependency of `serde` since 1.0.220; the local registry has
  1.0.229), `serde_derive`, `proc-macro2`, `quote`, `syn`, and `unicode-ident`;
- `rg -n '\bf(32|64)\b' crates/forum-core/src crates/forum-cron/src` must find nothing;
- a probe copies `forum-core` to a temporary directory, adds a test module that uses
  `std::collections::HashMap`, and checks that `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` fails.

### D.1.4 Trusted computing base

Verified (Kani now, Verus later): `forum-core` and `forum-cron`.

Trusted, not proved, as §28 lists:

| Component | Why it is trusted | What checks it |
|---|---|---|
| rustc 1.94, Kani 0.68 with CBMC, Quint 0.33, Apalache, TLC | Tools | — |
| SQLite (bundled by `rusqlite`) and `zstd` | Storage: the state tables, the history, the search index; compression of the history | The four constraints of §24 on the state tables as a second line of defence; the persist-and-reload and history-replay tests (D.12.6); triggers that keep the history append-only |
| `forum-server` (the shell), including `rmcp`, `axum`, `tokio` | IO, rendering, JSON, search, masking | Unit and property tests, fuzzing, the §32 scenario over HTTP, the live race test, crash tests |
| `forum-keys` | Normalisation | Property tests for idempotence and totality; K2 checked by the shell's `check_keys` (D.11.8) |
| `jiff` and `jiff-tzdb` | Build the frozen `TzTable` passed into the core | Cross-check tests against `forum-cron`'s own arithmetic |
| SHA-256 (`sha2`), canonical JSON (`serde_json`) | The `op_id` digest and the bearer-token hashes; the encoding of state rows and events (D.7.6) | Round-trip and golden tests; the persist-and-reload test decodes every state row it wrote (D.12.6) |
| The Quint model and its correspondence with the core | Tested by trace replay, not proved | `forum-conformance` |

FNV-1a-64 lives in the core (it decides `next`) and is checked by Kani against pinned test vectors;
it is not part of the trusted base.

## D.2 Primitive types and units

All types are in `forum_core::types` unless marked otherwise. Every type derives
`Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Debug`; the integer newtypes also derive `Copy, Default`;
`forum-cron`'s public types derive the same. Under the `serde` feature every type of the state,
commands, events, and results derives `Serialize, Deserialize`, with two exceptions:
- the invariant registry and violation types (`InvariantInfo`, `Violation`, `ViolationDetail`,
  D.9) hold `&'static` data, so they derive `Serialize` only (`#[cfg_attr(feature = "serde",
  derive(Serialize))]`);
- every newtype over `String` (`Name`, `Label`, `ClassName`, `OpId`, `KeyStr`, `PrincipalKey`)
  deserialises through its validating constructor with `#[serde(try_from = "String", into =
  "String")]`, so a decoded event or command cannot smuggle in an invalid value.

No type derives `Hash`. Every newtype over `String` has a private field and a validating constructor
(`Name::new(&str) -> Option<Name>`), so an invalid value cannot exist inside the core.

`kani::Arbitrary` cannot be derived for types that hold `String`, `Vec`, or `BTreeMap`. Under
`cfg(kani)` the integer newtypes and the field-less enums derive it; every other type a harness needs
gets a hand-written bounded generator in `forum-core/src/kani/gen.rs` (for example a `Name` from a
two-letter alphabet, a map of at most 2 entries), so each harness's unwinding bound covers its
input.

No `Option<Option<T>>` appears in a command or an event: `serde_json` writes `None` and `Some(None)`
both as `null` and reads `null` back as `None`, so a cleared field would replay as "unchanged".
Three-state fields use `Change<T>`:

```rust
/// A field change in a patch. `Keep` is the serde default, so an absent field means Keep.
#[derive(Default)]
pub enum Change<T> { #[default] Keep, Clear, Set(T) }
```

### D.2.1 Time and durations

```rust
/// Milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z. The core's only notion of time.
pub struct Time(pub u64);

/// A non-negative duration in milliseconds.
pub struct Dur(pub u64);

/// An agent-supplied point in time: absolute, or relative to the command's clamped `now`.
pub enum When { At(Time), In(Dur) }

impl Time {
    pub const ZERO: Time = Time(0);
    /// Saturating: a deadline never wraps.
    pub const fn plus(self, d: Dur) -> Time { Time(self.0.saturating_add(d.0)) }
    /// Saturating at zero.
    pub const fn minus(self, d: Dur) -> Time { Time(self.0.saturating_sub(d.0)) }
    pub const fn since(self, earlier: Time) -> Dur { Dur(self.0.saturating_sub(earlier.0)) }
}
impl When {
    pub const fn resolve(self, now: Time) -> Time {
        match self { When::At(t) => t, When::In(d) => now.plus(d) }
    }
}

pub const SECOND: Dur = Dur(1_000);
pub const MINUTE: Dur = Dur(60_000);
pub const HOUR: Dur = Dur(3_600_000);
pub const DAY: Dur = Dur(86_400_000);
```

Units:
- **Time and durations: milliseconds, `u64`.** Milliseconds keep `taken_at < lease_until` (H5)
  strict and match the shell's clock. `u64` avoids negative times in Kani and Quint; every addition
  saturates.
- **`est` and `horizon`: minutes, `u32`** (§5, §10.4).
- **Byte budgets: bytes, `u32`** (`hello.budget` = 4,096 bytes of rendered UTF-8).
- **Cron slots: whole minutes**, stored as `Time` with `t.0 % 60_000 == 0`.
- **Day indices** (statistics, coverage): `u64` days since the epoch, `day_of(t) = t.0 / 86_400_000`,
  or local days through `forum_cron::local_day_hour` where the coverage check needs them.

### D.2.2 Identifiers and counters

```rust
pub struct NodeId(pub u64);     // Counters::next_node; 0..=7 are the reserved nodes
pub struct Eid(pub u64);        // global feed-entry id, Counters::next_eid, first is 1
pub struct SessionId(pub u64);  // Counters::next_session, first is 1
pub struct Seq(pub u64);        // per-node feed sequence; first entry is 1, 0 means empty
pub struct Version(pub u64);    // per node, for version and digest_version; a new node has 1
pub struct Fence(pub u64);      // per-node hold counter; a new node has 0, the first token has 1
pub struct PrincipalId(pub u32); // Counters::next_principal; 0 is the reserved `user` (CS-1)

/// Hold token "<node id>.<fence>". The hold's identity: holds are keyed by token.
pub struct Token { pub node: NodeId, pub fence: Fence }

/// Every entity born from a feed entry has that entry's Eid as its id.
pub type RequestId = Eid;
pub type QuestionId = Eid;     // people, agent, and user questions
pub type SaidId = Eid;
pub type CommitmentId = Eid;   // the eid of the opening `ack`
pub type DecisionId = Eid;
pub type ObjectionId = Eid;
pub type UserEntryId = Eid;    // `from_user` entries
pub type DigestId = Eid;
pub type NoteId = Eid;         // addressed messages: say, agent questions, agent answers

pub const ROOT: NodeId = NodeId(0);            // "/"
pub const USER: NodeId = NodeId(1);            // "/@user"
pub const USER_DECISIONS: NodeId = NodeId(2);  // "/@user/decisions"
pub const USER_DIGEST: NodeId = NodeId(3);     // "/@user/digest"
pub const SYS: NodeId = NodeId(4);             // "/sys"
pub const SIGNALS: NodeId = NodeId(5);         // "/sys/signals"
pub const PEOPLE: NodeId = NodeId(6);          // "/@people": the directory of people (FQ-5, D-3)
pub const TEAMS: NodeId = NodeId(7);           // "/@teams": the directory of teams (FQ-5, D-3)
pub const FIRST_FREE_NODE: NodeId = NodeId(8);

/// The reserved principal `user`, interned by Genesis: the principal of every entry when no other
/// is known, and the last stage of every addressee chain (CS-1, CS-2).
pub const USER_PRINCIPAL: PrincipalId = PrincipalId(0);
```

External forms, parsed and rendered by the core (Kani proves the round trips): node ids `#12`, entry
ids `e57`, session ids `s-4`, tokens `12.3` (`Token::parse(&str) -> Option<Token>`,
`Token::render(&self) -> String`). A principal is shown by its key (`mail:alice@corp.example`, or
`user`), never by its id. `chat/` and `kb/` are not reserved; they are ordinary nodes made on demand
by `node create`. `@people` and `@teams` are reserved (Genesis makes them, so the server can find the
directory and nobody can move, merge, or close it), and their children are ordinary nodes that agents
create and edit with the existing node commands (FQ-5, D-3, D.11.9):
- a **person** is an open child of `@people` that carries `person:<principal key>` keys, one per
  alias of that human (`person:mail:bob@corp.example`, `person:slack:t01/u02bob`); K1 keeps each alias
  on at most one open node, so create-or-join finds the person by any alias and a second claim raises
  a `duplicate` signal; the tag `gone` marks a leaver;
- a **team** is an open child of `@teams`; its members are the person nodes named by its own
  `owners` setting, never an inherited one, so a team with none has no members (§4, D.4.3, A-116);
- a work node's **owners** are the `owners` of the nearest node among it and its ancestors whose
  `owners` is not empty, ROOT included: person or team nodes, a team standing for its members.

The server reads the directory in five places only (§4): the addressee chain of a question for the
user (D.8.12), the digest's audience (D.8.13), alias resolution, which treats every alias of one
person as that person (`same_person`, D.8.11), `is_container`, by which only their flags make
persons and teams candidates for `next` (D.4.3, A-113), and the child limit, which does not count
them (D.8.4, A-113). The last two read only the parent: every child of `@people` or `@teams`
counts, with or without `person:` keys (`is_directory`, D.4.3). `@<class>` mailboxes are not
created in the first release, because class addressing is a later release (A-82).

### D.2.3 Labels, names, paths, classes, operations, text

```rust
/// A class name from the bearer-token configuration: [a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}.
pub struct ClassName(String);

/// Tags, kind, needs, caps: [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_.:-]{0,63}. The core reads two tags: `offer`, and
/// `gone` on a person node (D.2.2).
pub struct Label(String);
pub const OFFER: &str = "offer";
pub const GONE: &str = "gone";

/// One path step: 1..=128 bytes of UTF-8, no '/', no control characters, not "." or "..",
/// no leading or trailing whitespace, not starting with '#'.
pub struct Name(String);

/// A path as a sequence of names from the root. "/" is the empty sequence.
pub struct Path(pub Vec<Name>);

/// How a command names a node: by path (resolved step by step, §4) or by id ("#12").
pub enum NodeRef { Path(Path), Id(NodeId) }

/// Client-chosen retry id: 1..=64 bytes of printable ASCII.
pub struct OpId(String);

/// A principal: a human an agent serves (§3, CS-1), taken at the agent's word. Either the reserved
/// "user", or "<scheme>:<value>" (`mail:alice@corp.example`, `slack:t01/u02abc`), at most 256
/// bytes, already normalised by the shell (`forum_keys::normalise_principal`, D.11.14). The `user:`
/// scheme is refused, because it names log entries (`user:e12`). A principal key is not itself a node
/// key, and a principal is never a permission; a person node carries it inside a `person:<key>` key
/// (D.2.2, D.2.4), to which K1 and K2 apply.
pub struct PrincipalKey(String);
pub const USER_KEY: &str = "user";

/// SHA-256 of the request after secret masking (computed by the shell, compared by the core, D.8.1,
/// D.11.5, CS-35), so a stored digest reveals nothing that masking removed.
pub struct ReqDigest(pub [u8; 32]);

/// Free text, already masked by the shell. The core compares node-content texts for equality
/// (O2) and measures lengths in bytes: the digest's (digest.max) and every text of a command
/// (text.max, L1, A-114); it never parses text.
pub struct Text(pub String);
```

### D.2.4 Keys

```rust
/// A normalised key "<scheme>:<value>". The identity of a key is this string only. A request's
/// origin is stored like a key, as a `Key` with its normaliser version (§7: "message ids are
/// normalised like keys"; K2 covers every origin, A-61): the id of the message it came in, in its
/// conversation's scheme (`chat:<channel>/<thread>/<message>`, `issue:<project>#<n>/<comment>`,
/// `mail:<message-id>`, D.11.14), a `user:e<n>` entry (`NormVer(0)`), or, when the message has no
/// id, the conversation key. The core never parses one: it compares origins by their `KeyStr` for
/// Q1 and passes them through.
pub struct KeyStr(String);

/// Normaliser version recorded with every stored key and every request's origin (K2). Version 0
/// marks keys and origins the core makes itself (`user:e<eid>` on routing, `repeat:<id>:<slot>`),
/// whose canonical form is fixed by construction; versions 1.. are `forum_keys::VERSION` values.
pub struct NormVer(pub u16);

/// A key as it arrives in a command: already normalised by the shell (§7).
pub struct Key { pub key: KeyStr, pub nv: NormVer }

impl KeyStr {
    /// Text before the first ':'.
    pub fn scheme(&self) -> &str;
    /// A conversation key names a conversation with people outside the swarm (§9.1): its scheme
    /// is one of `params.conversation_schemes` (by default `chat`, `issue`, and `mail`); every
    /// other scheme names an object, such as a paper or a proof (A-30, CS-36).
    pub fn is_conversation(&self, schemes: &BTreeSet<Label>) -> bool;
    /// `repeat:` keys are made only by the server (A-90): an agent-supplied key with this scheme
    /// is `invalid(ReservedKey)`, and `forum-keys` rejects the scheme as well.
    pub fn is_reserved(&self) -> bool;
    /// `user:e<eid>` keys route `from_user` entries (§8.2).
    pub fn user_entry(&self) -> Option<UserEntryId>;
    /// `person:<principal key>` names one alias of a person (D.2.2, FQ-5): the value is a principal
    /// key, normalised by `forum_keys::normalise_principal` (D.11.14); `user` is allowed, so that one
    /// human's anonymous client and named client can be one person.
    pub fn person(&self) -> Option<PrincipalKey>;
    /// The canonical key of a user entry: "user:e<eid>".
    pub fn of_user_entry(e: UserEntryId) -> KeyStr;
    /// The canonical key of an occurrence: "repeat:<series id>:<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>".
    pub fn of_occurrence(series: NodeId, slot: Time) -> KeyStr;
}
```

### D.2.5 Small enums used everywhere

```rust
pub enum LinkRel { Continues, DerivedFrom, ConflictsWith, Duplicate, SupersededBy }

/// §5: by convention done, failed, dropped, or superseded; `Missed` is the server's own (§12);
/// any other label is kept as `Other`. Agents may not pass `Missed` (A-66).
pub enum Outcome { Done, Failed, Dropped, Superseded, Missed, Other(Label) }

pub enum SaidKind { Ack, Reply, Result, Correction, Question }   // Question only through talk ask
pub enum ToUserKind { Ack, Question, Result }
pub enum ReleaseReason { Handoff, Blocked, Cannot }
pub enum ViewMode { Brief, Full, Review }
pub enum Expects { None, Ack, Reply }                            // stored; semantics later (§29)
pub enum Evidence { Attempt, Observation, Inference, Reported }  // stored; semantics later (§29);
                                                                 // `checked` is later (D.15.7)
pub enum SignalKind { Duplicate, Conflict }

/// First-release addressees (§13). `class:`, `cap:`, and `everyone` are a later release (§29):
/// the shell rejects them with `invalid` (hint: later release). `principal:<key>` and a bare `user`
/// are stored as the principal they name when the note is recorded (CS-3, D.8.16).
pub enum Addressee { Session(SessionId), Holder(NodeId), Holders(NodeId), Principal(PrincipalId) }

/// Who asked for a request (§9.4, CS-4): a principal, for a user request (origin `user:e<n>`), or
/// someone outside the swarm or an agent, whose name is text in the request entry.
pub enum Requester { User(PrincipalId), External }

/// §6 entry types, in this order.
pub enum EntryType {
    Note, Request, Question, Answer, Decision, Checkpoint, Said, Heard,
    FromUser, ToUser, Approve, Object, Resolve, Retract, System, Late,
}
```

### D.2.6 FNV-1a-64 and its byte encoding

The tie-break of `next` is a ring (CS-12, D-1): the candidates of one aged group stand on a circle
at `fnv_id(id)`, and each session starts at its own point `fnv_session(session)` and goes round, so
`h` is the distance from the session's point to the candidate's (§10.4 as amended):

```
fnv_id(id)          = FNV-1a-64(0x00 ‖ id.to_le_bytes())          // 9 bytes
fnv_session(s)      = FNV-1a-64(s.0.to_le_bytes() ‖ 0x01)         // 9 bytes
h = tie_hash(s, id) = fnv_id(id).wrapping_sub(fnv_session(s))     // (… − …) mod 2^64
```

`id` is the candidate's node id, or the entry id for a routing item. Offset basis
`0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325`, prime `0x0000_0100_0000_01b3`, each step `h = (h ^ u64::from(b))
.wrapping_mul(prime)`. Because `fnv_id` does not depend on the session, one index ordered by
`(tier, ⌊since/1 h⌋ − priority, fnv_id, id)` serves every caller: a session's first candidate in a
group is the first at or after its own point, a range query (CS-16).

```rust
pub fn fnv1a64(bytes: &[u8]) -> u64;
pub fn fnv_id(id: u64) -> u64;
pub fn fnv_session(session: SessionId) -> u64;
/// fnv_id(id).wrapping_sub(fnv_session(session)).
pub fn tie_hash(session: SessionId, id: u64) -> u64;
```

Fixed-width integers rather than decimal strings, because Quint extracts the bytes with `/` and `%`
(D.10.6), so a simulated trace picks exactly the candidate Rust picks (A-43). The integers are
little-endian so that the bytes that vary between nearby ids and sessions are hashed first and every
later byte mixes them: with the big-endian bytes of 1.1, ids and session counters that differ only in
their low bytes land on one short arc of the ring, and in a simulation of 5 to 50 consecutive sessions
over groups of 10 to 1,000 candidates (random ids, and a burst of consecutive ids) every session
picked the same candidate; little-endian bytes keep the share of sessions that collide at 9 to 53 %,
against 15 to 45 % for 1.1's per-session hash (the review's TP-2 measured the same factor of about
2). The leading `0x00` and the trailing `0x01` keep the two inputs apart. Pinned test vectors,
checked by unit tests and by the Kani harness `fnv_reference`:

| Input | FNV-1a-64 |
|---|---|
| `""` | `0xcbf29ce484222325` |
| `"a"` | `0xaf63dc4c8601ec8c` |
| `"foobar"` | `0x85944171f73967e8` |
| `fnv_id(0)` | `0xe604823a249029bf` |
| `fnv_id(6)` | `0x2c23d803e2f46cf9` |
| `fnv_id(42)` | `0x8f919d0115208895` |
| `fnv_id(u64::MAX)` | `0x7a4969ca2d631437` |
| `fnv_session(s-0)` | `0xe604813a2490280c` |
| `fnv_session(s-1)` | `0x529a2ddc8ff5355f` |
| `fnv_session(s-2)` | `0x0cd92bf54dc61432` |
| `fnv_session(s-17)` | `0x893f83b5d9a4968f` |
| `fnv_session(s-u64::MAX)` | `0x280457de49e07df4` |
| `tie_hash(s-0, 0)` | `0x00000100000001b3` |
| `tie_hash(s-1, 6)` | `0xd989aa2752ff379a` |
| `tie_hash(s-1, 42)` | `0x3cf76f24852b5336` |
| `tie_hash(s-2, 42)` | `0x82b8710bc75a7463` |
| `tie_hash(s-17, 5)` | `0xc1df1b57143f208b` |
| `tie_hash(s-u64::MAX, u64::MAX)` | `0x524511ebe3829643` |

## D.3 Parameters

`Params` is part of the state, recorded by `Genesis` and by `ParamsChanged` (D.7), so replay never
depends on the running configuration. Shell-only parameters live in the same struct, so the
constitution is rendered from one place.

```rust
pub struct Params {
    // holds (§10.1)
    pub lease_first: Dur,            // lease.first         15 min
    pub lease_default: Dur,          // lease.default       20 min
    pub lease_max: Dur,              // lease.max           2 h
    pub lease_ceiling: Dur,          // lease.ceiling       8 h
    pub renew_max: u32,              // renew.max           3
    pub hold_per_session: u32,       // hold.per_session    2
    // sessions (§3)
    pub presence_silence: Dur,       // presence.silence    15 min
    pub presence_resolution: Dur,    // presence.resolution 3 min: a call refreshes presence at most
                                     //   this often (CS-14)
    pub session_retain: Dur,         // session.retain      24 h: then a silent session retires
                                     //   (CS-8)
    // retries (§20.1, O1)
    pub op_retain: Dur,              // op.retain           24 h: how long an op_id record lives
                                     //   (CS-8)
    // keys (§7, §9.1)
    pub conversation_schemes: BTreeSet<Label>, // conversation.schemes {chat, issue, mail} (CS-36)
    // people (§9)
    pub commitment_followup: Dur,    // commitment.followup 90 min
    pub question_recheck: Dur,       // question.recheck    4 h
    pub question_max_rechecks: u32,  // question.max_rechecks 2
    // principals and questions for them (§8.4, CS-2, CS-33)
    pub user_question_due: Dur,      // user_question.due   72 h, raised to the addressee's p90 gap
    pub user_question_due_absent: Dur, // user_question.due_absent 1 h: an absent addressee (CS-2)
    pub user_question_max_pending: u32, // user_question.max_pending 20 per principal (CS-33)
    pub user_gap_window: Dur,        // user_gap.window     28 days
    // (no forum-default addressee: the forum's owners are ROOT's `owners`, forum data that agents
    //  keep, D.2.2, D-3, FQ-5)
    // agent communication (§13)
    pub deliver_window: Dur,         // deliver.window      24 h
    pub talk_wait_max: Dur,          // talk.wait_max       50 s        (shell)
    // budgets (§10.4, §20.3, §5)
    pub hello_budget: u32,           // hello.budget        4096 bytes  (shell)
    pub brief_budget: u32,           // brief.budget        16384 bytes (shell)
    pub digest_max: u32,             // digest.max          2048 bytes  (core validates)
    pub leave_better_max: u32,       // leave_better.max    3
    // refusals (§10.3)
    pub refusal_ttl: Dur,            // refusal.ttl         7 days
    pub refusal_window: Dur,         // refusal.window      7 days
    pub refusal_backoff: Dur,        // refusal.backoff     1 h: one session's `cannot` (CS-7)
    pub refusal_quorum: u32,         // refusal.quorum      3 sessions make their class refuse (CS-7)
    pub too_big_attempts: u32,       // too_big.attempts    3
    // pause, archive (§19, §5)
    pub pause_ttl: Dur,              // pause.ttl           2 h
    pub archive_after: Dur,          // archive.after       7 days
    // recurring work and capacity (§12, §17)
    pub coverage_window: Dur,        // coverage.window     28 days
    pub capacity_window: Dur,        // capacity.window     7 days
    // safety valves (§19)
    pub write_per_hour: u32,         // write.per_hour      120 per session (shell)
    pub queue_max_wait: Dur,         // queue.max_wait      10 s: then limit(Busy) (shell, CS-29)
    pub text_max: u32,               // text.max            65536 bytes per free-text argument,
                                     //   after masking: then limit(TextTooLong) (the shell answers,
                                     //   `apply` repeats the check; L1, A-114)
    pub tree_max_depth: u32,         // tree.max_depth      16
    pub tree_max_children: u32,      // tree.max_children   500 open agent-made children (CS-10),
                                     //   persons and teams not counted (A-113)
    pub settle_batch: u32,           // settle.batch        1000 deadlines per transaction (shell)
    pub instructions_max: u32,       // instructions.max    512 characters (shell)
    // tidying (§14, 1.8)
    #[serde(default)]
    pub offer_stale: Option<Dur>,    // offer.stale         90 days; None only in parameters
                                     //   recorded before 1.8 (D.7.6), which `valid` refuses
}

impl Default for Params { /* the values in the comments above */ }

impl Params {
    /// The ranges and orders every consumer relies on. Genesis and AdminCmd::SetParams refuse
    /// params that fail it.
    pub fn valid(&self) -> bool;
}
```

`Params::valid` requires:
- every `Dur` field is at least `SECOND` (A-68: a zero duration would create a deadline at the
  instant of the event that created it, and settling relies on new deadlines lying strictly later),
  and `offer_stale` is set (1.8);
- `lease_first <= lease_default <= lease_max <= lease_ceiling`;
- `hold_per_session`, `question_max_rechecks`, `too_big_attempts`, `leave_better_max`,
  `tree_max_children`, `settle_batch`, `write_per_hour`, `digest_max`, `instructions_max`,
  `user_question_max_pending`, and `refusal_quorum` are at least 1; `renew_max` may be 0;
- `user_question_due_absent <= user_question_due` (an absent addressee never waits longer than a
  present one);
- `refusal_backoff <= refusal_ttl` (one session's refusal never outlives the class's, CS-7);
- `3 × presence_resolution <= presence_silence` (silence still fires at least two thirds of
  `presence.silence` after the last call, CS-14);
- `session_retain > lease_ceiling` and `session_retain > presence_silence`: a session retires only
  after every hold it took has ended and after it fell silent (D.8.23, CS-8);
- `conversation_schemes` contains none of `user`, `repeat`, and `person` (a person's key names a
  human, not a conversation, D.2.2);
- `tree_max_depth >= 3` (signal nodes live at depth 3, `/sys/signals/<signal>`);
- `text_max >= digest_max` (a digest within `digest.max` is never refused as too long, §22, A-114);
- `hello_budget >= 512` and `brief_budget >= 1024`.

Health thresholds and the fallback work estimate are constants in `forum_core::health`, not
parameters, because the specification gives no values for them (A-41, CS-9, CS-31):

```rust
pub const IDLE_LOW_PERMILLE: u32 = 200;   // "idle share is low": below 20 %
pub const IDLE_HIGH_PERMILLE: u32 = 500;  // "idle share is high": above 50 %
pub const FALLBACK_EST_MIN: u64 = 30;     // demand estimate with no est and no completed work
pub const DONE_RING: usize = 101;         // completed nodes kept for the median (D.4.9)
pub const HEALTH_TOP: usize = 10;         // items listed per reason, besides its count (CS-9)
pub const RED_SHARE_PERMILLE: u32 = 10;   // a counted reason is red from 1 % of its population
pub const PAUSE_RED_PERMILLE: u32 = 100;  // a pause is red at ROOT or over 10 % of the candidates
pub const FLAGS_GROWTH_MIN: u32 = 50;     // FlagsPilingUp: growth over capacity.window above
pub const FLAGS_GROWTH_PERMILLE: u32 = 100; //   max(50, 10 % of the start), and growth on each
pub const FLAGS_GROWTH_DAYS: u64 = 3;     //   of the last 3 days (CS-31)
```

Bounds on what the user side shows and stores are constants in `forum_core::user`, for the same
reason (CS-2, CS-3, CS-5, D-3):

```rust
pub const HELLO_USER_ITEMS: usize = 5;    // items of user_decisions and user_digest in hello
pub const UQ_REQUESTERS_MAX: usize = 3;   // requester stages of a chain (D.8.12)
pub const UQ_OWNERS_MAX: usize = 3;       // owner stages of a chain: the nearest owners, then ROOT's
pub const UQ_CHAIN_MAX: usize = 8;        // 1 explicit + 3 requesters + 3 owners + `user` (U1)
/// A digest entry not shown to its principal within this time leaves the pending list, counted in
/// `State::digest_left` (CS-5, D.4.12); it stays in `@user/digest`. Real time, never scaled.
pub const DIGEST_RETAIN: Dur = Dur(28 * 86_400_000);
```

How long a finished entity stays in memory is a constant in `forum_core::state` (D-5, D.4.12). It is
not a parameter of §22: no agent sees it, and it is real time, never scaled, so no model run reaches
it (D.10.5):

```rust
pub const FINISHED_RETAIN: Dur = Dur(7 * 86_400_000);
```

Bounds on what a query lists or scans are constants in `forum_core::query` (§18: lists carry
`shown/total` or `≥k`):

```rust
pub const MOVED_MAX: usize = 20;          // entries the `moved` warning lists, newest first (CS-17)
/// Notes a `hello` or a `talk wait` delivers at most, oldest first (1.5, §13, §22, D.8.16): only
/// those are read; the rest wait for the next call.
pub const INBOX_DELIVER_MAX: usize = 10;
pub const WHO_MAX: usize = 10;            // sessions `who` and `hello.present` list (CS-21)
pub const SCAN_MAX: u32 = 2_000;          // entries a filtered scan visits before it says ≥k
pub const BACKLINKS_MAX: usize = 20;      // items per list and page of what rests on a node (CS-22)
pub const PAGE_DEFAULT: u32 = 50;         // `view feed`, `user_log`, and `history` pages (A-78)
pub const PAGE_MAX: u32 = 200;
```

The bounds of the next calls (§20.9, §22's fixed values: 3 items, `total` exact below 20, 5 ids
per list, a checkpoint due after 5 minutes or 1 minute before the lease ends) are constants of
`forum_core::query::guide`, listed with its types in D.8.26. The byte bounds of a rendered item (a
call of 256 bytes, `why` 100, a path over 64 bytes as its id, keys never cut) are the shell's
(D.11.7).

## D.4 State

### D.4.1 Where each field of §5 lives

The core keeps a field only if `apply`, `settle`, a query, or an invariant reads it (D.0.2,
principle 6). Every field the core keeps is also in the shell's state tables (D.11.6), which are the
source of truth; the last column names the state-table columns that carry the §24 constraints, and
the shell's other uses.

| §5 field | In the core | Elsewhere in the shell (D.11.6, D.11.12) |
|---|---|---|
| `id`, `path`, `aliases` | `Node::place`, `State::names`, `State::aliases` | `st_names` (unique names per parent) |
| `keys` | `Node::keys` (string and normaliser version) | `st_keys` (one open carrier per key) |
| `kind`, `tags` | `Node::kind`, `Node::tags` | — |
| `title`, `body`, `fields`, `files` | `Node::title`, `body`, `fields`, `files` | the node's search document |
| `digest` | `Node::digest` | the node's search document |
| `capacity`, `status`, `priority`, `est`, `needs`, `due` | yes | `st_nodes.capacity` (holders ≤ capacity) |
| `waits_for`, `depends_on` | `Node::wait`, `Node::depends_on` | — |
| `owners` (new, D-3) | `Node::owners`: person or team nodes, inherited from the nearest owned ancestor, except a team's members, which are its own `owners` only (A-116) | — |
| `repeat` | `Role::Series(Series { repeat })` (cron text, parsed cron, and frozen tz table) | — |
| `agreements` | `Node::agreements`, and `Node::agreements_at`, its last change (1.4, `view agreements`) | — |
| holders, attempts, checkpoint counter, flags, `created_by`, rollup | `State::holds`, `Node::attempts`, `Node::checkpoints`, `ix` flags and rollup (the children's and the subtree's, CS-32), `Node::origin` | `st_holds` (holders ≤ capacity); flags and rollups rendered from the core |

### D.4.2 The state

```rust
pub struct State {
    // ---------- base: facts (mirrored by the Quint model, D.10.3; stored in the state tables) ----
    pub params: Params,
    /// T1: the largest `at` of any applied event.
    pub last_now: Time,
    pub counters: Counters,
    /// Events that `evolve` could not apply as given (D.7.5). check_invariants requires 0.
    pub anomalies: u64,

    pub nodes: BTreeMap<NodeId, Node>,
    /// Live names: (parent, name) -> node. Disjoint from `aliases` (K3).
    pub names: BTreeMap<(NodeId, Name), NodeId>,
    /// Former names: (parent, name) -> node.
    pub aliases: BTreeMap<(NodeId, Name), NodeId>,

    /// Metadata of the feed entries the core reads (`keeps_meta`, D.4.5, CS-17). Immutable once
    /// inserted (O3); it leaves memory with its entity, or `FINISHED_RETAIN` after its own time when
    /// it bears none (D.4.12). Every other entry is counted in its node's `seq` and kept in the
    /// history.
    pub entries: BTreeMap<Eid, EntryMeta>,

    /// Holds that have not ended. An ended hold leaves the map; its history is in the log.
    pub holds: BTreeMap<Token, Hold>,

    // The entity maps hold the resident entities: a finished one leaves memory FINISHED_RETAIN after
    // it finished, and its state row stays in the state tables (D.4.12).
    pub requests: BTreeMap<RequestId, Request>,
    pub pquestions: BTreeMap<QuestionId, PQuestion>,     // questions to people (§9.3)
    /// Questions between agents (§13); one leaves with its note, at `until` (D.4.12).
    pub aquestions: BTreeMap<QuestionId, AQuestion>,
    pub uquestions: BTreeMap<QuestionId, UQuestion>,     // questions for the user (§8.4)
    pub commitments: BTreeMap<CommitmentId, Commitment>,
    pub saids: BTreeMap<SaidId, Said>,
    pub decisions: BTreeMap<DecisionId, Decision>,
    pub objections: BTreeMap<ObjectionId, Objection>,
    pub user_entries: BTreeMap<UserEntryId, UserEntry>,  // `from_user` entries (§8.1)
    pub digest: BTreeMap<DigestId, DigestEntry>,         // `@user/digest` (§8.5)
    /// Addressed messages (§13) until their `until`: evolve drops a note at the first event at or
    /// after it (CS-17), as nothing delivers it later.
    pub notes: BTreeMap<NoteId, Note>,
    /// `approve` entries per node version (§11.2 warning). The warning counts the versions from the
    /// node's `content_version` on (CS-34).
    pub approvals: BTreeMap<(NodeId, Version), u32>,
    /// What `talk retract` struck out: an entry or a node, never removed (O3). A basis reference
    /// to a target here is stale (`basis_changed`, D-4, D.8.17). Retractions are rare, so this
    /// grows with history only by them.
    pub retracted: BTreeSet<BasisTarget>,

    /// Live refusals, one record per (node, class) with an entry per refusing session (CS-7). An
    /// entry leaves when it expires; the record leaves with its last entry, or when cleared.
    pub refusals: BTreeMap<(NodeId, ClassName), Refusal>,
    /// The classes that asked for work with an open `next` within `refusal.window`, with the caps
    /// they asked with (E1, CS-7). A class leaves the map when its last caps profile expires.
    pub classes: BTreeMap<ClassName, ClassActivity>,
    /// Open signals: key -> signal node (S1). A resolved signal leaves the map.
    pub signals: BTreeMap<SignalKey, NodeId>,
    /// Active pauses by scope node. An expired or lifted pause leaves the map.
    pub pauses: BTreeMap<NodeId, Pause>,

    /// Live and silent sessions. A session leaves at `SessionRetired`, `session.retain` after its
    /// last `Touched` (its presence's last refresh, §3), holding nothing (CS-8, D.8.23).
    pub sessions: BTreeMap<SessionId, Session>,
    /// Interned principals (§3, CS-1): key -> id, never removed. Genesis interns `user` as
    /// USER_PRINCIPAL; every other key enters by `PrincipalSeen` the first time a command names it,
    /// a `person:<key>` key included (D.2.2), so every alias of a person has an id.
    pub principal_ids: BTreeMap<PrincipalKey, PrincipalId>,
    /// Retry store (O1): (class, op_id) -> digest, session, and expiry. Evolve drops a record at
    /// the first event at or after its `expires_at` (CS-8).
    pub ops: BTreeMap<(ClassName, OpId), OpRecord>,

    // ---------- history: values that depend on event order (D.4.9; stored in the state tables) ----
    pub stats: Stats,
    /// The time each candidate of `next` became one (§10.4 `since`): the event that made it a
    /// candidate, an occurrence's slot, a routing item's entry time. It depends on history, so it
    /// is stored, not recounted; its key set equals `ix.next.of`'s (R1, CS-16).
    pub since: BTreeMap<Cand, Time>,
    /// Each principal's `from_user` times, ascending. At each message of `p`, evolve drops the times
    /// of `p` before `at − user_gap.window`, with the window in force then (monotone in `at`, so it
    /// commutes with T2); readers search from `now − user_gap.window` (D.8.12, CS-2). History, not an
    /// index: what a prune kept depends on the window at each message, and the user entries it came
    /// from may have left memory (D.4.12), so it is stored rather than recounted.
    pub user_msgs: BTreeMap<PrincipalId, Vec<Time>>,
    /// The time each resident entity leaves memory (D.4.12): `FINISHED_RETAIN` after it finished, or
    /// after the last reference that held it back went, or after a restore; for a pending digest
    /// entry, DIGEST_RETAIN after its creation or its restore. It leaves at the first event at or
    /// after that time. History: it depends on when the entity finished.
    pub leaving: BTreeMap<EntityRef, Time>,
    /// Digest entries that left the pending list unshown after DIGEST_RETAIN, per principal (CS-5,
    /// D.4.12): `hello` adds them to its count as older entries, in `@user/digest`.
    pub digest_left: BTreeMap<PrincipalId, u64>,

    // ---------- derived: indices with a full-recount oracle (R1, F, T4) ----------
    pub ix: Ix,
}

pub struct Counters {
    pub next_node: NodeId,       // starts at FIRST_FREE_NODE
    pub next_eid: Eid,           // starts at Eid(1)
    pub next_session: SessionId, // starts at SessionId(1)
    pub next_principal: PrincipalId, // starts at PrincipalId(1); 0 is `user` (CS-1)
    pub events: u64,             // events applied since genesis (O3: the log length)
}
```

### D.4.3 Nodes

```rust
pub struct Node {
    /// None only for ROOT.
    pub place: Option<Place>,
    pub origin: Origin,                      // §5 `created_by`
    pub created_at: Time,

    // content (O2): a change of title, body, fields, files, or status bumps `version`;
    // a change of digest bumps `digest_version`; agreements bump neither (A-3).
    pub title: Text,
    pub body: Text,
    pub fields: BTreeMap<Text, Text>,        // value: canonical JSON text (sorted keys, no spaces)
    pub files: BTreeMap<Text, Text>,         // file name -> a reference: a URL or a path, with an
                                             // optional content hash (`sha256:<hex>`) the server
                                             // stores and never checks; the artefact lives outside
                                             // the forum (FQ-5); empty at creation, set by
                                             // `update` only (A-97)
    pub status: Text,
    pub digest: Text,                        // at most params.digest_max bytes
    pub agreements: Text,                    // empty means none (§11.2)
    /// 1.4 (§20.4, D.14.5): when the agreements were last set, by `create` or `update`; None while
    /// the node never had any. `view agreements` shows it as the agreements' last change.
    pub agreements_at: Option<Time>,

    // labels and settings
    pub kind: Option<Label>,
    pub tags: BTreeSet<Label>,               // contains "offer" while the node is offered
    pub capacity: u32,                       // slots, default 1; reserved nodes have 0
    pub priority: i32,                       // default 0, higher first
    pub est: Option<u32>,                    // minutes
    pub needs: BTreeSet<Label>,
    pub due: Option<Time>,
    /// One-shot marker for the Due deadline: true once `now >= due` has been processed
    /// (D.4.8). Never read by a flag predicate.
    pub due_fired: bool,
    /// 1.8 (§5, §14): when the node was last touched (below); None for a node loaded from a state
    /// written before 1.8. `#[serde(default)]`.
    pub touched_at: Option<Time>,
    /// 1.8: the one-shot marker of the Stale deadline at `touched_at + offer.stale` (D.4.8); a
    /// touch clears it. Never read by a flag predicate. `#[serde(default)]`.
    pub stale_fired: bool,
    /// The node's owners (D-3, FQ-5): person or team nodes (D.2.2); empty means "inherit from the
    /// nearest owned ancestor". On a team node this field itself names the team's members, never
    /// an inherited value: a team with none has no members (§4, A-116). A setting like `needs`:
    /// it bumps no counter (A-3), and an `update` replaces it whole, last writer wins.
    pub owners: BTreeSet<NodeId>,

    pub keys: BTreeMap<KeyStr, NormVer>,
    pub links: BTreeSet<(LinkRel, NodeId)>,  // outgoing links
    pub depends_on: BTreeSet<NodeId>,
    pub wait: Option<Wait>,                  // the node's own wait (§10.3); at most one
    pub role: Role,
    pub life: Life,

    // the four counters of §5 (O2)
    pub version: Version,
    pub digest_version: Version,
    pub fence: Fence,
    pub seq: Seq,
    /// The `version` at the last change of title, body, fields, or files (1 at creation). Not a
    /// counter of its own: approvals from this version on are approvals of the current content
    /// (§11.2, CS-34), so a status, key, link, or open/closed change does not reset them.
    pub content_version: Version,

    // maintained by the server (§5)
    pub attempts: u32,                       // holds ended without a checkpoint since the last one
    pub checkpoints: u32,                    // checkpoint counter
    pub last_checkpoint: Option<Eid>,
    /// 1.4 (§10.4, D.14.5, re-run R30): the last hold that expired after the node's last
    /// checkpoint without a checkpoint of its own, which the brief's section 2 shows (an outside
    /// action may have happened); cleared by the next checkpoint or release on the node.
    pub expired_hold: Option<ExpiredHold>,
    pub open_intent: Option<Intent>,         // at most one open intent (§10.2)
    /// Questions whose recheck fired for this node: input of `question_recheck` (A-81).
    pub recheck_marks: BTreeSet<QuestionId>,
    /// Expired questions this node must proceed on: input of `proceed_on_assumption`.
    pub assume_marks: BTreeSet<QuestionId>,
    /// Total time held, credited when a hold ends (median of completed work, D.8.22).
    pub held_ms: u64,
    /// The highest `seq` of a people entry of this node whose metadata left memory (D.4.12): the
    /// `moved` warning's total is exact only for a `seen` at or above it (D.8.15).
    pub people_left: Seq,
    /// How many entities whose home is this node have left memory (D.4.12): the brief's sections 3
    /// and 4 then say that older items are in the feed (D.8.6).
    pub left: u32,
    /// 1.11 (§11.3, §24): the newest decision of the node that was retracted, kept in the node's
    /// hot row, so that `no_basis` names it after the decision leaves memory (D.4.12, D.8.17).
    /// Set by `DecisionRetracted { node: Some(n) }`; `#[serde(default)]`: None for a retraction
    /// recorded before 1.11.
    pub retracted_decision: Option<DecisionId>,
    /// 1.12 (§5, §20.9 rule 8): the node's last `intent_done`, of a checkpoint, a release, or a
    /// `hold check`, names a pull request (`words::names_pull_request`), set by the `Appended` of
    /// the entry that carries it, from the entry's flag (`pr_named`, never its text, D.7.6), and
    /// cleared by `NodeReopened`; in the hot row, `#[serde(default)]`. With the open intent's own
    /// flag it is `Node::merge_wait()`, which the next calls read only (D.8.26: `MergeWait`, and
    /// rule 8's decision branches `later`) and G1 (d) checks.
    pub pr_named: bool,
}

pub struct Place { pub parent: NodeId, pub name: Name }

pub enum Origin {
    Reserved,                 // the eight reserved nodes made by Genesis
    Agent(SessionId),         // node create
    Ancestor(SessionId),      // a missing ancestor made by node create or move (§4)
    Occurrence,               // made by the server for a series (§12)
    Signal,                   // made by the server under sys/signals (§14)
}

pub enum Life { Open, Closed(Closure) }

pub struct Closure {
    pub at: Time,                            // AR: archived iff now >= at + archive.after
    pub outcome: Outcome,
    pub merged_into: Option<NodeId>,         // K5: only with Outcome::Superseded
    /// 1.8 (§5, §11.3): the `resolve` entry of an objection upheld on the node while it was
    /// closed. `#[serde(default)]`. A reopen drops the closure, and the mark with it.
    pub upheld: Option<Eid>,
    /// 1.10 (§5, §11.3): the outcome it was closed with, before the first correction that still
    /// marks it, which a second, opposite verdict restores. `#[serde(default)]`: None for a
    /// correction recorded before 1.10, whose withdrawal keeps the outcome.
    pub corrected_from: Option<Outcome>,
    /// 1.11 (§13): the session that closed it, None for the server; a `say` without `to` at the
    /// closed node reaches it while it is live (D.8.16). Set by `NodeClosed { by }`;
    /// `#[serde(default)]`: None for a close recorded before 1.11.
    pub by: Option<SessionId>,
}

pub enum Role {
    Plain,
    Series(Series),
    Occurrence(Occurrence),
    Signal(SignalKey),
}

pub struct Series {
    pub repeat: Repeat,
    pub last_missed: bool,                   // input of `missed` (§14)
}
// Which occurrence is open is derived (`Ix::series_open`), so opening or closing an
// occurrence changes one node only. K6: that set has exactly one element while the series
// is open, and none while it is closed.

pub struct Repeat {
    pub cron_text: Text,                     // as the agent wrote it, for rendering
    pub cron: forum_cron::CronSpec,
    pub tz: forum_cron::TzTable,             // frozen by the shell (D.11.10)
    pub run_within: Dur,                     // > 0
}

pub struct Occurrence {
    pub series: NodeId,
    pub slot: Time,                          // UTC minute
    pub window_end: Time,                    // slot + run_within; also the node's `due` (A-57)
    pub phase: OccPhase,
    /// One-shot marker for the OccurrenceWindow deadline.
    pub window_fired: bool,
}
/// §25 occurrence states: `held` is derived from holds; closed states are the node's closure.
pub enum OccPhase { Waiting, Available }

pub struct Wait {
    pub on: WaitOn,
    pub set_at: Time,
    /// One-shot marker for the Wait deadline of Time and External waits. Resolution itself is
    /// the predicate `resolved(w, now)` of D.8.3 (T3); this field only keeps the queue exact.
    pub fired: bool,
}

pub enum WaitOn {
    /// A question to a person: resolves at its next recheck or when it leaves Open.
    Question { q: QuestionId, rechecks_at_set: u32 },
    /// A question for the user: resolves when it is answered, defaulted, or lapsed (A-31, CS-2).
    UserQuestion(QuestionId),
    /// Resolves while the target is closed (a merged node is closed).
    Node(NodeId),
    /// `{time}`: resolves at that time.
    Time(Time),
    /// `{external: what, recheck_after}`: resolves at that time. The `what` text is in the event.
    External(Time),
}

pub struct Intent { pub eid: Eid, pub session: SessionId,
                    pub pr_named: bool }   // 1.12: its text names a pull request; serde default

/// A hold that expired without a checkpoint of its own (1.4, §10.4): its token, its taker, and
/// when it expired.
pub struct ExpiredHold { pub token: Token, pub session: SessionId, pub at: Time }
```

`is_directory(n) := n.place = Some(Place { parent, .. }) ∧ parent ∈ {PEOPLE, TEAMS}`: a person or a
team of the directory, with or without `person:` keys (§4, A-113).

`is_container(n) := n.origin = Reserved ∨ n.role = Series(_) ∨ is_directory(n)` (A-29, A-113).
Containers never receive the server's `offer` tag when a hold ends, and an `offer` tag on them does
not make them candidates for `next`; only their flags do. A person or team is a record, not work:
offered, it would be taken as work and could be closed, which splits its aliases into separate
persons (A-113). The `offer` tag that `node create` adds when it cannot issue a hold (D.8.9) is
harmless on a container, which it does not make a candidate; it counts again only if the node later
stops being a container (a move out of the directory, or a removed `repeat`), as any tag would.

**Touched** (1.8, §5). `touched_at` is the `at` of the node's last touch: `NodeCreated`,
`NodeReopened`, `NodeUpdated`, `KeyAdded`, `KeyRemoved`, `LinkAdded` (its source), an `Appended`
on it other than a `Late` body (H4: a stale write changes nothing of the node but its feed), and the
`Fired` of its Wait deadline (a time or outside wait resolving at its time). A read (`Shown`), a hold
event, an `OfferSet`, a `WaitSet`, a mark, an intent event, and every other firing touch nothing:
a take, a checkpoint, a release, and a close each append an entry anyway, and a hold that expires
without a checkpoint records nothing, so its node keeps the time of its last write. A touch also
clears `stale_fired`. Tracking is gated on `params.offer_stale`: in a history written before 1.8,
whose parameters lack it, no event touches a node, so the history replays to the state tables it
wrote (D.7.6); a 1.8 server's first `ParamsChanged` sets it, and each node is then tracked from its
next touch.

**Upheld** (1.8, §5, §11.3). An objection upheld on a closed node corrects it (`NodeCorrected`,
D.7.4): `done` becomes `refuted` (`Outcome::Other(refuted)`) when the node's kind is `claim`, and
`failed` otherwise; another outcome stays; `closure.upheld := Some(resolve entry)`. A closed node
marked so is never a candidate (D.8.5), and a take of it is `closed` (`take_gate`, D.8.10). 1.10:
the first correction keeps the outcome it replaced in `closure.corrected_from`, and a second,
opposite verdict on the objection whose verdict marks the node withdraws the correction
(`CorrectionWithdrawn`): the outcome comes back, and the mark goes (D.8.17).

**Kept for good** (1.11, §24). What a rule reads of a finished entity for good lives on the node
that it belongs to, since the entity leaves memory (D.4.12): `retracted_decision`, the newest
retracted decision, in the hot row, set by `DecisionRetracted` when the event names the node, and
read by `query::no_basis` (D.8.17); and `closure.by`, who closed the node, set by `NodeClosed`, and
read by `say` (D.8.16). Both are appended with `#[serde(default)]` and set only from fields the
events carry since 1.11, so a history written before replays to the state tables it wrote
(D.7.6).

Reserved nodes have capacity 0, cannot be moved, merged, or closed, never carry `ready_to_close`,
and are never a conversation node, a request's node, a key carrier, or a routing target
(`invalid(ReservedNode)`), because nobody can take them to answer (A-29, A-66).

`occ_locked(o) := o.role = Occurrence { series: x, .. } ∧ open(x) ∧ x.role = Series(_)`: a closed
occurrence of a series that is still open and still a series cannot be reopened or taken (§12,
A-13), and is never a candidate. When the series closes or stops being a series, its closed
occurrences unlock, and `evolve` refreshes their classification (D.7.4).

**How a node is stored** (D.6.1, D.11.6). One `Node` in memory is four kinds of state row, so that
the frequent events rewrite only what they change:
- the **hot row** (`Fact::NodeHot`): the counters (`version`, `digest_version`, `content_version`,
  `fence`, `seq`, `attempts`, `checkpoints`, `held_ms`, `people_left`, `left`), `last_checkpoint`,
  `expired_hold`, `life`, `wait`, `open_intent`, the marks, `tags`, `due_fired`, `touched_at` and
  `stale_fired` (1.8), and the role's state (an occurrence's `phase` and `window_fired`, a series'
  `last_missed`); every `Appended`, hold
  event, checkpoint, and `OfferSet` rewrites it, and it holds no text;
- the **content row** (`Fact::NodeContent`): `place`, `origin`, `created_at`, the texts (title,
  body, fields, files, status, digest, agreements) with `agreements_at`, the settings (kind,
  capacity, priority, est, needs, due, depends_on, owners), and the role's definition (a series'
  `repeat` with its tz table, an occurrence's series, slot, and window end); only `NodeCreated`,
  `NodeUpdated`, `NodeMoved`, and a role change rewrite it;
- one **key row** per key (`Fact::Key`), written only at `KeyAdded` and `KeyRemoved`; its `open`
  column changes only at `NodeClosed` and `NodeReopened`;
- one **link row** per outgoing link (`Fact::Link`), written only at `LinkAdded`.

A long-lived intake node collects a `user:e<n>` key for every routed message (365,000 a year at 1,000
routed messages a day), and a held research node may carry a 30 KB body: with one row per node, each
`said` there, and each 5-minute checkpoint, rewrote all of it (gate G-8 checks the split).

### D.4.4 Holds

```rust
pub struct Hold {
    pub session: SessionId,   // the taker; the hold counts against it (H2)
    pub taken_at: Time,
    pub lease_until: Time,
    pub last_extended: Time,  // taken_at, then the time of each checkpoint or renew
    /// The lease terms in force at issue (snapshot), so a later ParamsChanged cannot break H5.
    /// H5 is evaluated with these terms, not with the current params (A-102).
    pub terms: LeaseTerms,
    /// L of §10.1: the requested lease for later extensions (A-8).
    pub l: Dur,
    pub renews: u32,          // renews since the last checkpoint (H5)
    pub checkpointed: bool,   // a checkpoint happened during this hold
    /// 1.4 (§10.1, R4): the outcome the node had when this hold's take reopened it, None when the
    /// node was open. Fixed at issue (`HoldIssued::reopened`); rule 8 of the next calls reads it
    /// to suggest closing the node again with that outcome once its flags are cleared (D.8.26).
    pub reopened: Option<Outcome>,
}

pub struct LeaseTerms { pub first: Dur, pub default: Dur, pub max: Dur, pub ceiling: Dur,
                        pub renew_max: u32 }

/// live(h, now) of §26. An ended hold is not in the map, so liveness is the lease predicate.
pub fn live(h: &Hold, now: Time) -> bool { now < h.lease_until }
```

### D.4.5 Feed entries and the entities born from them

```rust
pub struct EntryMeta {
    pub node: NodeId,
    pub seq: Seq,
    pub at: Time,
    pub by: Author,
    pub ty: EntryType,
    /// The principal of a `FromUser` entry (whose words) or a `ToUser` entry (to whom), None for
    /// every other type (CS-1, CS-4): the DigestShown precondition and the Settled and D1 checks
    /// read it from the state (D.7.4, D.9.2).
    pub principal: Option<PrincipalId>,
}

pub enum Author { Session(SessionId), Server }

/// Whether the core keeps an entry's `EntryMeta` (CS-17): every body except a checkpoint, a plain
/// note (`Note { to: None }`), a system entry other than `System(Digest)`, and a late write. Those
/// are about half of all entries at 10,000 agents (checkpoints alone are 10⁹ a year); the core reads
/// none of their metadata, so they live in the history and the shell's `entries` table only.
pub fn keeps_meta(body: &EntryBody) -> bool;
```

The structural part of every entry is the `EntryBody` carried by the `Appended` event (D.7.3); its
text is the `EntryText` of the same event. The entities below are created by `Appended` and changed by
their own transition events. Feed pages, the user log, and history are the shell's: it serves them
from its `entries` table and the history (D.11.6), so the core keeps no per-node feed index (CS-17).
An entry that a command names without the core keeping its metadata (`hide {entry}`, `retract
{entry}`, `reply_to`) exists when `eid < counters.next_eid`, because eids have no gaps; for `hide` and
`retract` the shell adds the entry's node from its `entries` table to the command (D.5.2). An entity
that a command names after it left memory is restored first (D.4.12).

```rust
pub struct Request {
    /// The conversation node (C1); for a user request, the node it was routed to. Changes only by
    /// merge (N5).
    pub node: NodeId,
    /// The message the request came in (A-61; D.2.4), with the normaliser version it was
    /// normalised with (K2): Q1, unique by `origin.key`, so a repeat of one message is the same
    /// request, and a new message in the same conversation is a new one.
    pub origin: Key,
    /// The conversation key the node was found by: its `where`, or its origin without one; for a
    /// user request its `user:e<n>` key (as `Appended(Request)` carries it, D.7.3). Only a `said`
    /// whose own key is this one answers the request (§9.4, 1.3, D.8.8).
    pub conv: KeyStr,
    pub from_user: Option<UserEntryId>,      // set when origin is user:e<entry>
    /// `User(p)` exactly when `from_user` is set, with `p` that entry's principal; only a
    /// `to_user` of kind `result` to `p` answers it (CS-4, A-23).
    pub requester: Requester,
    pub answered_by: Option<Eid>,            // the first qualifying answer after the request
    pub settled: Option<Settlement>,         // latched once, never cleared (Settled)
    pub moved_from: Option<NodeId>,
}
pub struct Settlement { pub decision: DecisionId, pub answer: Eid }

pub struct PQuestion {
    pub node: NodeId,                        // conversation node (C1); changes only by merge
    pub conv: KeyStr,
    pub blocking: bool,
    pub said: SaidId,                        // the `said` of kind question recorded with it
    pub state: PqState,
    pub rechecks: u32,                       // k of §25 open(k)
    pub recheck_at: Time,                    // meaningful while Open
    pub lapse: Option<Lapse>,                // set on expiry or escalation, kept after an answer
    pub assumed_by: Option<DecisionId>,      // the decision that recorded the assumption
    pub moved_from: Option<NodeId>,
}
pub enum PqState {
    Open,
    Expired,
    Escalated { uq: QuestionId },
    Answered { by: Eid },
    Superseded { by: QuestionId },
    Withdrawn { by: Eid },                    // 1.12 (§9.3): by a retract of it while open
}
pub enum Lapse { Expired, Escalated }

/// Leaves memory with its note, at `until` (D.4.12): nothing reads it after that; a later `talk
/// answer` is validated against the shell's `entries` table, which adds the node and the asker.
pub struct AQuestion {
    pub node: NodeId,
    pub asker: SessionId,
    pub state: AqState,
}
pub enum AqState { Open, Answered { by: Eid } }

pub struct UQuestion {
    pub source: UqSource,
    pub about: Option<NodeId>,
    /// The addressee chain, fixed at creation (CS-2, D.8.12): non-empty, no duplicates, at most
    /// UQ_CHAIN_MAX stages, the last one USER_PRINCIPAL (U1).
    pub to: Vec<PrincipalId>,
    /// The current stage: the question is addressed to `to[stage]` (U1: `stage < to.len()`).
    pub stage: u8,
    pub due: Time,                           // the current stage's due
    pub has_default: bool,                   // the default text is in the entry
    pub state: UqState,
    /// The decision that recorded the assumption after a lapse (CS-2), as PQuestion's.
    pub assumed_by: Option<DecisionId>,
}
pub enum UqSource {
    /// talk ask {to: user | principal:<p>} (A-16); `digest`: SHA-256 of the masked text and
    /// options, computed by the shell like the request digest (D.11.5), so that an identical ask
    /// for the same first addressee returns this question (D.8.12)
    Agent { session: SessionId, digest: ReqDigest },
    Escalation { question: QuestionId },     // a blocking people question (§9.3)
    Refusal { node: NodeId },                // every active class refused (§10.3)
}
/// §25 (CS-2): pending(k) -> pending(k+1) (re-addressed) | answered | defaulted | lapsed. The
/// stage is `UQuestion::stage`, so `Pending` covers every pending(k).
pub enum UqState { Pending, Answered { by: Eid }, Defaulted, Lapsed }

pub struct Commitment {
    pub node: NodeId,                        // conversation node (C1); changes only by merge
    pub conv: KeyStr,                        // refreshed and fulfilled only in it (§9.2)
    pub last_ack: Time,
    pub followup_at: Time,                   // last_ack + commitment.followup (snapshot)
    /// One-shot marker for the Commitment deadline; reset by a refreshing ack.
    pub followup_fired: bool,
    pub state: CommitmentState,
    pub moved_from: Option<NodeId>,
}
pub enum CommitmentState { Open, Fulfilled { by: SaidId } }

pub struct Said {
    pub node: NodeId,                        // conversation node (C1); changes only by merge (A-94)
    pub conv: KeyStr,
    pub kind: SaidKind,
    pub session: SessionId,
    pub state: SaidState,
    pub moved_from: Option<NodeId>,
}
pub enum SaidState { Pending, Confirmed, Unconfirmed, Withheld }   // Withheld: 1.9, §9.2

pub struct Decision {
    pub node: NodeId,
    pub settles: BTreeSet<RequestId>,
    pub state: DecisionState,
    /// What the decision rests on (§15, CS-22), in the order given, as validated references.
    pub basis: Vec<BasisRef>,
}
pub enum DecisionState { Active, Superseded { by: DecisionId }, Retracted { by: Eid } }

/// One reference of a decision's basis (§15, CS-22). The shell parses `#12@4`, a path with `@4`,
/// `#12`, `e57` or `entry:e57`, and `{external: what, checked_at, recheck?}`; the core validates
/// and stores the result, so a later check can read a year of decisions (events are immutable).
pub enum BasisRef {
    /// A node (after `merged_into`, as links resolve, A-88): the version cited, kept for rendering
    /// only, and the node's outcome when the decision was recorded, None while it was open. That
    /// snapshot is what `stale` compares with (D-4, D.8.17).
```
