```rust
    Node { id: NodeId, version: Option<Version>, life_at: Option<Outcome> },
    /// An entry, usually a decision.
    Entry(Eid),
    /// Something outside the forum; its `what` is a `TextField::Basis` text of the decision's entry,
    /// in the order of the external references. Stored only: its staleness is later (§29, D-4).
    External { checked_at: Time, recheck: Option<Time> },
}
/// What a node or entry reference points at: the key of `ix.cited_by` and of `State::retracted`.
pub enum BasisTarget { Node(NodeId), Entry(Eid) }

pub struct Objection { pub node: NodeId, pub state: ObjectionState, pub moved_from: Option<NodeId>,
                       /// 1.11 (§11.3): its newest deferral while open, a `resolve` entry that
                       /// decided nothing (`Appended(Resolve { deferred: true })`), which briefs
                       /// show. `#[serde(default)]`.
                       pub deferred: Option<Eid> }
pub enum ObjectionState { Open, Resolved { by: Eid }, Upheld { by: Eid } } // Upheld: 1.8, §11.3

/// `principal`: whose words these are (CS-1, D.8.11). `at`: the entry's time, for the
/// per-principal message times of D.8.12 (kept here so the index recounts from this map alone).
pub struct UserEntry { pub session: SessionId, pub principal: PrincipalId, pub at: Time,
                       pub routing: Routing }
/// §25: unrouted -> routed (Request, Clarifies) | answered (Answers) | no_action.
pub enum Routing {
    Unrouted,
    Request { node: NodeId, request: RequestId },
    Clarifies { request: RequestId },
    Answers { question: QuestionId },
    NoAction,
}

/// One entry per audience principal (CS-5, D.8.13): `to` is the human it is for, and only a
/// `to_user` to `to` shows it.
pub struct DigestEntry { pub item: DigestItem, pub to: PrincipalId, pub state: DigestState }
pub enum DigestItem {
    Assumption { question: QuestionId },              // a people question expired (§9.3)
    DefaultApplied { question: QuestionId },          // a user question defaulted (§8.4)
    RefusalDrop { node: NodeId, question: QuestionId }, // a refused node was dropped (§10.3)
    Lapsed { question: QuestionId },                  // a user question lapsed (§8.4, CS-2)
}
pub enum DigestState { Pending, Shown { by: Eid } }

/// An addressed message: `talk say {to}`, an agent question, or an agent answer (§13). It leaves the
/// state at its `until` (CS-17): the inbox already shows only notes with `until > now`.
pub struct Note {
    pub node: NodeId,
    pub to: Addressee,
    pub until: Time,
    /// Sessions the note is delivered to, fixed when it is recorded (A-49). `Principal(p)` notes
    /// are delivered instead to the sessions that serve `p` or an alias of it when they read (CS-3,
    /// A-18), and `Holders(a)` notes to the sessions that hold in `a`'s branch when they read
    /// (D-6); both are recorded with no recipients.
    pub recipients: BTreeSet<SessionId>,
    /// `holder:` with nobody holding the node: delivered to whoever takes it next.
    pub pending_holder: bool,
    /// Sessions that have received it in `hello` or `talk wait`. A `Holders(a)` note is read once
    /// per session through the session's cursor for the scope `a` instead
    /// (`Session::branch_seen[a]`, D.8.16), so a broadcast to 10,000 holders stores no set of
    /// 10,000.
    pub read_by: BTreeSet<SessionId>,
}
```

### D.4.6 Refusals, classes, signals, pauses

```rust
/// The refusals of one class on one node (§10.3, CS-7). Every time is a snapshot taken at the
/// `cannot`, so a ParamsChanged never changes what a stored refusal excludes (A-103).
pub struct Refusal {
    /// refusal.quorum when the record was created: the class has refused the node while at least
    /// this many entries are live (`class_refused`, D.8.14).
    pub quorum: u32,
    /// One entry per refusing session; a repeat by the same session renews its entry.
    pub by: BTreeMap<SessionId, RefusalEntry>,
}
pub struct RefusalEntry {
    pub backoff_until: Time,  // at + refusal.backoff: until then the whole class skips the node
    pub expires_at: Time,     // at + refusal.ttl: the entry counts towards the quorum until then
}

pub struct ClassActivity {
    /// The caps a session of the class held at each open `next` (CS-7), mapped to that call's
    /// `at + refusal.window` (the latest call's, a snapshot, A-103). The class is active for node
    /// `n` while some profile here has caps ⊇ `n.needs` (D.8.14). A profile leaves the map when its
    /// window ends (the class's RefusalExpiry deadline, A-27); the map is never empty. Each profile
    /// is its own state row (`Fact::ClassProfile`), so an open `next` rewrites one small row, not
    /// every caps set the class has shown; `ix.class_ends` orders the window ends per class, so the
    /// deadline and the expiry find the earliest in O(log) (D.4.10).
    pub caps_seen: BTreeMap<BTreeSet<Label>, Time>,
}

/// One signal per (kind, unordered pair): a < b always.
pub struct SignalKey { pub kind: SignalKind, pub a: NodeId, pub b: NodeId }

pub struct Pause {
    pub until: Time,          // P1: now < until <= last_renewed + ttl
    pub last_renewed: Time,
    pub ttl: Dur,             // pause.ttl at the last renewal (snapshot)
    pub by: SessionId,        // the last session to pause or renew it
    pub class: ClassName,     // that session's class, shown with the pause (CS-9)
}
```

The reason of a pause is the text of its `System(Paused)` entry, which the shell projects
(D.11.6) and shows in the status line, `control health`, and an empty `next` (CS-9).

### D.4.7 Sessions and the retry store

```rust
pub struct Session {
    pub class: ClassName,
    pub started_at: Time,
    /// The time of the last `Touched`: within `presence.resolution` of the last successful call
    /// that appended events (CS-14, D.8.23).
    pub last_seen: Time,
    pub silence_at: Time,                    // last_seen + presence.silence (snapshot)
    /// When the Retire deadline fires (CS-8): the largest `now + session.retain` of the session's
    /// touches (a snapshot that never decreases), so it lies after every hold the session took.
    pub retire_at: Time,
    /// §25 live ⇄ silent. Set by the Silence deadline, cleared by Touched. On a settled state
    /// silent == (now >= silence_at and no hold in `holds` has `session` = this one), the
    /// predicate T3 reads: a session is never silent while a hold it took is live (§3, 1.4, R27).
    pub silent: bool,
    pub caps: BTreeSet<Label>,
    pub horizon: Option<u32>,                // minutes
    /// The principals the session serves (CS-1), at the agent's word: bound by `hello {principal}`
    /// (at `SessionOpened` or later) and by every `from_user` it records. A per-person client passes
    /// its human's key from its own configuration; tokens bind no principal (FQ-5). Empty for a
    /// session that serves no human (a coding agent, a scheduled job): it gets no user items in
    /// `hello`, no `user_decisions` count, and no `principal:` notes (CS-3). Every alias of a
    /// principal it serves counts as served (`same_person`, D.8.11).
    pub principals: BTreeSet<PrincipalId>,
    /// The highest seq shown to this session per node (§9.2 `seen`).
    pub shown: BTreeMap<NodeId, Seq>,
    /// Per scope node `a`, the newest `holders:<a>` note delivered to this session (D-6, D.8.16):
    /// its inbox shows the live `holders:` notes of the branches it holds in that are newer than
    /// the cursor of their own scope (0 when absent). One entry per scope the session has read a
    /// note from: at most depth + 1 per node it has held, gone with the session at retirement.
    pub branch_seen: BTreeMap<NodeId, Eid>,
    /// 1.4 (§20.9 rule 12, R13): the principals this session has recorded a `to_user` to, each as
    /// named (`Appended(ToUser)` inserts its principal; aliases are read through `same_person`
    /// when rule 12 runs). Base state, because a `to_user` entry's metadata leaves memory
    /// (D.4.12) while the session lives; at most one entry per principal it reported to, gone
    /// with the session at retirement.
    pub told: BTreeSet<PrincipalId>,
    /// 1.12 (§10.4): the hold this session last released as `handoff`, and the release plus the
    /// hold's `lease.first`: `next` (D.8.5), `leave_better` (D.8.7), and rule 13 keep that node
    /// from the session while its `fence` is still the token's and that time has not come
    /// (`handed_back`). Set by the release's `Appended`; `#[serde(default)]`.
    pub handed_off: Option<HandedOff>,   // HandedOff { token: Token, until: Time }
}

pub struct OpRecord {
    pub digest: ReqDigest,
    /// The session the first execution ran in (CS-8): a repeat that names another session is
    /// `op_id_conflict`, so a colliding `op_id` never hands one agent another's token (D.8.1).
    pub session: SessionId,
    /// `at + op.retain` of the first execution (a snapshot): the record answers repeats while
    /// `expires_at > now`, and evolve drops it at the first event at or after that time (CS-8).
    pub expires_at: Time,
}
```

The full outcome of the first execution is in its `OpRecorded` event, in the history; the shell keeps
the rendered response bytes with the record in its `st_ops` row and returns them on a repeat
(D.11.6). The core keeps only what O1 compares: 1.1's record with the full `Result<Done, Error>` was
0.9 to 1.9 TB a year at 10,000 agents (review TP-7), for a value no command reads.

Session status text and the `hello` intent text are not in the core; they are in the events, and the
shell's `sessions` table points at those events for the live and silent sessions that `talk who`
lists; a retired session's row leaves it, and history views read the events (D.11.6).

### D.4.8 Deadlines

```rust
/// Kind order of §17. Derived Ord follows the declaration order.
pub enum DeadlineKind {
    Lease, Wait, Recheck, UserQuestion, Commitment, OccurrenceSlot, OccurrenceWindow,
    RefusalExpiry, Due, Pause, Silence, Retire,
}

/// Derived Ord follows the declaration order, then the payload (A-43).
pub enum Owner {
    Hold(Token),                    // Lease
    Node(NodeId),                   // Wait, OccurrenceSlot, OccurrenceWindow, Due, Pause (scope)
    Entry(Eid),                     // Recheck (people question), UserQuestion, Commitment
    Refusal(NodeId, ClassName),     // RefusalExpiry of the entries of one refusal record (CS-7)
    Class(ClassName),               // RefusalExpiry: a caps profile's window ends (A-27, CS-7)
    Session(SessionId),             // Silence, Retire (CS-8)
}

/// Fires in derived order (at, kind, owner), as §17 requires.
pub struct DeadlineKey { pub at: Time, pub kind: DeadlineKind, pub owner: Owner }
```

The pure deadline function, one clause per kind. A deadline exists exactly while its owner still
needs the firing; firing it applies a transition or sets a one-shot marker, after which the clause
returns `None`. All times are stored in the owner when it is created or refreshed, so a
`ParamsChanged` never moves a queued deadline.

```rust
pub fn deadline_of(s: &State, kind: DeadlineKind, owner: &Owner) -> Option<Time>;
```

| Kind | Owner | Queued while | At | Firing (D.8.2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lease | `Hold(t)` | `t` in `holds` | `lease_until` | `HoldEnded{Expired}` removes the hold |
| Wait | `Node(n)` | `n` open, its wait is `Time(T)` or `External(T)`, `!wait.fired` | `T` | sets `wait.fired` |
| Recheck | `Entry(q)` | `pquestions[q].state = Open` | `recheck_at` | next recheck, expiry, or escalation |
| UserQuestion | `Entry(q)` | `uquestions[q]` `Pending`, with or without a default (CS-2) | `due` | `UqDefaulted` with a default; otherwise `UqReaddressed` to the next stage, or `UqLapsed` at the last |
| Commitment | `Entry(c)` | `commitments[c]` `Open` and `!followup_fired` | `followup_at` | sets `followup_fired` |
| OccurrenceSlot | `Node(o)` | `o` open occurrence, phase `Waiting` | `slot` | `OccurrenceAvailable` |
| OccurrenceWindow | `Node(o)` | `o` open occurrence, phase `Available`, `!window_fired` | `window_end` | sets `window_fired`, then the missed check |
| RefusalExpiry | `Refusal(n, c)` | `(n, c)` in `refusals` | the smallest `expires_at` of its entries | `RefusalExpired` removes the entries that expired (CS-7) |
| RefusalExpiry | `Class(c)` | `c` in `classes` | the smallest window end in `caps_seen` | removes the profiles whose window ended, then the E1 check (CS-7) |
| Due | `Node(n)` | `n` open, `due = Some(d)`, `!due_fired` | `d` | sets `due_fired` |
| Stale (1.8, last in §17's order) | `Node(n)` | `n` open, not reserved, `touched_at = Some(t)`, `!stale_fired`, `offer_stale = Some(d)` | `t + d` | sets `stale_fired`; `stale` turns on where its other conditions hold (D.8.3) |
| Pause | `Node(p)` | `p` in `pauses` | `until` | `PauseExpired` |
| Silence | `Session(s)` | `!sessions[s].silent` | `max(silence_at, the largest lease_until of the holds with session = s, last_now)` (1.4, R27: never while a hold it took is live; found through `ix.holds_by_session[s]`, recounted over `holds`; the floor at `last_now` binds only while an event at `last_now` has just ended the session's last hold after its `silence_at`) | sets `silent`, then `said` entries become unconfirmed |
| Retire | `Session(s)` | `s` in `sessions` | `retire_at` | `SessionRetired` removes the session (CS-8) |

```rust
/// The queue recount: every owner's deadline. T4 compares it with ix.deadlines.
pub fn recount_deadlines(s: &State) -> BTreeSet<DeadlineKey>;
```

A refusal entry's `backoff_until` has no deadline: only `next` reads it, as a predicate at its own
`now`, and no flag, classification, or E1 condition depends on it (D.0.2, principle 3; CS-7).

**A holder's silence** (1.4, §3, R27). A checkpoint within `presence.resolution` of a take touches
nothing (CS-14) but extends the lease (to `lease.default` and beyond), so under 1.3 a holder fell
silent at `silence_at` while its hold was live and saw `STALE SESSION` on its next call. The Silence
deadline therefore waits for the later of `silence_at` and the end of the session's last lease, read
from its at most `hold.per_session` holds. Lease ends move only at `HoldIssued`, `HoldExtended`, and
`HoldEnded`, so those events sync the owner `Session(h.session)` too (D.7.4). The Lease key of the
last hold has rank `Hold`, before `Session`, so at an equal time the hold ends first and the session
then falls silent holding nothing; the deadline is still a pure function of the base state (T4).

The key is floored at `last_now`. When the last hold ends after `silence_at`, which is R27's own
case (a checkpoint made the lease outlive `silence_at`), the larger of the other two terms is
`silence_at`, which lies before the event: at a lease's expiry, and when another session's command
ends the hold early, by `close_node`'s `held_by_other`, a merge, or a move. Without the floor the
key would land in the past, against T1 (a firing's `at >= last_now`) and T4. With it, the key lies
at the event's time: after an expiry, the Silence firing follows the Lease firing at the same time;
in a command, the key lies at exactly `now`, and the post-settle of D.8.1 fires it in the same call,
so the holder's pending `said` entries become unconfirmed there. On a settled state the floor never
binds: a session that is not silent holds a hold whose `lease_until > now`, or has
`silence_at > now` (T3).

**The Stale key** (1.8, §14). It is queued for every open node that is not reserved and was touched
since 1.8, whether or not the node is an offer: whether it is one (`offer`, capacity, no container)
is the flag's question (D.8.3). A tag, a capacity, or a role can change without a touch (a
`NodeUpdated` touches, but an `OfferSet` at a hold's end does not), and a key conditioned on them
could then appear in the past (T4). A `ParamsChanged` sets every open node's marker to
`touched_at + offer.stale <= at` and re-reads every node's key, so a lowered `offer.stale` neither
leaves a key in the past nor loses one.

`evolve` sets every marker that would put a deadline at or before the event's own time when the
owner is created or changed: `due_fired := due <= at`, `wait.fired := T <= at` (D.7.4). Commands
clamp the remaining agent-supplied times (A-68), so no command creates a deadline earlier than its
`now`. Two can equal `now`: a user question whose explicit `due` lay in the past, and the Silence
key of a session whose last hold the command ended after that session's `silence_at` (above, 1.4);
the post-settle of D.8.1 fires both in the same call.

### D.4.9 Statistics

Statistics feed `control health` and the coverage warning only; no decision reads them.

```rust
pub struct Stats {
    /// Day index -> counters. Pruned by evolve to the days within capacity.window of the
    /// event's `at` (deterministic, monotone in `at`, so it commutes with T2).
    pub days: BTreeMap<u64, DayStats>,
    /// Held minutes of the last DONE_RING nodes closed Done, oldest first (§17 "median of
    /// completed work", A-41).
    pub done_minutes: Vec<u64>,
    /// Open nodes whose estimate is already in `demand_min`: a node counts once per opening,
    /// however often it is handed off (A-41). Inserted when the node first becomes a
    /// `Cand::Node`; removed at its `NodeClosed`, so a reopened node counts again. Bounded by
    /// the open nodes.
    pub demand_counted: BTreeSet<NodeId>,
    /// The (caps, horizon) profiles of sessions (CS-9), keyed by the caps and the bit length of the
    /// horizon (0..=32; 33 for no horizon), each with the largest horizon seen under that key and
    /// the time it was last seen (opened, or set by `hello`). `Unreachable` reads it (D.8.22); it is
    /// history, because a session's profile outlives the session. Agents set the horizon to their
    /// remaining budget, so exact horizons would make about one key per session within
    /// capacity.window (3.4 × 10⁶ a week at the base profile); bit lengths make at most 34 per caps
    /// set. Pruned by evolve at each `SessionOpened` and `SessionHello` from the front of
    /// `ix.profiles_by_time`, to the keys seen within capacity.window, at O(what expired).
    pub profiles: BTreeMap<(BTreeSet<Label>, u8), ProfileSeen>,
    /// Session starts per UTC minute (`at / 60_000`), pruned by evolve at each `SessionOpened` to
    /// the minutes within coverage.window of its `at` (CS-17): at most 40,320 counters, where 1.1
    /// kept every start (4 × 10⁸ a year at 10,000 agents). The coverage check reads them (D.8.18);
    /// history, because sessions retire.
    pub starts: BTreeMap<u64, u32>,
}

/// The largest horizon seen under a profile key (None: no horizon), and when the key was last seen.
/// The largest may come from a session seen earlier in the window than `last_seen`; within one bit
/// length that over-reports reachability by less than a factor of 2, which `Unreachable` accepts.
pub struct ProfileSeen { pub max_horizon: Option<u32>, pub last_seen: Time }

pub struct DayStats {
    pub demand_min: u64,      // estimated minutes of work that became hold candidates, each node
                              // once per opening (Stats::demand_counted)
    pub supply_ms: u64,       // time held in holds that made progress: a checkpoint during the
                              // hold, a release, or a close or merge of the node (CS-31)
    pub lost_ms: u64,         // time held in holds that expired, or were moved off, without a
                              // checkpoint: the holds that count as attempts (CS-31)
    pub next_calls: u32,
    pub next_empty: u32,      // `next` found no candidate at all (CS-31)
    pub next_empty_for_you: u32, // candidates existed, and every one was excluded for the caller
    pub flagged_end: u32,     // |ix.flagged_active| after the day's last flag change (CS-31);
                              // set to the current count when the day's entry is created
}
```

A day's entry is created on its first use (`index::day_stats`) with `flagged_end` set to
`|ix.flagged_active|` at that moment, the count the day began with, and every later change of the
count records itself in its day. So a day on which no flag changed but another counter did holds
the count it began with, and a recorded 0 is a value, not a missing one: `FlagsPilingUp` reads it
as such (D.8.22). Before WP-D6 a new entry started at 0, so a day with other counters but no flag
change recorded a count of 0 it never had.

The statistics that decisions do read are the times of each principal's messages (`State::user_msgs`,
history, for the p90 due and absence, D.8.12) and the classes' caps profiles from their open `next`
calls (`State::classes`, base, CS-7).

### D.4.10 Derived indices

```rust
pub struct Ix {
    pub node: BTreeMap<NodeId, NodeIx>,
    pub children: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<NodeId>>,        // from Node::place
    pub flagged_children: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<NodeId>>,// parent -> children with flags
    /// Parent -> the children with `subtree_live > 0` (attended): what `holders:` delivery and `who
    /// {at}` descend through, so a parent with 10⁶ closed children costs nothing there. Updated on
    /// the ancestor chain when a node's `subtree_live` crosses 0 (HoldIssued, HoldEnded, NodeMoved).
    pub attended_children: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<NodeId>>,
    /// Parent -> the children that `leave_better` may suggest (`unheld_flagged`, D.8.7), and the
    /// same nodes by their candidate partition, so that neither form scans flagged nodes it would
    /// skip. Updated at the flag, candidate, and hold refresh of the node (D.7.4).
    pub unheld_flagged_children: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<NodeId>>,
    pub unheld_flagged_by_part: BTreeMap<PartKey, BTreeSet<NodeId>>,
    pub keys_open: BTreeMap<KeyStr, NodeId>,                 // K1: a map, so at most one
    pub keys_all: BTreeMap<KeyStr, BTreeSet<NodeId>>,        // open and closed carriers
    pub origins: BTreeMap<KeyStr, RequestId>,                // Q1, one per message (A-61)
    pub unsettled_requests: BTreeSet<RequestId>,             // the board's first pages (§18)
    /// User requests by requester (CS-25 board filter): all of them, and the unsettled ones.
    pub requests_by: BTreeMap<PrincipalId, BTreeSet<RequestId>>,
    pub unsettled_by: BTreeMap<PrincipalId, BTreeSet<RequestId>>,
    /// The people entries of each node (request, said, heard, question, answer), by seq: what
    /// `moved` lists (D.8.15, CS-17). Feed pages are the shell's (D.4.5).
    pub people: BTreeMap<(NodeId, Seq), Eid>,
    pub items: BTreeMap<NodeId, NodeItems>,                  // entities whose home is the node
    /// Decisions that list the request and are not retracted (§9.4: a superseded decision
    /// still counts). A decision leaves the set only at its DecisionRetracted.
    pub settling: BTreeMap<RequestId, BTreeSet<DecisionId>>,
    pub clarifications: BTreeMap<RequestId, BTreeSet<UserEntryId>>,
    pub flagged: BTreeSet<NodeId>,                           // flags != {}
    /// Flagged nodes that are `next` candidates (in `ix.next.of`, held back or not) or carry a live
    /// hold of their own: the work `FlagsPilingUp` watches (CS-31). A flagged node that nobody can
    /// take (a merged node, a capacity-0 node) is `NoMover`'s business, not growth.
    pub flagged_active: BTreeSet<NodeId>,
    pub next: NextIx,                                        // the candidate index (CS-16, D.8.5)
    pub series_open: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<NodeId>>,     // series -> open occurrences (K6)
    /// Series -> its flagged occurrences, open or closed, wherever they are in the tree: the nodes
    /// whose classification depends on the series being open (`occ_locked`), which a close,
    /// reopen, or change of `repeat` of the series refreshes (D.7.4). An occurrence moved out of
    /// its series is no longer its child, so `flagged_children` does not find it (WP-D6). Kept by
    /// the node refresh (its flags) and the `OccurrenceDetached` arm (it leaves its series), and
    /// recounted from the flagged occurrences by their series (R1).
    pub flagged_occurrences: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<NodeId>>,
    /// 1.4 (§20.4, D.14.5): the nodes whose `agreements` are not empty, open or closed, by id: what
    /// `view agreements` reads, so that its answer does not depend on where in the tree the
    /// agreements sit.
    pub agreements: BTreeSet<NodeId>,
    pub unrouted: BTreeSet<UserEntryId>,                     // N1
    /// Pending user questions by current addressee `to[stage]`, in `hello` order (CS-3, CS-33).
    pub pending_uq_by: BTreeMap<PrincipalId, BTreeSet<UqRank>>,
    pub refusal_question: BTreeMap<NodeId, QuestionId>,      // pending Refusal{n} question
    /// Pending digest entries by audience principal, oldest first (CS-5).
    pub pending_digest_by: BTreeMap<PrincipalId, BTreeSet<DigestId>>,
    pub waiters: BTreeMap<WaitKey, BTreeSet<NodeId>>,        // reverse of Node::wait
    pub dependents: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<NodeId>>,      // reverse of depends_on
    /// Reverse of `Node::links`: target -> (relation, source), what `view node {view: full}`
    /// lists as incoming links (CS-22).
    pub backlinks: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<(LinkRel, NodeId)>>,
    /// The `Active` decisions whose basis names the target (CS-22): what rests on a node or an
    /// entry, and whose staleness a change of the target refreshes (D-4). A node reference is filed
    /// under `Node(resolve_merged(m))`, so that a merge re-files the citers of `from` under `into`,
    /// and a refutation of `into` reaches them (D.8.17).
    pub cited_by: BTreeMap<BasisTarget, BTreeSet<DecisionId>>,
    pub marked_by_question: BTreeMap<QuestionId, BTreeSet<NodeId>>, // reverse of the marks
    pub holds_by_session: BTreeMap<SessionId, BTreeSet<Token>>,
    /// The `said` entries each session recorded that are `Pending` or `Unconfirmed` (1.2's
    /// `pending_saids`, widened by 1.3, when rule 2 of the next calls read both states). Since
    /// 1.5 rule 2 reads only the `Pending` ones: an entry the session listed in `unsent`, or left
    /// by falling silent, is unconfirmed, and its node's `unconfirmed_said` is for whoever checks
    /// the conversation (§20.9; the final usability round). The Silence arm, a release, and a
    /// close read the `Pending` ones too (D.8.2, D.8.10).
    pub open_saids_by: BTreeMap<SessionId, BTreeSet<SaidId>>,
    /// The unrouted `from_user` entries each session recorded (`UserEntry::session`): rule 5 of
    /// the next calls (§20.9).
    pub unrouted_by: BTreeMap<SessionId, BTreeSet<UserEntryId>>,
    pub refused: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<ClassName>>,      // reverse of refusals
    pub live_sessions: BTreeSet<SessionId>,                  // not silent
    pub live_by_class: BTreeMap<ClassName, u32>,             // |live sessions| per class (CS-21)
    /// (expires_at, class, op_id) of every op record, and (until, note) of every note: evolve
    /// drops their front at each event (CS-8, CS-17).
    pub ops_expiry: BTreeSet<(Time, ClassName, OpId)>,
    pub notes_until: BTreeSet<(Time, NoteId)>,
    /// (time, entity) of `State::leaving`: evolve drops the front (D.4.12).
    pub leaving_by_time: BTreeSet<(Time, EntityRef)>,
    /// Bound, unread notes of the sessions in `sessions`: a note whose recipient has retired (an
    /// answer to a retired asker) is in no inbox (CS-8).
    pub inbox: BTreeMap<SessionId, BTreeSet<NoteId>>,
    pub pending_holder: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<NoteId>>,  // holder: notes waiting for a taker
    /// Live `holders:<a>` notes by their scope `a`, read when a session's inbox is read (D-6).
    pub branch_notes: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<NoteId>>,
    /// (until, note) of `principal:` notes, by principal (CS-3).
    pub user_notes: BTreeMap<PrincipalId, BTreeSet<(Time, NoteId)>>,
    pub principal_key: BTreeMap<PrincipalId, PrincipalKey>,  // reverse of principal_ids
    /// The directory (D.2.2, D-3): each alias principal -> its person node (an open child of PEOPLE
    /// carrying `person:<key>`), and each person node -> its alias principals.
    pub person_of: BTreeMap<PrincipalId, NodeId>,
    pub aliases_of: BTreeMap<NodeId, BTreeSet<PrincipalId>>,
    /// (last seen, key) of `stats.profiles`, for its prune (D.4.9); and each class's caps profiles
    /// by window end, for its RefusalExpiry deadline (D.4.6).
    pub profiles_by_time: BTreeSet<(Time, (BTreeSet<Label>, u8))>,
    pub class_ends: BTreeMap<ClassName, BTreeSet<(Time, BTreeSet<Label>)>>,
    pub deadlines: BTreeSet<DeadlineKey>,                    // T4: == recount_deadlines
    pub deadline_at: BTreeMap<(DeadlineKind, Owner), Time>,  // for O(log n) move and cancel
}

pub enum WaitKey { Node(NodeId), Question(QuestionId) }      // people and user questions

/// The `hello` order of an addressee's pending questions (CS-33): the `about` node's priority,
/// highest first (0 without `about`), then the due, then the id. Derived Ord, field order.
pub struct UqRank { pub neg_priority: i64, pub due: Time, pub q: QuestionId }

/// A candidate for `next` (§10.4). Derived Ord: Node < Status < Route (the kind rank).
pub enum Cand { Node(NodeId), Status(NodeId), Route(UserEntryId) }

/// The candidate index of `next` (CS-16, D.8.5). Every candidate of the classification is in `of`.
/// One that no session-independent exclusion holds back is also in its partition, in key order, so
/// that a session's best candidate is a range query; one held back (an open `depends_on` target, or
/// a pause over it) is in `held` instead, ready to move back.
pub struct NextIx {
    pub of: BTreeMap<Cand, CandAt>,
    pub parts: BTreeMap<PartKey, BTreeSet<NextKey>>,
    pub held: BTreeMap<Cand, Held>,
    pub nodes: u32,                  // Node and Status entries of `of`: the backlog (CS-21)
    /// 1.4 (§10.4, R27): the open nodes that the classification would make a `Cand::Node` but for
    /// an unresolved wait (the row "n open, waiting(n)" of D.8.5), so that an empty `next` counts
    /// them (`EmptyWhy::waiting`). Kept at the same flag and candidate refresh as `of`.
    pub waiting: BTreeSet<NodeId>,
    /// The non-empty partitions' needs sets as a trie over their sorted labels, each end holding
    /// the partitions' est buckets: a caller's eligible needs sets are found by descending only
    /// through labels it has, at O(eligible sets and their prefixes), not O(all partitions) (D.8.5).
    pub needs_trie: NeedsTrie,
}
pub struct NeedsTrie { pub buckets: BTreeSet<u8>, pub next: BTreeMap<Label, NeedsTrie> }
/// Where a candidate sits. `since` repeats `State::since[c]`, its source.
pub struct CandAt { pub since: Time, pub part: PartKey, pub key: NextKey }
/// A partition: the candidate's `needs`, and its `est` bucket: 0 without `est`, else the bit length
/// of `est` (1..=32), so a bucket below the bit length of a session's horizon fits it entirely.
/// Routing items are in the partition with no needs and bucket 0.
pub struct PartKey { pub needs: BTreeSet<Label>, pub est_bucket: u8 }
/// Derived Ord, field order: the tier; the hour group `⌊since / 1 h⌋ − priority` (smaller is older,
/// so it orders like −aged, CS-12); the ring position `fnv_id(id)` (D.2.6); the id; the kind rank.
pub struct NextKey { pub tier: u8, pub group: i64, pub fnv: u64, pub id: u64, pub kind: u8 }
/// Why a candidate is held back for every caller: an open `depends_on` target, and the nearest
/// paused ancestor-or-self, if any.
pub struct Held { pub depends: bool, pub paused_by: Option<NodeId> }

pub struct NodeIx {
    pub flags: FlagSet,
    pub depth: u32,                 // ROOT = 0
    pub children: u32,
    pub open_agent_children: u32,   // open children with origin Agent or Ancestor (L1, CS-10);
                                    //   L1 does not compare it at PEOPLE and TEAMS (A-113)
    pub open_children: u32,
    pub held_children: u32,         // children with a live hold on themselves
    pub flagged_children: u32,
    pub live: u32,                  // live holds on the node itself
    pub subtree_live: u32,          // live holds on the node or any descendant ("attended")
    pub sub: Subtree,               // the descendants by state (CS-32)
}

/// The node's descendants, not the node itself, by state (CS-32): progress below a node (how many
/// sub-lemmas are proved, refuted, or open), exact however large the subtree, where `view list`
/// stops at SCAN_MAX visits. `u64`: ROOT counts every node of the forum.
pub struct Subtree {
    pub open: u64,
    pub done: u64,                  // closed with outcome `done`
    pub failed: u64,                // closed with outcome `failed`
    pub other: u64,                 // closed with any other outcome (dropped, superseded, missed, …)
    pub flagged: u64,               // with flags, open or closed
}

pub struct NodeItems {
    // every entity whose home is the node: history views, merges, and recounts
    pub requests: BTreeSet<RequestId>,
    pub pquestions: BTreeSet<QuestionId>,
    pub aquestions: BTreeSet<QuestionId>,
    pub uquestions: BTreeSet<QuestionId>,    // user questions with `about = Some(n)` (A-92)
    pub commitments: BTreeSet<CommitmentId>,
    pub saids: BTreeSet<SaidId>,
    pub decisions: BTreeSet<DecisionId>,
    pub objections: BTreeSet<ObjectionId>,
    // the open subsets that flags, answers, and brief sections read (CS-20)
    pub unsettled: BTreeSet<RequestId>,                  // settled = None
    /// The requesters of the unsettled user requests on the node, each with its oldest such
    /// request, ordered by it: `(r, p)`. `chain` and `audience` read the first few (D.8.12).
    pub requesters_by_age: BTreeSet<(RequestId, PrincipalId)>,
    /// settled = None and answered_by = None, by `Request::conv`: a `said` answers only its own
    /// conversation's (§9.4, 1.3), so it reads one entry, not the node's other conversations
    pub unanswered: BTreeMap<KeyStr, BTreeSet<RequestId>>,
    /// Unsettled and unanswered, and listed by a decision that is not retracted (`ix.settling`
    /// non-empty): owed a reply (rule 6 of §20.9).
    pub owed_reply: BTreeSet<RequestId>,
    /// Unsettled with an answer, so no such decision lists it: owed a decision (rules 7 and 8).
    pub owed_decision: BTreeSet<RequestId>,
    pub open_pq: BTreeMap<KeyStr, BTreeSet<QuestionId>>,  // people questions `Open`, by conversation
    pub open_commitments: BTreeSet<CommitmentId>,        // `Open`
    pub open_saids: BTreeSet<SaidId>,                    // `Pending` or `Unconfirmed`
    pub unconfirmed: BTreeSet<SaidId>,                   // `Unconfirmed`
    pub open_objections: BTreeSet<ObjectionId>,          // `Open`
    pub active_decisions: BTreeSet<DecisionId>,          // `Active`
    pub stale_basis: BTreeSet<DecisionId>,               // `Active`, with a stale reference (D-4)
}

/// The fourteen flags of §14, in table order: the twelve of 1.1's first release,
/// `basis_changed` (one hop, D-4), and `stale` (1.8).
pub enum Flag {
    Unrouted, UnansweredRequest, OpenCommitment, UnconfirmedSaid, OpenIntent, QuestionRecheck,
    ProceedOnAssumption, Objection, BasisChanged, TooBig, Overdue, ReadyToClose, Missed, Stale,
}
/// Bit i is the Flag with discriminant i.
pub struct FlagSet(pub u16);

pub enum Mark { Recheck, Assume }

/// Full recount of every index from the base state at `now`. R1, F, and T4 compare with it.
pub fn recount(s: &State, now: Time) -> Ix;
```

Every index is maintained incrementally by `evolve` (D.7.4) and compared with `recount` by
`check_invariants`. The rollup of §5 ("how many children are open, held, and flagged") is
`open_children`, `held_children`, and `flagged_children`; the subtree rollup `sub` (CS-32) counts
every descendant by state, and is recounted by adding each node to each of its ancestors, while
`evolve` keeps it with O(depth) work per event: a create, close, or reopen changes one count on each
ancestor, a node whose flags turn empty or non-empty changes `flagged` on each ancestor, and a move
takes the node and its own `sub` off the old ancestors and adds them to the new ones (D.7.4). The
basis indices are recounted from the `Active` decisions: `cited_by` by each node and entry
reference, and `stale_basis` by `stale` over each one's references (D.8.17); `backlinks` from
`Node::links`. `ix.next` is recounted from the classification of every node and entry, with the
`since` of each candidate read from `State::since`, which depends on history and is stored rather
than recounted (its key set must equal `ix.next.of`'s, and every value is at most `now`). The open
subsets of `NodeItems` are recounted from the entities' states, so a flag refresh, an answer, and a
brief cost O(open items on the node) rather than O(its history): a conversation node near the root
collects 10⁴ to 10⁵ items, and about 50 hold events a second refresh its flags (review TP-13,
FS-16). Every index is recounted over the resident state: an entity that left memory is in no index
(D.4.12). `user_msgs` is history, not an index (D.4.2): a recount from the user entries would need
entries that left memory, and would disagree with the stored times after a `ParamsChanged` of
`user_gap.window` until each principal wrote again. `attended_children`, the `unheld_flagged` sets,
`person_of` and `aliases_of`, `branch_notes`, `profiles_by_time`, `class_ends`, `leaving_by_time`,
and the needs trie are recounted from what they index, `flagged_occurrences` from the flagged
occurrences by their series, `ix.agreements` (1.4) from the nodes whose `agreements` are not empty,
and `ix.next.waiting` (1.4) from the classification of every open waiting node.

The four indices that 1.3's next calls read (§20.9, D.8.26) are recounted the same way:
`open_saids_by` from the resident `said` entries by `Said::session` and state, and `unrouted_by` from
the resident user entries by `UserEntry::session` and routing, both only for the sessions in
`sessions` (a retired session is nobody's "you": its entries stay with their flags, `unconfirmed_said`
and `unrouted`, as their movers), and `owed_reply` and `owed_decision` from
each node's unsettled requests, their `answered_by`, and `ix.settling`. `evolve` keeps them in the
arms that already touch their sources: `Appended(Said)`, `SaidConfirmed`, and `SessionRetired` for
the first; `Appended(FromUser)`, `EntryRouted`, and `SessionRetired` for the second; `Appended(Request)`, `RequestAnswered`, `RequestSettled`,
`RequestMoved`, a decision's `Appended` with `settles`, and `DecisionRetracted` (each request the
decision lists) for the last two. None of their members is finished, so none leaves memory while
listed (D.4.12). They let a session's next calls cost
O(log) per item even on a held hub with 10⁴ unsettled requests (D.12.8), where a scan of
`unsettled` would grow with the hub.

### D.4.11 Size

At the production profile (25,000 sessions a year): at most a day of sessions with their `shown`
maps, 10,000 to 20,000 nodes with their content, the metadata of the entries the core keeps, and
small entity maps: well under 100 MB a year, held by the single writer and loaded from the state
tables at startup (D.11.8) in about a second. The personal profile is about a tenth of it. Feed texts
never enter the core.

At 10,000 agents (0.9 to 4.4 × 10⁸ sessions a year, review §4) 1.1's state grew by 651 to 2,645 GB a
year, mostly `op_id` records with full outcomes, entry metadata, and sessions. With session
retirement, `op_id` expiry, notes dropped at `until`, entry metadata only where the core reads it,
and session starts as minute counters (CS-8, CS-17), what is live takes 0.35 to 1.5 GB whatever the
forum's age. The finished entities (settled requests, answered questions, confirmed `said` entries,
superseded decisions, and their entry metadata) are made at 62 to 248 GB a year; each leaves memory
`FINISHED_RETAIN` (7 days) after it finished, so memory holds about a week of them, 1.2 to 4.8 GB,
and their rows stay in the state tables (D-5, D.4.12). Nodes are the exception in the first release: they stay in memory for good until WP-D8 (D.4.13,
planned after the release). Startup loads only the resident rows, so its
time follows this bounded size whatever the forum's age: gate G-7 loads a year of the high profile
within 5 minutes (D.12.8). Accepting the growth for a year instead would make every restart (a token
revocation, a parameter fix, a crash) cost about 40 minutes at month 12, at G-7's own rate of 1 GB per
10 s.

### D.4.12 Finished entities leave memory (D-5)

The core keeps an entity only while a rule may read it without a command naming it. An entity that
has finished, and that no such rule still needs, leaves memory `FINISHED_RETAIN` after that moment;
its state rows stay in the state tables, marked not resident (D.11.6), and the history keeps every
event, so nothing is deleted. The rule is the entity's own state, wherever its node is: reserved
nodes (`@user` and its children never close) and long-lived open hubs are covered as well as
archived nodes.

```rust
/// An entity the core may drop from memory and restore (D-5).
pub enum EntityRef {
    Request(RequestId), PQuestion(QuestionId), UQuestion(QuestionId), Commitment(CommitmentId),
    Said(SaidId), Decision(DecisionId), Objection(ObjectionId), UserEntry(UserEntryId),
    Digest(DigestId), Meta(Eid),
}
/// One entity brought back by `Ev::Restored`, with the metadata of the entry it was born from.
pub enum Restored {
    Request(RequestId, Request, EntryMeta), PQuestion(QuestionId, PQuestion, EntryMeta),
    UQuestion(QuestionId, UQuestion, EntryMeta), Commitment(CommitmentId, Commitment, EntryMeta),
    Said(SaidId, Said, EntryMeta), Decision(DecisionId, Decision, EntryMeta),
    Objection(ObjectionId, Objection, EntryMeta), UserEntry(UserEntryId, UserEntry, EntryMeta),
    Digest(DigestId, DigestEntry, EntryMeta), Meta(Eid, EntryMeta),
}
```

| Entity | Finished when | Held back while |
|---|---|---|
| Request | settled | — |
| People question | answered or superseded; expired with its assumption recorded; escalated once its user question is finished | a wait or a mark names it |
| User question | answered or defaulted; lapsed with its assumption recorded; lapsed, with source `Escalation { q }`, once `q` was answered, or once `q` has left memory, which it does only once answered, since an escalated people question leaves only after its user question is finished and only an open one is superseded (`evolve::answered_late`, mirrored by `spec::leaving_expected`; a late answer withdrew the assumption: the year simulation's Y-1, 2026-10-03, built in WP-D6) | a wait or a mark names it; with source `Escalation { q }`, while `q` is resident (E1 (d)) |
| Commitment | fulfilled | — |
| `said` | confirmed | it is the `answered_by` of a resident request (Settled reads its kind and its conversation key) |
| Decision | superseded or retracted | an active decision cites it (`ix.cited_by`), or an unsettled request lists it (`ix.settling`: a superseded decision still settles) |
| Objection | resolved | — |
| User entry | routed, and its request (a `Request` or `Clarifies` routing), if any, settled | — |
| Digest entry | shown; or pending for DIGEST_RETAIN, after which it leaves at once, counted in `State::digest_left[to]` (CS-5) | — |
| Agent question | leaves with its note at `until`, whatever its state | — |
| Entry metadata | with the last entity born from it (an `ack` bears a `said` and a commitment); an entry that bears none (answer, `heard`, `to_user`, approve, resolve, retract) from its own `at` | while it is the `answered_by` of a resident request |

**How an entity leaves.** `evolve` records in `State::leaving` the time an entity leaves:
`FINISHED_RETAIN` after the event that finished it, or after the event that removed the last
reference holding it back (a wait or a mark cleared, a citer superseded, a request settled); for a
pending digest entry, DIGEST_RETAIN after its creation, until it is shown. Step 1 of `evolve` (D.7.4)
pops `ix.leaving_by_time` while `time <= e.at`: the entity leaves its map and every index, its home
node's `left` rises (and `people_left`, for a people entry's metadata), a pending digest entry is
counted in `digest_left[to]`, and `evolve_tracked` marks its facts dirty and records its last value
in `Tracked::departed` before removing it (D.6.1), so the shell writes that value to its rows, marked
not resident, instead of deleting them. Like the expiry prune, it is monotone in `at`, so it
commutes with T2. An agent question and its note leave together at `until` (the notes prune). A
people question that leaves lets go of the user questions it escalated to, which it held back, and
finds them by a scan of `uquestions`, so its departure costs O(resident user questions); an index
of user questions by source would make it O(log n), and none exists yet.

**Reads.** Every rule that reads an entity without a command naming it reads resident entities only,
and the "held back" column keeps resident what such a rule reads: the question of a live wait or
mark, the decisions a resident citer or an unsettled request names, a resident request's answer.
Queries that reach finished items show the resident ones and then continue from the state rows
through the shell (the board's settled rows, by eid or by `entries.principal`, D.8.8), or say what is
older: the brief's sections 3 and 4 of a node whose `left` is above 0 end with "older items are in the
feed" and a total of `≥k` (D.8.6); the `moved` warning's total is exact only for a `seen` at or above
the node's `people_left` (D.8.15).

**Commands.** A command that names an entity that left memory restores it first. In the writer job,
before `apply` (D.8.1), the shell checks every id the command names (the requests of `settles`,
`clarifies`, and `re`; the questions of `answers`, `heard {answers}`, and `waits_for: {question}`; the
decisions of `supersedes` and of entry references in `basis`; the `said` entries of `said_id`,
`corrects`, and `unsent`; objections; the user entries and digest entries of `re`; the user entry of
`talk route`; the user entries of the `user:e<n>` keys of `node create`; and, through its `origins` table, the request of a `request`'s origin, so Q1 holds across memory) and, for
each that is not resident but has a state row, decodes the row and calls the core's
`restore_tracked` (D.6.1), which checks that each item is absent and below `next_eid` and emits
`Restored { items }`, as a transaction of its own before the command's. An entity still
resident whose leaving time has come by `now` (`leaving_due`, D.6.1) would be pruned by the
command's first event, so the plan treats it as departed and restores it from its row, which is
current: `restore_tracked` keeps such an item, the `Restored` event's step 1 prunes it, and its arm
re-inserts it (WP-D6). `evolve` re-inserts the restored items with their indices, and sets their
`leaving` time from the restore, FINISHED_RETAIN or, for a pending digest entry, DIGEST_RETAIN
ahead, so nothing the command needs leaves during it; a restored digest entry that left unshown
comes out of `digest_left`. Restores are events, so the history replays to the same state. `talk
answer` to an agent question that left needs no restore: the shell adds the question's node and
asker from its `entries` table, and the answer is recorded and delivered as before (D.8.16).

**Checks.** Every state invariant ranges over the resident state, and R1 recounts it. O3 allows two
changes to `entries`: the prune, for metadata whose time has come, and `Restored` (D.9.2). D1 is
checked when the step creates the digest entries, because a shown entry leaves memory while its
question may stay. The proptests advance past FINISHED_RETAIN (D.12.3), and the persist-and-reload
test compares resident rows with the state and a restore with the row it read (D.12.6). The model
keeps every entity: FINISHED_RETAIN and DIGEST_RETAIN are real-time constants that no model run
reaches (D.10.5).

### D.4.13 Closed nodes leave memory (WP-D8, planned after the first release)

**Status.** Designed and reviewed on 2026-10-03; its implementation was deferred until after the
first release, to finish the release sooner. Until it lands, the first release keeps every node
in memory for good: at 10,000 agents that grows by tens to hundreds of GB a year (below), so gate
G-6 fails at that scale, and D.4.11's "whatever the forum's age" holds for the entities of D.4.12,
not for nodes. A personal or company forum (10⁴ to 10⁵ nodes) is unaffected. The design follows, as
written and revised after its adversarial review; the questions at its end are to be decided before
the work starts.

The core keeps every node for ever, with its title, body, fields, files, digest, and agreements
(D.4.3), and D.4.12 lets only finished entities leave memory. Gate G-6 (WP-F4) found the cost: its
smoke run made about 2,000 nodes a day at 30 simulated agents, and every one stayed resident. That
breaks D.4.11's claim that the live state is 0.35 to 1.5 GB whatever the forum's age, and G-6's own
bound of at most 10 GB, flat after FINISHED_RETAIN. WP-D8 lets a closed node that nothing live needs
leave memory a day later, with what is still on it. A write that names it brings it back with what
left with it; a read is served from its rows and brings nothing back. It reuses the mechanism D.4.12
built for entities: state rows marked not resident, a `Restored` event before the command, and the
shell's tables for what views show.

Agents see one thing 1.5 already shows for entities: when a write brings a node back, `view history`
of that node lists the `restored` event. Briefs, lists, `view find`, backlinks, warnings, and their
totals are what they would be had the node stayed (proptest item 16). This section amends D.4.2,
D.4.3, D.4.10 to D.4.12, D.5.2, D.6.1, D.7.2, D.7.4, D.7.6, D.8.2, D.8.4, D.8.6, D.8.9, D.8.19,
D.8.20, D.8.25, D.9.1, D.9.2, D.10.5, D.11.6 to D.11.8, D.11.11, D.11.15, D.12.1, D.12.3, D.12.5,
D.12.6, D.12.8, and D.13.2, each where it says.

#### How much memory nodes take

**Nodes a day.** D.15.2 supports two readings that differ by a factor of about 4.6:
- **Per session.** The review's session (740 s) makes 0.5 creates, 0.2 of which join, so 0.3 new
  nodes; multiplied by D.15.2's sessions a day. That gives 2.6 to 13 × 10⁷ nodes a year, the "up
  to 10⁸ nodes a year from the generic call mix" of D.15.1.
- **Per call.** `swarm-sim` keeps the review's counts as proportions of a profile's calls
  (`mix::WORKER`: 30 of 687 draws create), over sessions of 30 minutes at base rather than 740 s.
  Its smoke run made 2,000 nodes a day at 30 agents: 67 per agent-day, 3.1 % of base's 2,160 calls
  per agent-day, and 6.7 × 10⁵ a day at 10,000 agents.

| Profile | Sessions a day | Calls a day | New nodes a day, per session | New nodes a day, per call |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| low | 2.4 × 10⁵ | 1.08 × 10⁷ | 7.2 × 10⁴ | 3.3 × 10⁵ |
| base | 4.8 × 10⁵ | 2.16 × 10⁷ | 1.4 × 10⁵ | 6.7 × 10⁵ |
| high | 1.2 × 10⁶ | 4.32 × 10⁷ | 3.6 × 10⁵ | 1.3 × 10⁶ |

Occurrences (one per series and slot), signals, and missing ancestors add a few per cent. G-6
drives `swarm-sim`, so it meets the per-call reading. The design must hold at either reading
(D.15.1), and it is sized for the larger one.

**Bytes per node.** These are estimates from the types of D.4.3. G-6 measures the real figure as
bytes per resident node.
- **The `Node` itself.** Five texts, ten maps and sets, the role with a series' `repeat`, the
  counters, and the closure take about 0.8 KB inline. Ascending ids leave Rust's B-tree leaves about
  55 % full, so a slot of `nodes` costs 0.8 to 1.5 KB; a startup's bulk load packs them.
- **Small maps.** Each non-empty one (keys, tags, links, `depends_on`) allocates a leaf of about
  0.3 KB.
- **Indices.** `names`, `ix.node`, `ix.children`, `ix.keys_all`, and `ix.backlinks` add about 0.3 KB.

| Node | Its texts | In memory |
|---|---|---|
| `swarm-sim`'s: a 5-word title, a 40-word body, one key on half of them | 0.4 KB | about 2 to 2.5 KB |
| typical: a body of 1 to 4 KB, a digest, fields, a key or two | 2 to 6 KB | about 3 to 8 KB |
| research: D.4.3's 30 KB body | 30 KB | about 32 KB |

**Growth without WP-D8**, at 2.5 KB a node (typical nodes take 1.5 to 3 times as much):

| Profile | Nodes a year, per session | GB a year, per session | Nodes a year, per call | GB a year, per call |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| low | 2.6 × 10⁷ | 66 | 1.2 × 10⁸ | 304 |
| base | 5.3 × 10⁷ | 131 | 2.4 × 10⁸ | 608 |
| high | 1.3 × 10⁸ | 330 | 4.9 × 10⁸ | 1,215 |

G-6's 30 days at base hold 2.0 × 10⁷ nodes, about 50 GB, five times its bound.

**Active decisions** add to it.
- **They never leave.** A decision finishes only when it is superseded or retracted (D.4.12), and
  it stays in its node's `items`.
- **They are as frequent as nodes.** `talk decide` is 35 of 687 draws, and a close with `settles`
  records one too: about 2.2 × 10⁵ a day at base per session and 7.8 × 10⁵ per call, at 0.3 to 1 KB
  each with their metadata and the node's `NodeItems`.
- **The cost.** Another 24 to 285 GB a year at base. Worse, a node holding an active decision could
  never leave, so WP-D8 also lets the active decisions that no rule reads leave with their node
  (below).

**With WP-D8.** A closed node stays resident NODE_RETAIN (1 day) after it becomes free, and as long
as something live holds it before that. The resident closed nodes are then about `(1 + h)` days of
closures, where `h` is the mean time, in days, that something live holds a closed node: an
unfinished entity on it (an unsettled request, an open question or objection), an agent question
until its note's `until`, a closed subtree, which empties one level a day, or the knowledge graph
("What is left"). With D.4.11's live state and D.4.12's week of finished entities, at `h = 0`:

| Profile | A day of closures, per call, at 2.5 KB | the same at 3 to 8 KB | Live state | Finished entities | Total, at 2.5 KB | Total, at 3 to 8 KB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| low | 0.83 GB | 1.0 to 2.6 GB | 0.35 GB | 1.2 GB | 2.4 GB | 2.6 to 4.2 GB |
| base | 1.7 GB | 2.0 to 5.4 GB | 0.71 GB | 2.4 GB | 4.8 GB | 5.1 to 8.5 GB |
| high | 3.3 GB | 3.9 to 10.4 GB | 1.52 GB | 4.8 GB | 9.6 GB | 10.2 to 16.7 GB |

By the per-session reading, a day of closures is 4.6 times smaller. So G-6, at base with
`swarm-sim`'s nodes, expects about 4.8 GB, flat after FINISHED_RETAIN + NODE_RETAIN (8 days),
against its 10 GB. With typical nodes, base stays within 10 GB while `h` is below 0.3 to 2.4, and
high exceeds it even at `h = 0`. NODE_RETAIN is the lever: at an hour, a day of closures shrinks 24
times, at the price of a restore for each write to a node closed more than an hour before. G-6
reports `h`, the age histogram of the resident closed nodes, bytes per resident node, and restores an
hour by tool, so that the constant rests on a measurement (F19's variant has typical bodies).

#### When a node leaves

A node is **free** when it is closed, is not reserved (reserved nodes never close, K8), and none of
the references below holds it. A free node leaves memory NODE_RETAIN after it became free. It takes
with it the entities still homed at it and the metadata of its people entries, and a write that
names it brings them back with it (below).

```rust
/// How long a free node stays in memory (D.4.13). Real time, never scaled, and not a parameter of
/// §22, like FINISHED_RETAIN.
pub const NODE_RETAIN: Dur = Dur(86_400_000);
```

| # | The node is held while | The rule that would read it | Answered in O(log) by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | a resident child exists | K4, paths, depth, the rollups (§5) | `ix.children[n]` |
| 2 | an entity homed at it pins it (below) | flags, answers, settling, merges, briefs | `ix.pinned[n]` (new) |
| 3 | it has an open intent | the `open_intent` flag, M1 | `n.open_intent` |
| 4 | a resident node waits on it, depends on it, or is merged into it | T5's `reaches` from that node, `held.depends`, M1b's chains, K5's `resolve_merged` | `ix.waiters[Node(n)]`, `ix.dependents[n]`, `ix.merged_from[n]` (new) |
| 5 | an active decision's basis names it, as stored (before `merged_into`) | `stale`, and so `basis_changed` (D-4) | `ix.cited_ids[n]` (new) |
| 6 | a pause or a refusal record is on it | the Pause firing appends on its scope; `e1_check` reads the node | `pauses`, `ix.refused[n]` |
| 7 | its `agreements` are not empty | `view agreements` and `hello.orientation` read `ix.agreements` | `ix.agreements` |

**Entities.** Each entity has a home node:
- requests, people and agent questions, commitments, `said` entries, decisions, and objections:
  their `node`;
- a question for the user: its `about`;
- user entries and digest entries: the reserved `@user` and `@user/digest`.

An entity **pins** its home unless it has a `leaving` entry (D.4.12: finished, and not held back) or
it is a carried decision (below). An agent question has no `leaving` entry, so it pins its node until
it leaves with its note at `until`. Entry metadata never pins: a people entry's metadata leaves with
its node, an entity's with its entity, and any other at its own time. `ix.pinned[n]` counts the
entities that pin `n`. `evolve` adjusts it wherever an entity is created, changes state, gains or
loses its `leaving` entry, moves (a merge), leaves, or is restored, and wherever a decision gains or
loses a citer or an unsettled request that lists it.

A decision is **carried** when all of these hold:
- it is `Active`;
- its basis has no node reference and no entry reference;
- no active decision cites it (`ix.cited_by[Entry(d)]` is empty);
- no unsettled request lists it.

Such a decision never finishes by D.4.12's rule, but nothing reads it without a command naming it:
- `try_settle` reads it only for an unsettled request, which holds it back;
- a citer would hold it back;
- `stale` never fires on a basis without references.

So it leaves with its node and comes back with it. Two existing rules change with it:
- Settled's state clause reads a request's decision and answer only when they are resident (D.9.2).
  A settled request on another node may outlive a carried decision, and `step_Settled` already
  checked the settlement when it happened.
- `talk retract {entry}` joins D.4.12's restore list, because its target may be a carried decision
  that the retraction moves to `Retracted`.

**The `said` hold goes.** D.4.12 holds a confirmed `said`, and its entry metadata, while it is the
`answered_by` of a resident request, only so that Settled's state clause can read its kind and its
conversation key. That clause now reads an answer only when it is resident, so both rows of D.4.12's
table lose this hold. Without the change a closed conversation node would stay 8 days after its
request settled rather than 1 (the request's 7, then NODE_RETAIN).

**What leaves with the node, and comes back with it.** When the node leaves, so does every resident
entity homed at it (the finished ones, each before its own leaving time, and the carried decisions)
and the metadata of every people entry on it (`ix.people`). Each raises `left` or `people_left` as
D.4.12's leaving does. The node's departed row records them in `away`: each with the time it would
have left on its own (none for a carried decision), and the node's `people_left` before it left. A
restore of the node brings back those whose time lies after `now`, each keeping its recorded time,
and sets `people_left` to what D.4.12 would have made it: the larger of the recorded value and the
newest people entry that does not come back. So section 4's active decisions, sections 3 and 4's
finished items, their `≥k` totals, and the `moved` total are what they would have been had the node
stayed.

**What a free node lacks**, by construction:
- flags: every flag a closed node can carry comes from an entity that pins it or from its open
  intent (D.8.3), and `close_node` clears its recheck and assume marks (D.8.12);
- holds (H6);
- deadlines: every node-owned deadline is an open node's, or a pause's (D.4.8);
- a place among the candidates.

**What does not hold a node**:
- the two nodes of an open signal: the commands that resolve a signal name them, and search hits find
  their `disputed` mark through `ix.signals_by_b` (new) from either side (D.8.19);
- notes: `ix.pending_holder` and `ix.branch_notes` are keyed by id and never read the node;
- `owners` naming it: a departed node is closed, so the chain reads it as "anything else", exactly
  as for a closed one (D.8.12);
- the metadata of a non-people entry (approve, resolve, retract): O2 compares an entry with its node
  only when the node is resident;
- links, which may chain without end (the `continues` attempts of a research key, D.8.9);
- references that are only displayed (`moved_from`, a routing's node, a digest entry's node).

**The leaving time.**

```
leaving[Node(n)] := max(t, slot_floor(n)) + NODE_RETAIN
    t: the time of the event at which n became free: its close, the event that removed its last
       hold, its restore, or the `Pruned` that turned node leaving on (with its spread, below)
    slot_floor(n): the latest instant among the names n holds, its live name and its aliases, that
       lie under a node of role Series (open or closed) and have the slot form of
       forum_cron::slot_name ("YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ"); 0 if none
```

`evolve` sets the entry when a node becomes free, removes it when the node stops being free, and
keeps an existing time otherwise. T3 checks that `leaving` holds exactly the free resident nodes.

The **slot floor** keeps K3 in the one place where the server names a node without a command:
- **The problem.** `open_next_occurrence` names an occurrence after its slot, adding `-<id>` only
  when the name is live in memory (D.8.18). An earlier child or alias with that name, an occurrence
  dropped before its slot, an agent's node named like a slot, or an occurrence moved away (which
  leaves an alias behind), could have left meanwhile. The firing would then take a name a departed
  node holds, the writer would trip `st_names`' primary key, and the server would crash on every
  restart at the same firing.
- **The fix.** Every future slot lies after `now`, and with the floor a node holding a name or an
  alias under a series that reads as an instant leaves only after that instant. So no departed node
  holds the name of a slot still to come.
- **Plain nodes that become series.** An `update {repeat}` that makes a plain node a series is a
  write: the shell first restores the departed nodes holding a slot name or alias under it that lies
  after `now`, and `evolve` resyncs the resident ones.

**Why not "archived plus FINISHED_RETAIN".** Tying the leaving to the archive (closed for
`archive.after`, 7 days) and then FINISHED_RETAIN would keep a fortnight of closures resident: at
base 9.3 × 10⁶ nodes, 23 GB, by the per-call reading that G-6 drives, and 6 to 16 GB with typical
nodes even by the per-session one. Archiving is a list filter, not a memory rule (§5: it "only
affects the default of `view list`"), so WP-D8 leaves `archive.after` and AR untouched, and the shell
lists closed nodes that left memory from the state tables (below).

#### What stays in memory

Nothing of the departed node: no id in `names`, `aliases`, `keys_all`, or `children`, and no stub,
since stubs would grow at 10⁵ to 10⁶ a day. Its parent keeps counts of what left beneath it, so that
the rollups, `ready_to_close`, and L1's heights stay exact:

```rust
pub struct Node {
    // … D.4.3's fields, then, appended with #[serde(default)] so that an older row decodes (D.7.6):
    /// What has left memory below this node (D.4.13), in its hot row; None while nothing has.
    pub left_below: Option<Box<LeftBelow>>,
    /// Only on a departed node's row: what left memory with it (D.4.13); None while resident.
    pub away: Option<Box<Away>>,
}

/// The children of a node that have left memory, with all their descendants (which left before
/// them, rule 1).
pub struct LeftBelow {
    pub children: u32,
    /// Those children and their descendants by outcome; `open` and `flagged` stay 0, because a
    /// node leaves closed and unflagged.
    pub sub: Subtree,
    /// For each departed child, 1 + the height of its subtree, as a count per value, so that the
    /// height a move checks stays exact when one of them comes back.
    pub heights: BTreeMap<u32, u32>,
}

/// What left memory with a node: each entity, and each people entry's metadata, homed at it, with
/// the time it would have left on its own (None for a carried decision), and `people_left` before.
pub struct Away {
    pub items: Vec<(EntityRef, Option<Time>)>,
    pub people_left: Seq,
}
```

When `c` leaves, only its parent `p` changes:
- `p.left_below.children` rises by 1;
- `p.left_below.sub` adds `c`'s own outcome and `c.left_below.sub`;
- `p.left_below.heights[1 + h(c)]` rises by 1, with `h(c)` the largest key of
  `c.left_below.heights`, or 0.

A restore undoes exactly that, and `c`'s own `left_below` travels in its row. The ancestors' `ix.sub`
totals do not change at all, and `NodeMoved` needs nothing new, because `left_below` stays on the
node that moves.

The recount, and so R1:
- `ix.node[n].children` = the resident children + `left_below.children`;
- `ix.node[n].sub` = the resident descendants by state + the `left_below.sub` of `n` and of each
  resident node below it;
- a move's height = the largest, over the resident nodes `m` of the subtree, of `depth(m) − depth(n)
  + h(m)`;
- `AdminCmd::SetParams`' current-usage check of a lowered `tree.max_depth` reads `depth(m) + h(m)`
  over the resident nodes.

Four derived indices are new, each recounted from the resident state:
- `ix.merged_from` (into → the resident nodes merged into it);
- `ix.cited_ids` (a node id as an active decision's basis stores it → those decisions; `cited_by`
  files the same references by `resolve_merged`);
- `ix.alias_places` (an alias's target → its places, so that a departing node takes its aliases);
- `ix.signals_by_b` (the larger node of an open signal → the signal, so that `disputed` finds it
  from either side when the other node has left, D.8.19).

`ix.pinned` is the fifth (above). Every other index ranges over the resident nodes, as D.4.12 made
them range over the resident entities. An index keyed by a target loses a departing node's outgoing
references (its links leave `backlinks[target]`, its dependencies `dependents[target]`, its merge
`merged_from[into]`) and keeps the entries that resident sources hold for it: `backlinks[n]` stays,
because links do not hold; rules 4 and 5 leave no such entries in the others. A restore adds the
node's outgoing references back.

**How each reader stays right.** D.8 reads nodes in these places:

| Reader | After WP-D8 |
|---|---|
| Path resolution, `#id`, names, aliases (D.8.4) | Through the lookup (below): a write restores what it names, a read is served from the rows |
| A name a `create` or `move` takes, and missing ancestors | The shell restores the departed node holding any row, a name or an alias, at each target, so `NodeCreated` and `NodeMoved` see it and remove an alias in memory. Occurrences keep K3 by the slot floor, and a signal's name contains its own new id |
| K1, joins, K7, `conv_node` | `keys_open` holds open carriers, which are resident; `conv_node`'s case 1 walks ancestors, which are resident |
| `continues` at `create` (§7, D.8.9) | The shell adds each key's newest carrier from `st_keys` to the command, so `preds` is unchanged without a restore |
| `view find {key}`, the key hint (D.6.3) | The shell answers from `st_keys` |
| The rollups, `ready_to_close`, `list.under`, `view agreements`' `subtree_size` | The resident counts plus `left_below` |
| L1 (depth, a move's height, a lowered `tree.max_depth`) | The resident depths plus `left_below.heights` |
| `ix.next`, the flags, `flagged*`, `unheld_flagged*`, `attended_children`, `health`, `leave_better`, `who`, holders | Unchanged: a free node is unflagged, unheld, and no candidate |
| Waits and dependencies, T5's `reaches`, M1b (D.8.4, D.9.3) | By rule 4, which the `Restored` precondition enforces, every target of a resident node's edges is resident, so a walk from a resident node never leaves memory. A merge restores the departed dependents of `from` first, so N5 redirects them too |
| `merged_into`, `resolve_merged`, K5 | Rule 4 and the `Restored` precondition keep every chain from a resident node resident |
| `cited_by`, `stale`, `basis_changed` (D.8.17) | A based active decision pins its node (rule 2) and holds what it cites (rule 5), so every refresh and recount reads resident nodes |
| `backlinks` (D.8.25) | The core lists the resident incoming links and dependents; the shell renders those two lists from its tables `links_in` and `depends_in` (new), and `cited_by` from the core, whose active citers are all resident |
| The brief's `continues` walk (D.8.6) | One walk, as before, whose outgoing `continues` links come from a link source: memory for a resident node, the `Fact::Link` rows for a departed one; unsettled requests still come from `ix.items`, so a resident older carrier beyond a departed one keeps them |
| `view list` (D.8.25) | Below |
| `view agreements`, `hello.orientation` | Rule 7 keeps `ix.agreements` complete; a departed `under` has no agreements below it |
| The `owners` chain, persons, teams (D.8.12) | A departed owner is closed, so it is "anything else", as before |
| `occ_locked`, a series' occurrences | A departed series is closed, so its occurrences are unlocked, as before. Open occurrences are resident |
| Pauses, refusals, E1 | Rule 6 |
| Search hits' `disputed` (D.11.12) | `ix.signals_by_b` and the signal's key range, from either node |
| Paths, titles, and states of departed nodes in a response (the board, a digest entry, `moved_from`, a routing, search hits, backlinks, predecessors, owners, notes) | One helper, `Source::node_row(n)`, reads them from the content and hot rows, walking `place` upwards; every renderer goes through it, so none renders "unknown" or an empty path |

#### How a node comes back

**The lookup.** One resolver serves every place that names a node. It resolves in memory first; from
the first path step memory lacks, through `st_names` (a name or an alias row); and an id below
`next_node` that memory lacks, through its rows. Besides the restore plan and the reads below, it
serves two shell checks that run before `apply` (F4):
- `write.per_hour` (D.11.15): a node the lookup finds counts as existing, so the rate refusal applies
  whether the target is resident or not;
- `talk wait {for}` (D.11.11): its readiness check and its `since` take the node from the lookup, so
  a wait on a departed node parks, with the node's `seq` from its hot row.

**Writes.** In the writer job, after the pre-settle and before `apply`, the shell already restores
the entities a write names (D.8.1, D.4.12). It now also plans which departed nodes to restore, from
the lookup and `S.nodes`:
1. **Every node the write names.** `at`, `on`, `path`, `target`, `to`, `under`, `for`, `scope`,
   `from`, `into`, `depends_on`, `owners`, `waits_for: {node}`, a basis node reference, and
   `holder:` and `holders:` addressees.
2. **Whatever holds a target's name.** For `create` and `move`, at each `(parent, name)` the command
   takes, missing ancestors included, the departed node holding a row there, a name or an alias.
3. **A merge's dependents.** The departed dependents of `from`, from `depends_in`.
4. **Slot names.** For an `update {repeat}` that makes a plain node a series, the departed nodes
   holding a name or an alias under it whose slot lies after `now`.
5. **Nodes the shell adds.** The node of `hide {entry}`, of `retract {entry}`, and of `talk
   answer`'s question (D.5.2).
6. **Homes.** The home of every entity restored, and the node of its metadata.

**The closure.** Then, until nothing changes, it adds each planned node's departed parent (from its
content row's `place`), its departed `merged_into` (hot row), and its departed `depends_on` targets
(content row). Restoring the targets keeps rule 4, and with it T5 and K5, over the resident state.
For example, `A` and `B` departed with `A → B` and `B → X`; a restore of `A` alone, followed by
the edge `X → A`, would close a cycle that a walk stopping at departed `B` cannot see. Last, it adds
the `away` items of every planned node whose time lies after `now` or that have none.

**The newest carrier needs no restore.** For a `create` whose key no open node carries, the shell
adds to the command each such key's newest carrier, the largest id in `st_keys`, as it adds `node`
and `asker` to `talk answer` (D.5.2); `decide` takes the larger of it and the last of
`ix.keys_all[k]` (D.8.9). `NodeCreated` has no precondition on link targets (D.7.4), so `continues`
is unchanged and yesterday's attempt stays where it is.

**The event.** The planned nodes go first, parents before children, then the entities, in one
`Restored` event, in the restore transaction D.4.12 already has:

```rust
pub enum EntityRef { /* D.4.12's variants */, Node(NodeId) }               // appended (D.7.6)
pub enum Restored { /* D.4.12's variants */, Node(NodeId, Box<NodeRow>) }  // appended

/// A node as its state rows hold it (D.11.6): the node with its keys, links, `left_below`, and
/// `away`, the aliases that name it, and the approvals of its versions.
pub struct NodeRow { pub node: Node, pub aliases: Vec<(NodeId, Name)>,
                     pub approvals: Vec<(Version, u32)> }
```

`restore_tracked` drops a node item that is resident or not below `next_node`, as it drops entities
(D.6.1). The node's `approvals` (`State::approvals`, keyed by node) leave and return with it. The
precondition of a node item (D.7.4) is: absent; below `next_node`; its parent, its `depends_on`
targets, and its `merged_into` resident or earlier in the same event; its live name and its aliases
free. An entity item's home must be resident or earlier in the event. So rule 4 is a property of the
core, and a plan that misses a target is an anomaly, which every test and debug build catches (F7).
An entity item listed in its home's `away` keeps the time recorded there; the arm then clears the
node's `away`.

**Cost.** A restore reads, per node, its content row, its hot row, its keys (by the new index
`st_keys(node)`), its alias rows (`st_names(node) WHERE alias = 1`), its link and approval rows (by
key prefix in `st_facts`), and the rows of its `away` items. A departure writes the same rows. So a
departure is bounded by the node's keys, links, aliases, approvals, and the entities that leave with
it. A restore is bounded by the same for every node of its closure: the node's departed ancestors,
its departed `depends_on` and `merged_into` closures (a pipeline of 1,000 departed steps restores all
1,000 when its last step is written to), and, for a merge, the departed dependents of `from`, which
the merge's `DependsRedirected` events already cost. An intake node with 10⁵ `user:` keys costs 10⁵
rows to leave and to come back, but such a node is rarely closed.

**Reads never restore** (`Cmd::is_read`: the views, `hold check`, `talk who`, `talk wait`, `hello`,
and the read controls). Restoring for a read would write an event with the node's whole text and
keep the node resident another day for every look at an old result; CS-14's "a re-read appends
nothing" would no longer hold. Instead:
- **The core.** The shell hands a departed node that a read names to the core as
  `NodeRef::Departed { id, seq }`, an appended variant that no tool call decodes to (the shell adds
  it, as it adds `since` to `talk wait`, D.5.2). `apply::target` resolves it to `id` for a read
  when `id < next_node`, and refuses it for a write (`invalid(BadParams)`: a shell bug). `Shown`'s
  precondition becomes "the session exists and the node is below `next_node`", and `show` takes the
  `seq` of the reference.
- **`view node`.** `query::brief` takes, for a node that is not resident, its row and the rows of
  its `away` items whose time lies after `now`, and files them into a `NodeItems` with the same
  function that files `ix.items`. Flags, holders, and open items are then empty, as for any free
  node; the rollup comes from `left_below`; the inherited agreements from the nearest resident
  ancestor upwards (departed ancestors have none, rule 7); the `continues` walk from the link
  source; and the totals from `left`. One brief function serves both cases.
- **`view feed`, `view history`, `hold check`, `talk who`, `view agreements`, and `talk wait`** need
  nothing more: a departed node has no holds, attended children, agreements below it, or news, and
  the feed and the history are the shell's tables.

**`view list`** (D.8.25). The walk visits departed nodes too, in the same order as before (by id
without `under`; children by id under it), each counted against SCAN_MAX, so the page and its total
equal a run where nothing leaves. A resident node's fields and flags come from the core. A departed
node is closed and unflagged, so a filter with `closed: false` or `flags` needs only its id, and any
other filter its list fields from its rows. The writer reads the departed part through a bounded
cache (LIST_CACHE, 64 MiB): each departed node's list fields, each parent's departed children, and
the departed ids of each block of 4,096 ids, filled from the rows on a miss. A departed node cannot
change while it is away, so the writer keeps the cache exact by updating the entries a departure or
a restore concerns as it persists them. A list that visits the same departed nodes as an earlier
one, as the default list without `under` does, reads no row.

#### Events, evolve, recount, checks, startup, and replay

**No event for leaving, one for pruning.** Leaving is a pure function of the state and the times
of later events (the prune in step 1 of `evolve`), monotone in `at`, so it commutes with T2 and a
history replays it exactly. A `NodeLeft` event, or a `Leave` deadline kind, would add 10⁵ to 10⁶
events a day that carry nothing the state does not already determine, and deadlines exist to apply
§25 transitions (D.0.2, principle 3). But a prune that waits for the next event leaves two gaps:
- **The plan sees a due node as resident** (F1). If no deadline is due, the pre-settle emits nothing,
  so a node whose leaving time lies in `(last_now, now]` is still in memory: the plan does not
  restore it, and the command's first event prunes it under `apply`. On an idle personal forum the
  first call of the morning hits this; D.4.12's entities had the same hole until WP-D6, whose plan
  treats a resident entity whose leaving time has come as departed (`leaving_due`, D.4.12).
- **A long stop** (F17). The first event after it carries every departure that fell due since the
  last deadline: up to 10⁵ to 10⁶ a day of downtime in one transaction, every departed value held
  in `Tracked::departed` until it is written.

So `settle` (D.8.2) emits `Pruned`, an appended event with no base change but the gate below; its
step 1 does the pruning, as every event's does:

```
settle(s, now, max):                                // D.8.2, with D.4.13's prunes
    now := max(now, s.last_now)
    fired := 0
    if not s.nodes_leave: emit Pruned at s.last_now // the gate, once per forum
    while fired < max:
        k := s.ix.deadlines.first()
        b := k.at if k is Some and k.at <= now, else now
        if more than PRUNE_CHUNK (10,000) leaving times are <= b:
            emit Pruned at the PRUNE_CHUNK-th of them; fired += 1; continue
        if k is None or k.at > now:
            if a leaving time is <= now: emit Pruned at now
```
