```rust
    /// A principal key used for the first time (CS-1). `id = next_principal`.
    PrincipalSeen { id: PrincipalId, key: PrincipalKey },
    /// At most once per `presence.resolution`, unless the session was silent or the command
    /// issues a hold (CS-14, CS-8). `retire_at = max(old, at + session.retain)`.
    Touched { session: SessionId, silence_at: Time, retire_at: Time },
    /// The session leaves the state at its Retire deadline, holding nothing (CS-8).
    SessionRetired { session: SessionId },
    SessionStatus { session: SessionId, text: Text },
    InboxRead { session: SessionId, notes: BTreeSet<NoteId> },
    /// Only when `seq` raises the session's `shown[node]` (CS-14).
    Shown { session: SessionId, node: NodeId, seq: Seq },
    /// `open`: the call had no query, so the session asked for any work it can do; it records
    /// the session's caps as a profile of its class until `class_window_end` (CS-7).
    NextCalled { session: SessionId, outcome: NextOutcome, open: bool, class_window_end: Time },

    // ---- nodes (§4, §5, §12, §16)
    NodeCreated { id: NodeId, parent: NodeId, name: Name, origin: Origin, init: NodeInit },
    NodeUpdated { node: NodeId, patch: NodePatch },
    KeyAdded { node: NodeId, key: Key },
    KeyRemoved { node: NodeId, key: KeyStr },
    LinkAdded { node: NodeId, rel: LinkRel, to: NodeId },
    NodeMoved { node: NodeId, parent: NodeId, name: Name },
    NodeClosed { node: NodeId, outcome: Outcome, merged_into: Option<NodeId>,
                 by: Option<SessionId> },                         // 1.11: the closer, serde default
    NodeReopened { node: NodeId },
    OfferSet { node: NodeId, on: bool },
    WaitSet { node: NodeId, wait: Option<WaitOn> },
    DependsRedirected { node: NodeId, from: NodeId, to: Option<NodeId> },
    MarkSet { node: NodeId, mark: Mark, question: QuestionId, on: bool },
    IntentOpened { node: NodeId, intent: Intent },
    IntentClosed { node: NodeId, end: IntentEnd },
    IntentMoved { from: NodeId, to: NodeId },                    // merge (A-94)
    SeriesOutcome { series: NodeId, missed: bool },
    OccurrenceAvailable { node: NodeId },
    OccurrenceDetached { node: NodeId },                         // A-13, A-75
    SignalDetached { node: NodeId },                             // A-89

    // ---- holds (§10)
    /// `reopened` (1.4, R4): the outcome the node had when this take reopened it (the take's
    /// `NodeReopened` precedes it), None otherwise; stored as `Hold::reopened`.
    HoldIssued { token: Token, session: SessionId, lease_until: Time, terms: LeaseTerms, l: Dur,
                 reopened: Option<Outcome> },
    HoldExtended { token: Token, lease_until: Time, by: Extension },
    HoldEnded { token: Token, end: HoldEnd },

    // ---- feed (§6): one entry, and the entity its body creates
    Appended { eid: Eid, node: NodeId, seq: Seq, by: Author, body: EntryBody, text: EntryText },

    // ---- entity transitions (§25)
    RequestAnswered { request: RequestId, by: Eid },
    RequestSettled { request: RequestId, decision: DecisionId, answer: Eid },
    RequestMoved { request: RequestId, to: NodeId },
    PqRecheckAt { q: QuestionId, at: Time },
    PqRechecked { q: QuestionId, rechecks: u32, next: Time },
    PqExpired { q: QuestionId },
    PqEscalated { q: QuestionId, uq: QuestionId },
    PqAnswered { q: QuestionId, by: Eid },
    PqSuperseded { q: QuestionId, by: QuestionId },
    PqWithdrawn { q: QuestionId, by: Eid },                      // 1.12 (§9.3): a retract, while open
    PqAssumed { q: QuestionId, decision: DecisionId },
    PqMoved { q: QuestionId, to: NodeId },
    AqAnswered { q: QuestionId, by: Eid },
    UqAnswered { q: QuestionId, by: Eid },
    UqDefaulted { q: QuestionId },
    UqReaddressed { q: QuestionId, stage: u8, due: Time },      // pending(k) -> pending(k+1), CS-2
    UqLapsed { q: QuestionId },                                  // CS-2
    UqAssumed { q: QuestionId, decision: DecisionId },           // the lapse's assumption, CS-2
    CommitmentOpened { c: CommitmentId, node: NodeId, conv: KeyStr, followup_at: Time },
    CommitmentRefreshed { c: CommitmentId, followup_at: Time },
    CommitmentFulfilled { c: CommitmentId, by: SaidId },
    CommitmentMoved { c: CommitmentId, to: NodeId },
    SaidConfirmed { said: SaidId, via: ConfirmVia, link: Option<Text> },
    SaidUnconfirmed { said: SaidId },
    SaidWithheld { said: SaidId },                               // 1.9 (§9.2)
    SaidMoved { said: SaidId, to: NodeId },                      // merge (A-94)
    EntryRouted { entry: UserEntryId, routing: Routing, reason: Option<Text> },
    DecisionSuperseded { d: DecisionId, by: DecisionId },
    DecisionRetracted { d: DecisionId, by: Eid,
                        node: Option<NodeId> },                   // 1.11: the node keeps it, serde default
    ObjectionResolved { o: ObjectionId, by: Eid, upheld: bool },  // 1.8: upheld, serde default
    ObjectionMoved { o: ObjectionId, to: NodeId },               // merge (A-94)
    DigestShown { entry: DigestId, by: Eid },
    /// One session's `cannot` (CS-7): its entry in the class's record; `quorum` is used only when
    /// the record is new.
    Refused { node: NodeId, class: ClassName, session: SessionId, backoff_until: Time,
              expires_at: Time, quorum: u32 },
    /// The entries of the record with `expires_at <= at` expire; the record goes with its last.
    RefusalExpired { node: NodeId, class: ClassName },
    RefusalsCleared { node: NodeId, by: Eid },                   // A-56
    SignalOpened { key: SignalKey, node: NodeId },
    SignalResolved { key: SignalKey },
    Paused { scope: NodeId, until: Time, ttl: Dur, by: SessionId, class: ClassName,
             renewed: bool },                                    // `class`: shown (CS-9)
    Unpaused { scope: NodeId },
    PauseExpired { scope: NodeId },
    NoteBound { note: NoteId, session: SessionId },
    Hidden { target: HideTarget, reason: Text },
    /// `expires_at = at + op.retain`. The outcome stays in the history only: evolve stores the
    /// digest, the session, and the expiry (CS-8).
    OpRecorded { class: ClassName, op: OpId, digest: ReqDigest, session: SessionId,
                 expires_at: Time, outcome: Result<Done, Error> },

    // ---- memory (D-5)
    /// Entities that left memory, brought back because a command names them (D.4.12). The values
    /// are their state rows, read by the shell; evolve re-inserts them with their indices.
    Restored { items: Vec<Restored> },

    // ---- 1.8
    /// An objection upheld on a closed node corrects it (§5, §11.3): its outcome (`refuted` or
    /// `failed` for `done`, else unchanged) and `closure.upheld := Some(by)`; no counter (O2).
    NodeCorrected { node: NodeId, outcome: Outcome, by: Eid },
    // ---- 1.10
    /// A second, opposite verdict on the objection whose verdict marks a closed node withdraws its
    /// correction (§5, §11.3): `closure.outcome := outcome` (`corrected_from`), the mark and
    /// `corrected_from` cleared; no counter (O2).
    CorrectionWithdrawn { node: NodeId, outcome: Outcome },
}

/// What a `next` found (CS-31): a candidate; no candidate at all in the index (a true empty,
/// the idle share); or candidates that were all excluded for this caller (by its needs, horizon,
/// class refusals, query, or a pause), which is not idleness but work it cannot do.
pub enum NextOutcome { Item, Nothing, NothingForYou }
pub enum IntentEnd { Done { by: Eid }, ResolvedByClose }
pub enum Extension { Checkpoint, Renew }
/// §25: live -> released | expired | ended_by_close. The cause says which restructuring ended
/// it; `Move` reuses ended_by_close for §16's "later writes become late" (A-6).
pub enum HoldEnd { Released, Expired, EndedByClose(EndCause) }
pub enum EndCause { Close, Merge, Move }
pub enum ConfirmVia { Explicit, Release, Close,
                      Recorded }                          // 1.11: its session held nothing (§9.2)
pub enum HideTarget { Entry(Eid), File { node: NodeId, name: Text } }

/// Everything a new node starts with. `due_fired` is computed by evolve (due <= at). `files`
/// starts empty (A-97).
pub struct NodeInit {
    pub title: Text,
    pub body: Text,
    pub fields: BTreeMap<Text, Text>,
    pub status: Text,
    pub digest: Text,
    pub agreements: Text,
    pub kind: Option<Label>,
    pub tags: BTreeSet<Label>,
    pub capacity: u32,
    pub priority: i32,
    pub est: Option<u32>,
    pub needs: BTreeSet<Label>,
    pub due: Option<Time>,
    pub depends_on: BTreeSet<NodeId>,
    pub owners: BTreeSet<NodeId>,
    pub keys: BTreeMap<KeyStr, NormVer>,
    pub links: BTreeSet<(LinkRel, NodeId)>,
    pub role: Role,
}

/// The fields an update changes, resolved. decide includes a field only if its value differs
/// (O2; for `repeat`, A-75's comparison); evolve counts an anomaly for a field equal to the current
/// value. `Change::Keep` is "absent" (D.2). `tags` and `needs` are the resulting sets, computed
/// by decide from the patch's additions and removals on the current sets (CS-34): the single
/// writer applies one command at a time, so the stored set is exact, and replay never recomputes it.
pub struct NodePatch {
    pub title: Option<Text>,
    pub body: Option<Text>,
    pub fields: Option<BTreeMap<Text, Text>>,
    pub files: Option<BTreeMap<Text, Text>>,
    pub status: Option<Text>,
    pub digest: Option<Text>,
    pub agreements: Option<Text>,
    pub kind: Change<Label>,
    pub tags: Option<BTreeSet<Label>>,
    pub capacity: Option<u32>,
    pub priority: Option<i32>,
    pub est: Change<u32>,
    pub needs: Option<BTreeSet<Label>>,
    pub due: Change<Time>,
    pub depends_on: Option<BTreeSet<NodeId>>,
    pub owners: Option<BTreeSet<NodeId>>,
    pub repeat: Change<Repeat>,
}
```

### D.7.3 Entry bodies and texts

```rust
pub enum EntryBody {
    /// A plain note (`to: None`), or an addressed message, `talk say` (§13, A-17).
    /// `recipients` and `pending_holder` are fixed by decide when the note is recorded (A-49);
    /// a `principal:` or `holders:` note has none, its readers being found when they read (CS-3, D-6).
    Note { to: Option<Addressee>, until: Option<Time>, recipients: BTreeSet<SessionId>,
           pending_holder: bool, expects: Option<Expects>, reply_to: Option<Eid> },
    /// `requester` is `User(p)` with `p` the entry's principal when `from_user` is set, else
    /// `External` (the requester's name is then text, `TextField::Requester`) (CS-4). `origin` is
    /// the message, `conv` the conversation key the node was found by (`where`, or the origin
    /// without one; for a routed user entry its `user:e<n>` key), which C1's step check reads
    /// (A-61, D.9.2) and `evolve` stores as `Request::conv`, so that a `said` answers only its own
    /// conversation's requests (§9.4, 1.3).
    Request { origin: Key, conv: KeyStr, from_user: Option<UserEntryId>, requester: Requester },
    Question(QuestionBody),
    /// `talk answer` to an agent question; delivered to the asking session.
    Answer { question: QuestionId, recipient: SessionId, until: Time },
    /// `basis`: the validated references (CS-22); empty for every decision the server or a close
    /// records. The `what` of each external reference is a `TextField::Basis` text, in order.
    Decision { settles: BTreeSet<RequestId>, supersedes: Option<DecisionId>,
               assumes: BTreeSet<QuestionId>, evidence: Option<Evidence>,
               basis: Vec<BasisRef> },
    /// `hold checkpoint`, and the record of `hold release` (which counts as a checkpoint, A-9).
    Checkpoint { token: Token, release: Option<ReleaseReason>,
                 pr_named: Option<bool>,             // 1.12: an intent_done naming a PR; serde default
                 handed_off_until: Option<Time> },   // 1.12: a handoff's keeping; serde default
    Said { conv: KeyStr, kind: SaidKind, corrects: Option<SaidId>,
           voice: bool },                                         // 1.11: the voice by its cap, serde default
    Heard { conv: KeyStr, answers: Option<QuestionId> },
    FromUser { principal: PrincipalId },                       // whose words (CS-1)
    ToUser { kind: ToUserKind, verbatim: bool, re: BTreeSet<Eid>,
             principal: PrincipalId },                         // to whom (CS-4)
    Approve { version: Version },
    Object,
    Resolve { objection: ObjectionId, upheld: bool,            // 1.8: upheld, serde default
              deferred: bool },                                // 1.11: a deferral, serde default
    Retract { target: RetractTarget },
    System(SystemNote),
    /// A write made with a stale token (H4), with exactly what was attempted. The command lives
    /// in the event and the log only; evolve stores nothing of it in the state.
    Late { token: Token, attempted: Box<Cmd> },
    /// 1.8 (§10.2): `hold check {intent_done}`, by the entry's author, without a hold; its text is
    /// the `intent_done`. Type `checkpoint`; `keeps_meta` is false; it counts for no counter.
    IntentChecked { intent: Eid, pr_named: bool },  // 1.12: its text names a PR; serde default
}

pub enum QuestionBody {
    People { conv: KeyStr, blocking: bool, said: SaidId, supersedes: Option<QuestionId>,
             recheck_at: Time },
    Agent { to: Addressee, until: Time, recipients: BTreeSet<SessionId>, pending_holder: bool },
    /// Stage 0 of the chain `to`, due at `due` (CS-2, D.8.12).
    User { source: UqSource, about: Option<NodeId>, to: Vec<PrincipalId>, due: Time,
           has_default: bool },
}

/// What a `retract` strikes out: the type of a basis target, so a retraction is looked up in
/// `ix.cited_by` and stored in `State::retracted` as it is (D-4).
pub type RetractTarget = BasisTarget;

pub enum SystemNote {
    /// On USER_DIGEST: creates a digest entry for one audience principal (CS-5).
    Digest { item: DigestItem, to: PrincipalId },
    Closed { outcome: Outcome },                 // text: summary, verified, learnings
    Reopened,                                    // text: the reason
    KeysDropped { keys: Vec<(KeyStr, NodeId)> }, // K7: keys another open node carries
    MergedFrom { from: NodeId, last_checkpoint: Option<Eid> },   // text: from's digest (§16)
    Moved { from: Place },
    Renewed { token: Token },                    // text: the why
    ScheduleEnded,                               // a series with no further slot (A-51)
    Paused { until: Time },                      // text: the reason
    Unpaused,
    PauseExpired,
    Hidden(HideTarget),                          // text: the reason
    Defaulted { question: QuestionId },          // the default became the answer; rendered
                                                 // from the question's own entry
}

/// The free text of an entry. The core never stores it; the history records it once, in this
/// event, and the shell renders and indexes it from there (D.11.6, D.11.12).
pub struct EntryText { pub main: Text, pub extra: Vec<(TextField, Text)> }
pub enum TextField {
    Done, NextStep, Intent, IntentDone, File, Option, Recommendation, Default, Client, From,
    Requester, Summary, Verified, Learnings, Reason, Checked, Basis, Link, What, Why,
}
```

### D.7.4 What `evolve` does with each event

`evolve(s, e)`:
1. `s.last_now := max(s.last_now, e.at)`; `s.counters.events += 1` (saturating). Then the expiry
   prune: the `op_id` records with `expires_at <= e.at` and the notes with `until <= e.at` leave the
   state, popped from the front of `ix.ops_expiry` and `ix.notes_until`, with their entries in
   `ix.inbox`, `ix.pending_holder`, `ix.branch_notes`, and `ix.user_notes`, and with an agent
   question's `AQuestion` (CS-8, CS-17, D.4.12); and the entities whose `leaving` time is at or
   before `e.at` leave memory, popped from `ix.leaving_by_time` (D.4.12), a digest entry that is
   still pending being counted in `digest_left[to]`. It costs O(what left), and nothing when nothing
   did. Like the statistics prune
   it is monotone in `at`, so it commutes with T2: on every path the stored records, notes, and
   entities are exactly those whose end lies after `last_now`.
2. Checks the event's precondition (column 2). If it fails: `s.anomalies += 1`, and the base change is
   skipped, except that any id the event carries still advances its counter to `max(counter, id + 1)`.
3. Applies the base change (column 3).
4. Refreshes the derived indices for the objects the event touched:
   - **Deadline sync.** For each owner in column 4, recompute `deadline_of` and move, insert, or
     remove its key in `ix.deadlines` and `ix.deadline_at`.
   - **Basis refresh** (D-4). For each basis target the event changed (the node of `NodeClosed` and
     `NodeReopened`, the decision of `DecisionSuperseded` and `DecisionRetracted`, the target of an
     `Appended(Retract)`), recompute `stale` (D.8.17) for each decision in `ix.cited_by[t]`, set its
     membership in `ix.items[its node].stale_basis`, and add its node to the nodes refreshed below.
     It costs O(the target's direct citers × their references), one transaction even for a hub
     with 10⁴ citers (review RS-11).
   - **Flag and candidate refresh.** For each node in column 5, and each node the basis refresh
     added, in ascending id order: recompute
     `flags(s, n, e.at)` (D.8.3), update `ix.flagged`, the parent's `flagged_children`, for an
     occurrence its series' `flagged_occurrences`, and, when
     the flags turned empty or non-empty, `sub.flagged` of every ancestor (CS-32);
     then recompute the node's candidate classification (D.8.5) and update `ix.next` (CS-16), with
     `ix.next.waiting` (1.4: the node is in it while only an unresolved wait keeps it from being a
     `Cand::Node`): an
     entry that appears gets `s.since[c] := e.at` and goes into its partition, or into `held` when
     a `depends_on` target is open or a pause covers the node; one whose key, partition, or held
     state changed moves; one that disappears leaves `ix.next` and `s.since`. For a `Cand::Node(n)`
     that appears with `n ∉ stats.demand_counted`, it adds the node's estimate to
     `stats.days[day(at)].demand_min` and inserts `n` into `demand_counted`, so a node handed off
     five times is counted once (A-41);
     then, from the flags, the classification, and `ix.node[n].live`: `ix.flagged_active` (flagged,
     and a candidate or held by a live hold of its own, CS-31; when it changed,
     `stats.days[day(at)].flagged_end := |ix.flagged_active|`), and `n`'s membership in its parent's
     `unheld_flagged_children` and in `unheld_flagged_by_part` (D.8.7). A hold event refreshes its
     own node too, so `live` and these sets agree.
   - The structural indices of the event's own objects (`children`, `attended_children`,
     `keys_open`, `keys_all`, `origins`, `people`, `items` with its open subsets and
     `requesters_by_age`, `settling`, `waiters`, `dependents`, `backlinks`, `cited_by`,
     `marked_by_question`, `holds_by_session`, `open_saids_by`, `unrouted_by`, `refused`,
     `live_sessions`,
     `live_by_class`, `ops_expiry`, `notes_until`, `leaving_by_time`, `inbox`, `pending_holder`,
     `branch_notes`, `user_notes`, `principal_key`, `person_of`, `aliases_of`, `unrouted`,
     `requests_by`, `unsettled_by`, `pending_uq_by`, `refusal_question`, `pending_digest_by`,
     `series_open`, `agreements` (1.4), `profiles_by_time`, `class_ends`, the needs trie of
     `ix.next`, and the rollups of `NodeIx`, the subtree's `sub` on each ancestor included, CS-32)
     are updated by the same arm.
   - **Leaving** (D.4.12). When the event finishes an entity, or removes the last reference that
     held a finished one back, `leaving[x] := e.at + FINISHED_RETAIN` (and `ix.leaving_by_time`); a
     new digest entry gets `e.at + DIGEST_RETAIN` while it is pending; when a new reference holds an
     entity back again, it leaves `leaving`.
   - `evolve_tracked` adds to its `Tracked::facts` every fact (D.6.1) that steps 1 and 3 and the
     history changes of step 4 (`stats`, `since`, `user_msgs`, `leaving`, `digest_left`) touched;
     the indices are not facts. A fact that left memory is dirty too, and its entity's value
     before it left goes into `Tracked::departed`: the shell writes that value to its row, marked
     not resident (D.11.6).

"Ancestors" below means the chain from the node's parent to ROOT, at most `tree.max_depth` steps.
"Locked occurrences of `n`" means `ix.flagged_occurrences[n]`, the flagged occurrences of `n`
wherever they are in the tree: the only nodes whose classification depends on `n` being an open
series (`occ_locked`, D.4.3). An occurrence moved out of its series is no longer among its
children, so `ix.flagged_children[n]` would miss it (WP-D6). Only flagged closed occurrences can be
candidates, so refreshing the flagged ones is enough, and the cost stays bounded by the series'
flagged occurrences (§18).

| Event | Precondition | Base change | Deadline owners | Nodes refreshed (besides the event's own node) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Genesis` | `counters.events = 0` | params; the eight reserved nodes (origin `Reserved`, open, capacity 0, title = name, version 1, digest_version 1, content_version 1, no owners); names; `principal_ids["user"] := USER_PRINCIPAL`, `next_principal := 1` (CS-1) | — | all eight |
| `ParamsChanged` | — | params (existing deadlines keep their stored times); 1.8: every open node's `stale_fired := touched_at + offer.stale <= at` | `Node(n)` of every node (1.8: Stale) | every node (`too_big` and `stale` read a parameter) |

What `Appended` creates, by body:

| Body | Entity created or changed | Owner | Nodes refreshed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Note { to: Some(_) }` | a `Note` (`until` defaults to `at + deliver.window` in decide); `ix.notes_until`, so the note leaves at the first event at or after its `until` (CS-17); for `to: Principal(p)`, `ix.user_notes[p]`; for `to: Holders(a)`, `ix.branch_notes[a]` (D-6) | — | — |
| `Note { to: None }` | none | — | — |
| `Request` | a `Request` on the node, with the body's `requester`; `ix.unsettled_requests`; for `User(p)`, `ix.requests_by[p]` and `ix.unsettled_by[p]` | — | the node |
| `Question(People)` | a `PQuestion` (`Open`, `rechecks = 0`, `recheck_at` from the body, A-24) | `Entry(eid)` | the node |
| `Question(Agent)` | an `AQuestion` (`asker` = the author) and its `Note` | — | — |
| `Question(User)` | a `UQuestion` (`Pending`, `stage = 0`, the body's chain `to`, `assumed_by = None`); `ix.items[about].uquestions`; `pending_uq_by[to[0]]` | `Entry(eid)`, always (CS-2) | — |
| `Answer` | a `Note` addressed to `recipient` | — | — |
| `Decision` | a `Decision` (`Active`, with the body's `basis`); `ix.settling[r]` for each `r` it settles; `ix.cited_by[t]` for the target `t` of each node and entry reference (CS-22); its node's `stale_basis` if a reference is already stale (D-4) | — | the node |
| `Retract { target }` | `target` into `State::retracted` (D-4); a decision's own transition is the `DecisionRetracted` that follows | — | the citers of `target` (basis refresh) |
| `Checkpoint` | `checkpoints += 1`, `attempts := 0`, `last_checkpoint := eid`, `expired_hold := None` (1.4: a release's checkpoint too); the token's hold, if present, `checkpointed := true`; 1.12: with `pr_named: Some(b)`, which the command sets when the entry carries an `intent_done`, `pr_named := b`; with `handed_off_until: Some(t)`, which a `handoff` release sets to `at + hold.terms.first`, by a session `x`, `sessions[x].handed_off := {token, t}`; a log written before 1.12 carries neither, and replays to the tables it wrote (D.7.6) | — | the node |
| `IntentChecked` (1.12) | the node's `pr_named :=` the entry's `pr_named`, a flag the `hold check` sets from its `intent_done`, so that a log written before 1.12 replays to its tables (D.7.6) | — | — |
| `Said` | a `Said` (`Pending`) | — | the node |
| `FromUser { principal: p }` (`p` interned; `ToUser`'s principal likewise; both stored in `EntryMeta::principal`) | a `UserEntry` (`Unrouted`, `principal = p`, `at`); `State::user_msgs[p]` gains `at` and drops its times before `at − user_gap.window` (history, D.4.2); the author session's `principals += p` (CS-1) | — | USER |
| `ToUser { principal: p }` | the author session's `told += p` (1.4, rule 12, R13); a `to_user` binds no principal (D.8.11) | — | — |
| `Approve` | `approvals[(node, version)] += 1` | — | — |
| `Object` | an `Objection` (`Open`) | — | the node |
| `Resolve { deferred: true }` (1.11) | the objection's `deferred := Some(eid)` while it is `Open`; nothing otherwise | — | — |
| `System(Digest { item, to })` | a `DigestEntry` (`Pending`, `to`); `pending_digest_by[to]` | — | — |
| every other body | none | — | — |

**Touches** (1.8, §5, D.4.3). Besides the base changes above, the arms of `NodeCreated`,
`NodeReopened`, `NodeUpdated`, `KeyAdded`, `KeyRemoved`, `LinkAdded`, `Appended` (any body but
`Late`), and `Fired{Wait}` touch their node while `params.offer_stale` is set: `touched_at := at`,
`stale_fired := false`, the hot row dirty, and the owner `Node(n)` synced, which moves its Stale key
to `at + offer.stale`. An `Appended(IntentChecked)` changes nothing else but, 1.12, the node's
`pr_named :=` the entry's `pr_named`: the `IntentClosed` that follows it closes the intent, as
after a checkpoint (D.8.10).

### D.7.5 Totality

`evolve` has no error path:
- An event whose precondition fails (a missing referent, a transition from a state that §25 does not
  allow, an id that is not the counter's next value, a `seq` or `fence` that is not current + 1)
  increments `anomalies` and skips the base change; counters still advance to cover any id the event
  carries. `apply` and `settle` never produce such an event; `check_invariants` reports any anomaly,
  in debug builds, at a checked startup, and in the history-replay tests (D.9.1), so a buggy version
  is detected instead of silently diverging.
- Arithmetic saturates; there is no indexing, `unwrap`, or `panic!` (D.1.3).
- Inserting an existing key overwrites; removing a missing key does nothing.
- Every loop is over a finite collection or a bounded ancestor walk (at most `tree.max_depth` steps,
  and at most `nodes.len()` steps, so it terminates even on a corrupted cyclic parent chain).

Kani harnesses check "no panic, no overflow" for every `Ev` variant on a small arbitrary state
(D.12.5).

### D.7.6 Encoding and evolution of the event schema

Events are stored as canonical JSON (`serde_json`: struct fields in declaration order, enums
externally tagged, `BTreeMap` keys sorted, no floats), compressed with zstd, in the `events` table
with a `format` column, which is `1` in this release. `Event`, `Cmd`, `Done`, and `Error` use only
string-like map keys, which a round-trip property test checks; that test enumerates all three states
(`Keep`, `Clear`, `Set`) of every `Change<T>` field of `Patch` and `NodePatch`, because a two-level
`Option` would not survive the round trip (D.2). The rules for later releases:
- enum variants are only appended, never reordered or removed;
- struct fields are only appended, with `#[serde(default)]`;
- a change in `evolve` semantics that would change the replayed state of an existing log needs a new
  `format` value, a migration note in `docs/verification.md`, and an `evolve` that keeps accepting
  every older format. 1.8's touches avoid that: they are gated on `params.offer_stale`, which
  parameters recorded before 1.8 lack (`#[serde(default)]` reads it as `None`), so an older log
  replays through 1.8's `evolve` to the state it wrote, and the v1 fixture's replay test still holds
  (D.4.3). Its other additions are new variants (`NodeCorrected`, `IntentChecked`, the Stale kind)
  and fields with defaults that older logs never set (`upheld`). 1.10's do the same: a new variant,
  `CorrectionWithdrawn`, and `NodeCorrected`'s `was`, which sets `closure.corrected_from` and which
  a log written before 1.10 lacks, so its corrections replay with none, as its tables hold them;
  a checkpoint's `WaitSet { None }`, a `say`'s pending `holder:` note, and a non-holder's pending
  `said` are events that only a 1.10 log contains.
- 1.11: `NodeClosed`'s `by`, which sets `closure.by`, and `DecisionRetracted`'s `node`, which sets
  the node's `retracted_decision`, are appended with defaults, so a log written before 1.11 replays
  to the tables it wrote, with neither; `EntryBody::Said`'s `voice`, `EntryBody::Resolve`'s
  `deferred` (which marks `Objection::deferred`), `TalkCmd::Resolve`'s `defer`, and the variant
  `ConfirmVia::Recorded` likewise. A deferral's `Refused` and a verdict's `RefusalsCleared` on a
  closed node, and a `said`'s `SaidConfirmed { Recorded }` as it is recorded, are events that only
  a 1.11 log contains.
- 1.12: `Node::pr_named` and `Session::handed_off` are set from fields appended with defaults,
  `EntryBody::Checkpoint`'s `pr_named` and `handed_off_until`, `IntentChecked`'s `pr_named`, and
  `Intent`'s `pr_named` in `IntentOpened`, which the command computes from the texts and the hold.
  1.12 first derived both in `evolve`, from texts and releases that a 1.11 log holds too, so that
  replaying a 1.11 database (D.12.6, `forum-server replay`) gave flags its tables lacked; a state
  migration could not recompute them without the history, which D.7.6 rules out. With the fields,
  a log written before 1.12 replays to the tables it wrote, with neither flag, and a node or session
  of an upgraded database gains its flag at its next such entry; the store's test
  `a_history_written_before_1_12_replays_to_the_tables_it_wrote` rewrites a history in 1.11's JSON
  and replays it. `PqWithdrawn` is an event that only a 1.12 log contains.

**State rows** (FQ-2). The state tables (D.11.6) store each fact of D.6.1 as one row: its key as the
canonical JSON of the map key (a label set, as in `Fact::ClassProfile` and `Fact::Profile`, is a
sorted JSON array), and its value as the canonical JSON of the Rust value. A map inside a value whose
keys are neither strings nor integers is encoded as a list of pairs in key order
(`#[serde(with = "forum_core::serde_pairs")]`), which is canonical too. The same rules govern these rows: an appended field with `#[serde(default)]`, an
appended variant, or a new map decodes from an older row as it is.

**Upgrades are migrations of the state tables** (CS-28, review G-4). The genesis transaction records
the core's semantic version and `state_version` (1 in this release) in `meta`. Any change to a base
or history type that an older row does not decode into bumps `state_version` and comes with a
migration: a pure function over the stored rows, one per step, in
`forum-server/src/store/migrate.rs` (`v1_to_v2(fact, key, value) -> Vec<(Fact, key, value)>`), which
startup runs in one transaction before it loads the state (D.11.8), recording a history transaction
of kind `migrate` that names both versions. An upgrade therefore costs one pass over the state
tables, minutes at most at 10,000 agents (D.4.11), never a replay of the history, which would take 6
to 61 hours per year of history there (review §4). A migration may not need the history: a value
only the events determine would make the upgrade a replay, which a type change must therefore avoid.
Tests (D.12.6): a fixture database of every released `state_version` migrates, loads, and passes
`check_invariants`; and its history, replayed through the new `evolve`, equals the migrated tables,
which checks that the migration and the old formats' `evolve` agree.

The shell's tables (D.11.6) are versioned the same way, by `meta.shell_version`, with row-to-row
migrations in the same file, run in the same startup transaction; they never replay the history
either (D.11.8).

## D.8 Algorithms

### D.8.1 One call, end to end (T1, O1, sessions)

```
shell, per tool call (D.11.5):
  authenticate: bearer token -> class, and the token's default caps, if any (D.11.3), or HTTP 401
  parse the arguments' shape -> `invalid` on failure (answered by the shell; nothing is logged, no
      session opened, no stored op_id answer given: §21's precedence)
  mask secrets in every free text (D.11.13)
  if op_id given: digest := SHA-256(tool ‖ 0x00 ‖ canonical_json(masked arguments − {session,
      op_id})), masked with the masking version of the `st_ops` row of (class, op_id) if one
      exists, else the current one                                        // CS-35, D.11.5
  normalise keys (forum-keys), freeze tz tables (jiff), parse paths and times
  -> Cmd (an error here is `invalid`, answered by the shell, nothing logged)
  if cmd.longest_text() > text.max: answer `limit(TextTooLong)` (answered by the shell, nothing
      logged, no session opened; §21: it reaches nothing else; L1, A-114)
  search, for `hello`, `from_user`, `create`, and `view find {text}`: on a read-only connection to
      the search file, within SEARCH_BUDGET (D.11.12); the hits travel with the job, never in Cmd
  queue the job in its class's queue (D.11.2), or answer `limit(Busy)` (CS-29)
writer thread, a group of jobs at a time (D.11.2, CS-13):
  BEGIN IMMEDIATE
  for each job, until COMMIT_GROUP_MAX jobs or COMMIT_LINGER since the group's first:
    now := max(clock::now_ms(), S.last_now, max_now)            // T1, first clamp
    max_now := now                // in memory, not persisted: a call that appends nothing still
                                  // never sees time go backwards (A-101); after a restart the
                                  // floor is S.last_now
    pre-settle: (evs, st) := settle_tracked(&mut S, now, settle_batch, &mut dirty); persist evs,
                with the state rows of `dirty`, as a settle transaction; while st = More { COMMIT
                the group so far; BEGIN IMMEDIATE; settle the next batch }; st = Stuck(k): log k
                and abort the process (crash-only, D.8.2)
    if the command is a write, query::op_lookup(&S, class, op_id, now) finds nothing, and the
        session is over write.per_hour (D.11.15): if query::precheck(&S, &ctx, &cmd) finds no
        error, answer `limit(WritesPerHour)` (answered by the shell; nothing logged); if it finds
        one (a missing or foreign session, a missing target), go on: `apply` returns that error
        and appends nothing (§21's precedence: O1, the session, the target, then the rate limit,
        and only then a stale token, A-105)
    restore, unless op_lookup found a live record: for the ids the command names that are not
        resident but have a state row (D.4.12), restore_tracked(&mut S, now, the decoded rows,
        &mut dirty), persisted as a restore transaction
    (evs, out) := apply_tracked(&mut S, &Ctx { now, class, caps, session, op }, &cmd, &mut dirty)
    post-settle: the same settle, but a batch boundary does not COMMIT: every batch stays in the
        open transaction until the job's `st_ops` row is written (an `OpRecorded` never commits
        without its stored response, O1); if the settle ran past one batch, COMMIT the group right
        after that row (fires a deadline the command created at or before `now`)
    render the response from S, `out`, the job's search hits, and the next calls
        query::guide(&S, sess, now, &cmd, &out, &mut NoMeter), computed after the post-settle, on
        the settled state (T3; §20.9, D.8.26), with `sess` the call's session, opened by it if new,
        or None if the session check failed (D.11.7); for Reply::Replay read the stored response,
        next calls included, from the `st_ops` row instead
    if the job appended events: persist them, its `txs` row, the state rows of `dirty` (D.11.6),
        the shell's rows, and, with an op_id, the `st_ops` row with the rendered response
    // a job that appended nothing writes nothing (CS-14)
  COMMIT, if the group wrote anything
  reply to every job of the group; wake the `talk wait` sessions its events concern (D.11.11)
when every queue is empty and the first queued deadline is due: settle to now, as a group of its own
  (CS-30, D.11.2)
```

Every reply follows the commit that covers its job (§24: respond only after commit), including the
replies of jobs that wrote nothing, because they may have read what an earlier job of the group
wrote. Any storage error after `evolve` has run aborts the process before any reply of the group is
sent (crash-only); restart loads the state tables, which hold the last committed state (D.11.8), and
clients retry with their `op_id`. The in-memory state is never rolled back by hand.

`apply(s, ctx, cmd)`:

1. **Clock and text size.** `now := max(ctx.now, s.last_now)` (T1, second clamp: the core does not
   trust the shell). Debug builds assert that `s` is settled at `now`: no key in `ix.deadlines` has
   `at <= now`. Then, if `cmd.longest_text() > s.params.text_max`, return `([],
   Err(limit(TextTooLong)))`: nothing is applied, no session opens, and no `op_id` record is read
   or written (§21's precedence, L1, A-114). The shell has already answered such a call (above), so
   this is again the core not trusting the shell, and it makes L1's text half a property of the core
   that Kani checks (`limits_l1`, D.12.5).
2. **Retry (O1).** If `ctx.op = Some(op)` and `s.ops[(ctx.class, op.id)] = r` with `r.expires_at >
   now` (a record past its expiry that no event has dropped yet counts as absent, CS-8): if
   `r.digest == op.digest` and the call names no session or names `r.session` (`New` or
   `Existing(r.session)`), return `([], Ok(Done { reply: Replay, warnings: [], opened: None,
   stale_session: false }))`; otherwise return `([], Err(op_id_conflict))`. This happens before the
   session is resolved, so a retry after a reconnect cannot open a second session, and a repeat
   appends nothing (A-39). The key is `(class, op_id)` (§20.1), but a repeat that names another
   session of the class is a conflict (CS-8, review FS-5): in 1.1 it got the first call's response,
   bearer token included, and two agents then wrote under one fence. Only a first call (`New`) that
   reuses another agent's `op_id` with the same arguments still gets that response, which is why the
   schema asks for 96 random bits (D.11.5).
3. **Session.** `Existing(sid)`: the session must exist (`not_found(Session)`, which a retired
   session also gets, with the hint to open a new session, CS-8) and belong to `ctx.class`
   (`invalid(ClassMismatch)`); `stale := sessions[sid].silent`. `New`: the session is
   opened in step 5. `System`: the command must be `Cmd::Admin`, and the other two must not be
   (`invalid(BadParams)`, D.5.1); steps 5 and 6 then emit no `SessionOpened`, no `Touched`, and no
   `OpRecorded`.
4. **Validate.** `validate(s, sess, now, cmd) -> Result<Plan, Error>` is pure and reads only `s`. The
   order of checks is D.8.24's; each command section below refines it. `Plan` is internal
   (`pub(crate)`): one variant per command, holding the resolved ids, the chosen branch (create or
   join, the routing case, the candidate `next` picked), and the warnings computed on the pre-state,
   so that execution reads no unresolved reference.
5. **Execute.** An `Exec { s: &mut State, now, session, out: Vec<Event> }` emits events; `emit(ev)`
   pushes `Event { at: now, ev }` and immediately runs `evolve_mut`, so later steps read the updated
   state and the next free ids from `s.counters`.
   - If the session is new: `SessionOpened` first (with the `hello` arguments if the command is
     `session hello`, and its principal, D.5.1), preceded by `PrincipalSeen` when that principal's
     key is new (CS-1), whatever the validation result (A-38).
   - `Err(e)` with `e.code = StaleToken`: one `Appended(Late { token, attempted })` on the target node,
     carrying the attempted command (the shell renders it as the entry's text). No other event.
   - Any other `Err(e)`: no event. A failed call therefore records no `now` and does not make a
     silent session live (A-101).
   - `Ok(plan)`: `Touched { session, silence_at: now + presence.silence, retire_at:
     max(retire_at, now + session.retain) }` first, when the session is silent, or `now >= last_seen
     + presence.resolution`, or the command issues a hold (CS-14, CS-8; not after a fresh
     `SessionOpened`, and not under `System`); then the command's events (D.8.9 onwards).
6. **Record (O1).** If `ctx.op` is set and at least one event was emitted, emit `OpRecorded { class,
   op, digest, session, expires_at: now + op.retain, outcome }` last; `session` is the call's,
   opened by it if new. An error that emitted nothing is not recorded: it changed nothing, so the
   same `op_id` with any arguments is evaluated afresh later, and a different request with that
   `op_id` then executes rather than failing with `op_id_conflict` (the literal O1, A-106).
7. Return `(events, result)`.

`decide(s, ctx, cmd)` is `apply` on a clone. Execution never fails: every precondition it relies on
was checked in step 4, and every helper is total (it skips a missing referent rather than failing).

Settling is not part of the command. The pre-settle fires what time has made due; it would fire the
same events, in the same order, at the next call of any agent (T2). O1's "a repeat appends nothing"
therefore concerns the command's own events: a repeat's pre-settle may still append `Fired` events
and their effects, as any call's would (A-39).

**What O1 stores and compares** (A-39). The key is `(ClassName, OpId)` (§20.1). The comparison is the
32-byte `ReqDigest` and the session, computed by the shell over the masked arguments (D.11.5,
CS-35): O1 stays exact, because two requests with one digest are the same request up to masking,
after which the server could not tell them apart anyway, and SHA-256 makes a collision of two
different requests negligible. Stored, in the same transaction as the events: in the core,
`OpRecord { digest, session, expires_at }`; in the history, the `OpRecorded` event with the full
`Result<Done, Error>`; in the state table `st_ops`, the record with the rendered response bytes,
which a repeat returns verbatim, so an identical request gets the committed response back even if
the forum has changed since. The bytes include the next calls of the first execution (§20.1, §20.9):
the retrying agent never saw them, retries come within seconds, the next call that executes
recomputes them, and a stale item at worst meets an ordinary refusal whose own remedy recovers.
Recomputing them on a repeat would break O1's "returns the stored response" and the byte-identical
replay test (D.12.6) for advice nobody had read (NC-5, D.14.3). The next calls are not in `Done`
and not in `OpRecorded`: they are advice, outside `decide`'s outcome. They add at most about
2.3 KB to a stored response (three items, in the text and in `structuredContent`, D.11.7): at the
low, base, and high profiles' 56, 112, and 225 writes a second, each with an `op_id` (45 % of calls,
D.15.2), at most 11, 22, and 45 GB a day of `st_ops` bytes written, and as much deleted after
`op.retain`, so the table holds about a day of them and SQLite reuses the freed pages; G-8 measures
the file with the block rendered (D.12.8). A record lives for
`op.retain` (24 h, CS-8): retries come within a session's life, which is minutes and at most
`lease.ceiling` for a holder, and agents never return.
After that the same `op_id` executes afresh; the core's retry store is then bounded by a day of
calls (0.76 to 1.5 GB at 10,000 agents, where 1.1's grew by 0.9 to 1.9 TB a year, review TP-7).
Not stored: calls without an `op_id`, and errors that appended nothing (re-evaluating them is
harmless; a `full` may since have freed up; A-106).

### D.8.2 Settling and deadline firing (§17, T2, T4)

```
settle(s, now, max):
    now := max(now, s.last_now)
    fired := 0
    while fired < max:
        k := s.ix.deadlines.first()                 // minimum by (at, kind, owner)
        if k is None or k.at > now: return (events, Done)
        emit Fired { kind: k.kind, owner: k.owner } at k.at
        fire(s, k)                                  // the kind's effects, all at k.at
        if k is still in s.ix.deadlines: return (events, Stuck(k))
        fired += 1
    return (events, if s.ix.deadlines.first() is None or its at > now { Done } else { More })
```

A firing always removes its own key: its transition or marker makes `deadline_of` return `None`.
If a transition fails its `evolve` precondition (an anomaly, so a core bug, now reachable through
kinds whose transitions have preconditions, such as `SessionRetired` with a hold still present),
the key would stay the queue's minimum and be popped for ever; `settle` returns `Stuck(k)` instead,
and the shell aborts the process (crash-only), as it does for a violated database constraint.
`check_fire` reports the same in debug builds.

`fire(s, k)` per kind; every event carries `at = k.at` (§17: "each one fires with `now :=` its
deadline"):

| Kind | Owner | Effects after `Fired`, in order |
|---|---|---|
| Lease | `Hold(t)` | `HoldEnded { t, Expired }` (evolve: `offer` on, `attempts += 1` if the hold had no checkpoint); then, if `t.node` is an occurrence, `maybe_missed(t.node)` (D.8.18; a release and a move run it too, A-80) |
| Wait | `Node(n)` | none: `Fired` sets the marker and refreshes `n`, whose wait now resolves by predicate |
| Recheck | `Entry(q)` | `resolving :=` the nodes in `waiters[Question(q)]` whose wait is `Question { q, rechecks_at_set = q.rechecks }` (the waits this recheck resolves); `marked := resolving`, or `{q.node}` if `resolving` is empty and `q.node` is open, else `∅` (A-81); `k' := q.rechecks + 1`. If `k' < question.max_rechecks`: `PqRechecked { q, k', at + question.recheck }`, then `MarkSet { m, Recheck, q, on }` for each `m` in `marked`. Else if not blocking: `PqExpired { q }`, `add_digest(Assumption { q }, audience(Assumption { q }))` (D.8.13), then `MarkSet { m, Assume, q, on }` for each `m` in `marked`, or, if `marked` is empty (nobody waits and the conversation node is closed), `assume_now(q)` (D.8.17, A-104). Else (blocking): `uq := create_uq(Escalation { q }, about: q.node, false, None, None)` (D.8.12; no default, A-59), `PqEscalated { q, uq }`, and `WaitSet { w, Some(UserQuestion(uq)) }` for each `w` in `resolving`: the work cannot go on, so those nodes keep waiting, now for the user; no mark is set (A-93) |
| UserQuestion | `Entry(uq)` | With a default: `Appended(System(Defaulted { question: uq }))` on USER_DECISIONS (no text: the core holds none, and the shell renders the default from the question's own entry); `UqDefaulted { uq }`; then by source: `Agent` → `add_digest(DefaultApplied { uq }, audience(DefaultApplied { uq }))`; `Refusal { n }` → `refusal_default(n, uq)` (D.8.14). Without a default (every `Escalation` question, A-59, and agent questions asked without one), by stage (CS-2, D.8.12): if `uq.stage + 1 < uq.to.len()`, `UqReaddressed { uq, stage + 1, due: due_for(to[stage + 1], stage + 1, source, k.at) }`, and the question stays pending for its next addressee; otherwise `lapse(uq)` |
| Commitment | `Entry(c)` | none: `Fired` sets `followup_fired` and refreshes `c`'s node |
| OccurrenceSlot | `Node(o)` | `NodeUpdated { o, patch }` with the series' `title`, `body`, `needs`, and `est` that differ from the occurrence's, if any (1.4, §12, R10: the copy at availability, D.8.18); then `OccurrenceAvailable { o }` |
| OccurrenceWindow | `Node(o)` | `maybe_missed(o)` (`Fired` has set `window_fired`) |
| RefusalExpiry | `Refusal(n, c)` | `RefusalExpired { n, c }`: the entries that expired at `k.at` go; the owner's next key is the record's next expiry, if any (CS-7) |
| RefusalExpiry | `Class(c)` | `Fired` has removed the caps profiles whose window ended; then `e1_check(n)` for each `n` in `ix.refused`, ascending (D.8.14, CS-7) |
| Due | `Node(n)` | none: `Fired` sets `due_fired`; `overdue` turns on |
| Pause | `Node(p)` | `PauseExpired { p }`; `Appended(System(PauseExpired))` on `p` |
| Silence | `Session(s)` | `SaidUnconfirmed { x }` for each `Pending` `said` of `s` in `ix.open_saids_by[s]`, ascending (§9.2) |
| Retire | `Session(s)` | `SessionRetired { s }`: the session has been silent since its Silence deadline, and every hold it took ended before `retire_at` (D.8.23, CS-8) |

Settling also runs when the writer is idle (CS-30): with its queues empty, it settles to `now` as soon
as the first queued deadline is due, as a group of its own (D.11.2). By T2 that fires the same keys,
in the same order, with the same events, as the next call's pre-settle would; it contacts nobody, so
pull-only holds (§17 as clarified); it only moves the work off the first caller after a storm, which
was 0.2 to 0.75 s for 10,000 silences or 5,000 missed series (review TP-16, FS-17).

Properties:
- **Order.** `DeadlineKey`'s derived order is `(at, kind, owner)` with the kind order of §17
  (A-43 for the owner order).
- **Deadlines created while settling** enter the queue through `evolve` like any other and fire in the
  same loop if they are `<= now`. A firing at `k.at` creates deadlines only strictly after `k.at`:
  rechecks at `k.at + question.recheck`, user questions due, or re-addressed, at `k.at + d` with `d`
  at least `user_question.due_absent`, occurrence slots strictly after `max(slot, k.at)`; every
  duration is at least one second (`Params::valid`). `check_fire` asserts it.
- **Cancellation (T4).** A deadline is cancelled by changing its owner: `evolve` recomputes
  `deadline_of` for the touched owners and removes or moves the key. Because the queue always equals
  `recount_deadlines(s)` (checked), a key whose owner changed is not in the queue and cannot fire. A
  key fires at most once because firing makes its clause return `None` (a transition or a marker).
- **Idempotence.** If nothing is due, `settle` emits nothing (§17: "settling again changes nothing").
- **Path independence (T2).** `settle(S, t1)` then `settle(·, t2)` fires the same keys in the same
  order as `settle(S, t2)`. Two lemmas give it, by induction on the pops (they are the Verus
  obligation V-T2):
  - **L1.** `fire(s, k)` is a function of `(s, k)` only: every input is a field of `s` (including
    `s.params`, from which new deadlines such as the next recheck are computed) or `k.at`, never the
    settle target `t`. The predicates a firing evaluates read stored snapshots where a parameter
    could change between the deadline's creation and its firing (lease terms, `followup_at`, the
    window ends of a class's caps profiles in `active`, a refusal record's `quorum` and its
    entries' `expires_at` in `class_refused`, D.8.14).
  - **L2.** If `min(queue) <= t1 <= t2`, the next pop of `settle(·, t1)` equals the next pop of
    `settle(·, t2)`: both take the queue's minimum, and the queue order is total.

  When `settle(·, t1)` stops, the queue's minimum is above `t1`, and `settle(·, t2)` continues from
  the same state with the same pops. Settling does not record the `now` it was called with (only
  events do, A-101), so `last_now` ends at the same value on both paths. The statistics prune is
  monotone in `at`, so it commutes too. "A firing never adds a key at or before itself" is not needed
  for T2; it gives monotone event stamps (T1's step check) and is asserted by `check_fire`.
- **Batching.** `settle.batch` only splits the firings into transactions (D.8.1).

`check_fire(before, key, events, after)` (D.9) checks that `key` was the minimum of the queue, that
the events are exactly the table's, that `key` is gone from the queue afterwards, and that no new key
lies at or before `key.at`. State invariants are checked once a settle completes: between two firings
at the same instant the state is not yet settled (a hold whose lease ends at that instant is still in
the map until its own key fires), and §26 defines the invariants on settled states.

### D.8.3 Flags (§14, F)

Predicates over a settled state at `now`; every quantifier ranges over an open subset of the node's
`ix.items` (CS-20), so evaluating them costs O(open items on the node), whatever its history. Each
line equals 1.1's quantifier over every item, because a subset holds exactly the items in the state
the predicate asks for (R1 checks the subsets; `spec::flags` evaluates the quantifiers over every
entity, D.9.1).

```
attended(n)      := ix.node[n].subtree_live > 0      // a live hold on n or a descendant
held_self(n)     := ix.node[n].live > 0
waiting(n, now)  := n.wait = Some(w) ∧ ¬resolved(w, now)
resolved(w, now) := match w.on {
    Question { q, rechecks_at_set } => pq[q].state ≠ Open ∨ pq[q].rechecks > rechecks_at_set,
    UserQuestion(q)                 => uq[q].state ≠ Pending,
    Node(t)                         => closed(t),
    Time(T) | External(T)           => now ≥ T,
}
open_pq(n, k)    := items(n).open_pq[k] ≠ ∅          // an `Open` people question "to that person"
merged(n)        := n.life = Closed(c) ∧ c.merged_into ≠ None   // never a candidate (A-94)

unrouted(n)              := n = USER ∧ ix.unrouted ≠ ∅
unanswered_request(n)    := items(n).unsettled ≠ ∅
                            ∧ (closed(n) ∨ (¬attended(n) ∧ ¬waiting(n, now)))
open_commitment(n)       := ∃ c ∈ items(n).open_commitments:
                              closed(n) ∨ (¬attended(n) ∧ now ≥ c.followup_at
                                           ∧ ¬open_pq(n, c.conv))
unconfirmed_said(n)      := items(n).unconfirmed ≠ ∅ ∧ ¬attended(n)
open_intent(n)           := n.open_intent ≠ None ∧ ¬held_self(n) ∧ ¬waiting(n, now)
question_recheck(n)      := n.recheck_marks ≠ ∅
proceed_on_assumption(n) := n.assume_marks ≠ ∅
objection(n)             := items(n).open_objections ≠ ∅
basis_changed(n)         := items(n).stale_basis ≠ ∅ ∧ ¬merged(n)       // one hop (D-4, D.8.17)
too_big(n)               := open(n) ∧ n.attempts ≥ params.too_big_attempts
overdue(n)               := open(n) ∧ n.due = Some(d) ∧ now ≥ d      // occurrences: d = window_end
ready_to_close(n)        := open(n) ∧ n.origin ≠ Reserved ∧ n.fence > 0      // held once (1.6)
                            ∧ ix.node[n].children ≥ 1 ∧ ix.node[n].open_children = 0
missed(n)                := open(n) ∧ n.role = Series(x) ∧ x.last_missed
stale(n)                 := open(n) ∧ "offer" ∈ n.tags ∧ n.capacity > 0 ∧ ¬is_container(n)   // 1.8
                            ∧ ¬held_self(n) ∧ ¬waiting(n, now)
                            ∧ n.touched_at = Some(t) ∧ params.offer_stale = Some(d) ∧ now ≥ t + d

flags_of(s, n, now) -> FlagSet   // one bit per predicate above
```

`too_big` and `missed` hold on open nodes only (a Clarify of §14). Read literally, a node closed
after its third expired hold (a triage `drop`, or a merge as `superseded`, needs no checkpoint), or a
closed series whose last occurrence was missed, would carry the flag for ever; neither flag is in
`CLOSED_TAKE`, so `next` would never offer such a node, and it would stay in `ix.flagged`, its
parent's `flagged_children`, `sub.flagged`, and `flagged_active` for good. At 10,000 agents half of
all sessions vanish, so nodes reach three attempts daily: `FlagsPilingUp` would report growth that is
not work, `NoMover`'s population would grow with dead entries, and `leave_better` and `view list
{flags}` would scan them. With both flags open-only, every flag a closed node can carry is in
`CLOSED_TAKE`, except on a merged node, which nothing offers (A-94, A-96).

The predicates read times, not markers: `now ≥ T`, `now ≥ c.followup_at`, `now ≥ d`. The markers only
keep the deadline queue exact (D.4.8); on a settled state each marker equals its predicate, which T3
checks.

**Materialisation.** `evolve` recomputes `flags_of(s, n, e.at)` for every refreshed node (D.7.4) and
stores it in `ix.node[n].flags`. The refresh sets follow from each flag's inputs:

| Flag | Inputs | Events that change an input |
|---|---|---|
| `unrouted` | `ix.unrouted` | `Appended(FromUser)`, `EntryRouted` (both refresh USER) |
| `unanswered_request` | requests on n, life, attended, waiting | `Appended(Request)`, `RequestSettled`, `RequestMoved`, `NodeClosed`, `NodeReopened`, `HoldIssued`/`HoldEnded` on n or a descendant (ancestor chain), `NodeMoved` (both chains), `WaitSet`, wait resolution: `Pq*` and `Uq*` transitions through `waiters`, a target's `NodeClosed`/`NodeReopened` through `waiters`, `Fired(Wait)` |
| `open_commitment` | commitments on n, life, attended, `followup_at` vs now, open people questions on n | `CommitmentOpened`, `CommitmentRefreshed`, `CommitmentFulfilled`, `CommitmentMoved`, `Fired(Commitment)`, `Appended(Question(People))`, `PqExpired`, `PqEscalated`, `PqAnswered`, `PqSuperseded`, `PqMoved`, hold events (chain), `NodeClosed`, `NodeReopened`, `NodeMoved` |
| `unconfirmed_said` | said states on n, attended | `SaidUnconfirmed`, `SaidConfirmed`, `SaidMoved`, hold events (chain), `NodeMoved` |
| `open_intent` | intent, live holds on n, waiting | `IntentOpened`, `IntentClosed`, `IntentMoved`, `HoldIssued`/`HoldEnded` on n, `WaitSet`, wait resolution |
| `question_recheck`, `proceed_on_assumption` | marks | `MarkSet` |
| `objection` | objections on n | `Appended(Object)`, `ObjectionResolved`, `ObjectionMoved` |
| `basis_changed` (D-4) | the references of n's active decisions, and the state of what they name: a node's closure and outcome, a decision's state, `State::retracted`; n's `merged_into` | `Appended(Decision)` on n, `DecisionSuperseded` and `DecisionRetracted` of a decision on n; through `ix.cited_by` (the basis refresh of D.7.4), `NodeClosed` and `NodeReopened` of a cited node, `DecisionSuperseded` and `DecisionRetracted` of a cited decision, `Appended(Retract)` of a cited target; `NodeClosed` and `NodeReopened` of n (a merge) |
| `too_big` | attempts, `params.too_big_attempts`, life | `HoldEnded(Expired)`, `HoldEnded(EndedByClose(Move))`, `Appended(Checkpoint)`, `ParamsChanged`, `NodeClosed`, `NodeReopened` |
| `overdue` | due, life, now | `NodeCreated`, `NodeUpdated` (due), `NodeClosed`, `NodeReopened`, `Fired(Due)` |
| `ready_to_close` | children counts, life, fence (1.6) | `NodeCreated`, `NodeClosed`, `NodeReopened`, `NodeMoved` of a child (old and new parent); `HoldIssued` on n (the chain refresh) |
| `missed` | `last_missed`, life | `SeriesOutcome`, `NodeClosed`, `NodeReopened` |
| `stale` (1.8) | life, tags, capacity, role and place (container), live holds on n, waiting, `touched_at`, `params.offer_stale`, now | every touch (D.7.4), `OfferSet`, `NodeUpdated` (tags, capacity, repeat), `NodeMoved`, `HoldIssued`/`HoldEnded` on n, `WaitSet`, wait resolution, `ParamsChanged`, `Fired(Stale)` |

**Time-dependent flags and their deadlines (F, second half).** Between two events every flag
condition is monotone in time: it combines "lease ended", "wait time passed", "follow-up passed", and
"due passed", each of which can only become true as time passes, and each appears only with the
polarity that keeps the combination monotone (for example `¬attended` and `¬waiting` only grow). A
currently false condition therefore becomes true exactly at one of the times its inputs change, and
each such time is a queued deadline of its owner (lease, wait, commitment, due, and, 1.8, the
node's Stale key, which `¬held_self` and `¬waiting` only make reachable later, at a lease's end or a
wait's resolution, both of which refresh the node). `check_invariants` checks this directly as F1
and F2 (D.9). `stale` is open-only, as `too_big` and `missed` are, so every flag a closed node can
carry is still in `CLOSED_TAKE`.

### D.8.4 Tree, names, limits, cycles (§4, K3, K4, L1, T5)

- **Resolution** of `NodeRef::Path(steps)`: from ROOT, for each step take `names[(cur, step)]`, else
  `aliases[(cur, step)]`, else `not_found(Node)`. `NodeRef::Id(i)` must be in `nodes`. Command
  targets do not follow `merged_into`, so `take` on a merged node reports `closed` with
  `merged_into`, whatever flags it carries, and `next` never offers it (A-94); links resolve by
  following it (`resolve_merged`, bounded by `nodes.len()` steps). `node reopen` of a merged node
  still succeeds and clears `merged_into` (§16).
- **Creating or moving onto a name.** A live name at `(parent, name)` is `invalid(NameTaken)`. An
  alias there is removed by `NodeCreated` or `NodeMoved`. Missing ancestors are created as
  `Origin::Ancestor` plain nodes: capacity 1, title = their name, no tags, no hold, and their
  parent's `needs` (CS-26).
- **Limits (L1, A-28, CS-10, A-113).** `depth(n) <= tree.max_depth` for every node, ROOT at depth 0.
  `open_agent_children(p) <= tree.max_children` after every `create` and `move`, for every parent
  `p` other than PEOPLE and TEAMS, where only open children with origin `Agent` or `Ancestor`
  count: occurrences and signals are server-made and exempt, and a closed child no longer counts,
  because closed children never reach `next`, rollups are counters, and `view list` caps its scan,
  so counting them prevents no failure, while `chat/`, `kb/`, and busy task parents would fill up
  for good within hours at 10,000 agents (review FS-6, RS-17). The persons and teams of the
  directory, every child of PEOPLE and TEAMS, do not count at all (§4, §19, A-113): a company has
  1,000 to 5,000 principals, far over the default 500, and a directory that refused its next person
  would leave that human's aliases as separate principals. `open_agent_children` still counts them,
  so that one counting rule serves every parent, and L1 never compares it at those two parents.
  Checked on `create` (every new node, including ancestors and the first occurrence of a
  series), on `move` (`depth(new parent) + 1 + height(n) <= tree.max_depth`, with `height` computed by
  walking the subtree, and, when `n` is open and agent-made, the new parent's open agent children),
  and on `update` that adds `repeat` (the occurrence's depth). A reopen (`node reopen`, or `take` or
  `next` of a flagged closed child) is never refused for the child limit and may take a parent past
  it: refusing would leave a flagged node without a mover (M1), and `next` cannot fail. L1's child
  half is therefore a step invariant on `create` and `move`, and its depth half a state invariant
  (D.9.2). A loop that creates open nodes still stops at `tree.max_children`; one that creates and
  closes is bounded by `write.per_hour`.
- **Text size (L1, A-114).** No command stores a `Text` longer than `text.max` bytes after masking:
  the shell answers `limit(TextTooLong)` before queueing, and `apply` repeats the check before O1
  (D.8.1). Like the child half, it is a step invariant: a `ParamsChanged` that lowers `text.max`
  applies to later commands and leaves the stored texts alone (D.11.8). Without it, one call could
  store a text up to the transport's 1 MiB body cap, and a looping session 120 MiB an hour at
  `write.per_hour`, in a history from which nothing is deleted (FQ-4).
- **Ancestor walks** (`ancestors(n)`) stop at ROOT or after `nodes.len()` steps.
- **Tree cycles (K4).** `move` fails with `cycle` if the new parent is `n` or one of its descendants
  (walk up from the new parent).
- **Wait and dependency cycles (T5).** The edges are `x → t` for `x.wait = Some(Wait { on: Node(t),
  .. })`, resolved or not (a reopened target unresolves the wait, A-55), and `x → d` for
  `d ∈ x.depends_on`. Adding an edge `x → t` fails with `cycle` if `t = x` or `x` is reachable from
  `t`:

```rust
/// Iterative depth-first search with a visited set; at most nodes.len() pops. Returns the path
/// for the hint. `extra` carries edges the same command is about to add (merge redirects all of
/// them at once, and `extra_removed` the edges it drops).
pub fn reaches(s: &State, from: NodeId, to: NodeId, extra: &[(NodeId, NodeId)],
               extra_removed: &[(NodeId, NodeId)]) -> Option<Vec<NodeId>>;
```

### D.8.5 Candidates and `next` (§10.4)

**Classification** (session-independent, maintained in `ix.next` by `evolve`, CS-16). For a node `n`,
the first row that matches:

| Condition | Candidate |
|---|---|
| `n` is reserved (capacity 0) | none |
| `n` is an open occurrence in phase `Waiting` | none: not before its slot (§12) |
| `n` is closed and `occ_locked(n)` (its series is open and still a series) | none (A-13) |
| `n` is closed with `merged_into ≠ None` | none: `next` never undoes a merge (A-94) |
| `n` is closed with `upheld ≠ None` | none (1.8, §5, §11.3): an objection upheld on it corrected its outcome; only `node reopen` reopens it |
| `n` closed, `capacity > 0`, `flags ∩ CLOSED_TAKE ≠ ∅` | `Cand::Node(n)`: taking reopens it |
| `n` open, `waiting(n)`, `open_commitment ∈ flags` | `Cand::Status(n)`: `{status: node}`, no hold |
| `n` open, `waiting(n)` | none; in `ix.next.waiting` when the next row would match it but for the wait (1.4, §10.4) |
| `n` open, `live(n) < capacity`, and (`offer ∈ tags` ∧ ¬`is_container(n)`, or `flags ≠ ∅`, or `n` is an occurrence in phase `Available`) | `Cand::Node(n)` |
| anything else | none |

`CLOSED_TAKE = {unanswered_request, open_commitment, objection, open_intent, unconfirmed_said,
basis_changed}` (`open_intent` and `unconfirmed_said`: A-10; `basis_changed`: D-4, so that a
closed conclusion whose basis was refuted is offered, and taking it reopens it for re-examination).
It is `next`'s rule for which closed nodes to offer (§10.4), not `take`'s: `take` reopens a closed
node with any flag and refuses only an unflagged one (§21, §25, A-96). With `too_big` and `missed`
open-only (D.8.3), the two rules differ only on merged nodes, which neither reopens (A-94). Every
unrouted user entry is a `Cand::Route(e)`, a routing item needing no hold. "Free" means `live <
capacity` (A-65). Signal nodes carry the `offer` tag from creation, so they are candidates like any
offered node; a closed signal node can be a closed candidate, and taking it reopens it under A-89.
A person or team (`is_directory`, D.4.3) is a candidate only by its flags, as a series is (A-113):
one created with a hold and released stays out of `next` (it gets no `offer` tag either, D.7.4),
while an `unanswered_request` on it, say, still brings it to `next` if its capacity allows. A move
into or out of `@people` or `@teams` changes the moved node's classification, which the refresh of
the event's own node recomputes (D.7.4).

**Exclusions** (each counted in `EmptyWhy`). Two are the same for every caller, so the index holds
them back (`ix.next.held`, CS-16):
- `Node` and `Status`: some `d ∈ n.depends_on` is open (`depends`); `paused(n, now)` (`paused`,
  D.8.21; the paused ancestor's scope goes into `pause_scopes`, CS-9).

The others depend on the caller and are applied while reading the index:
- `Node` and `Status`: the caller's class has refused `n` (`class_refused`: at least the record's
  `quorum` live entries), or one of its sessions refused `n` less than `refusal.backoff` ago (an
  entry with `backoff_until > now`) (`refused`, E1, CS-7); `n.needs ⊄ caps(sess)` (`needs`);
  `n.est > horizon(sess)` when both are present (`horizon`);
- `Node` only: `sess` already holds `n` (`own`; §10.4, A-115). A session holds a node at most once
  (§10.1), so a node the caller already holds has no slot the caller can take, and `next` (and
  `hello.offers`) would only hand back the hold it has. It matters only for a node of capacity 2 or
  more. A status item needs no hold, so `own` does not apply to it (§10.4);
- the `query` filter (`query`, A-20): `under` (ancestor-or-self), `kind`, `tags ⊆ n.tags`. Routing
  items are offered only when the query is empty.

Routing items have no other exclusion (A-64).

**Order.** For each remaining candidate:

```
tier(c)  := 0  if c is Route, or flags ∩ T0 ≠ ∅,
                  or (c is an occurrence in phase Available ∧ ¬window_fired)
            1  if priority > 0 or flags ∖ {stale} ≠ ∅       // 1.8: stale alone raises nothing
            2  otherwise
            where T0 = {unrouted, unanswered_request, open_commitment, unconfirmed_said,
                        open_intent, question_recheck, proceed_on_assumption,
                        basis_changed}                     // basis_changed: D-4
aged(c)  := priority + ⌊now / HOUR⌋ − ⌊since(c) / HOUR⌋  // i64; priority 0 for Route (CS-12)
h(c)     := tie_hash(sess, id(c))                      // the ring distance of D.2.6; id: node
                                                       // id, or the entry eid
stale(c) := 1 if stale ∈ flags, else 0                 // 1.8 (§10.4): last in its tier
est(c)   := 1 if c is a Node without est and horizon(sess) is set, else 0
                                                       // 1.10: after the estimated ones
recheck(c) := 0 if c is a Node whose {external} wait fired, else 1   // 1.7: first in its tier
review(c) := 0 if c is a Status of a closed node (a review item), else 1
                                                       // 1.10: next after the recheck-due ones
aged'(c) := priority if review(c) = 0, else aged(c)    // 1.10: a review's key has no hours
request(c) := 0 if unanswered_request ∈ flags or c is a Route, else 1
                                                       // 1.11: requests first in their tier
needs(c) := −min(|needs(node(c))|, 15), 0 for a Route  // 1.11: more of the caller's caps first
key(c)   := (tier, stale, est, request, recheck, needs, review, −aged'(c), h, id, kind_rank)
                                                       // kind_rank: Node 0, Status 1, Route 2
                                                       // 1.11: a review's tier ignores objection
```

The index folds `stale` and `recheck` into the hour group (`index::cand_at_with`): a recheck-due
node's group lies `RECHECK_SHIFT = 2⁴⁰` hours below its own, and a stale one's `STALE_SHIFT = 2⁴²`
above, both far past any `⌊since / HOUR⌋ − priority` (within ±2³³), so the four bands of a tier sort
as recheck-due, plain, stale and recheck-due, stale, each in the order of its groups and the ring;
`NextKey` is unchanged (Kani `next_key_total`), and `health`'s oldest-candidate scan reads each
tier from the first entry of each band (D.8.22). 1.10: a review item's group is `−REVIEW_SHIFT −
priority`, `REVIEW_SHIFT = 2³⁶`, the same for every review of a priority, a band between the
recheck-due and the plain ones in which the ring alone orders the reviews (the lab's fifth round:
two sessions given the same oldest review reached opposite verdicts); a review is never stale or
recheck-due. `health` reads the review band whole, since its first entry is not its oldest: its
items are the closed nodes with an open objection, few beside the backlog. `est` depends on the
caller's horizon, which no partition knows, so the merge reads it (below). 1.11 (`index::band`):
the shifts grow to fit two more bands, a candidate without a request `NO_REQUEST_SHIFT = 2⁴⁵`
above, `RECHECK_SHIFT = 2⁴³` below, `NEEDS_SHIFT = 2³⁸` above for each label fewer than 15 that
the node needs, and `STALE_SHIFT = 2⁴⁷` above them all, so a tier's bands sort as (stale, request,
recheck, needs, review); `needs` is the same for every candidate of a partition, so `health` reads
eight bands a tier, each with its review band. A series whose open occurrence waits for its slot is
held back (`Held::before_slot`, from `series_open`, which the recount passes in), and a refreshed
occurrence refreshes its series.

`since(c)` is `State::since[c]` (the event that made `c` a candidate; for an occurrence, its slot;
for a routing item, the entry's time). The final `kind_rank` only separates a node and an entry that
share a numeric id.

**Why hour buckets and a ring** (CS-12, D-1, review TP-2 and FS-9). With 1.1's `aged = priority +
⌊(now − since) / 1 h⌋` and `h = FNV-1a-64(session ‖ 0 ‖ id)`, the relative order of two candidates
changes with `now` alone and differs between sessions, so no index can be kept in order by events:
the exact order costs a scan of the whole first aged group, about an hour of arrivals (36,000 to
62,000 candidates at 10,000 agents), 32 to 50 ms per `next` or `hello`, and a 07:00 herd of 20,000
calls costs about 76 s of writer time. With wall-clock hour buckets, `⌊now / HOUR⌋` is common to
every candidate, so `−aged` orders like `⌊since / HOUR⌋ − priority`, which changes only at events;
`aged` differs from 1.1's by 0 or 1. With the ring, a group is ordered by `fnv_id`, the same for every
caller, and each session starts at `fnv_session(sess)`: its first eligible candidate is a range query,
and concurrent sessions still spread over the group within about a factor of 2 of 1.1 (D.2.6). The
order stays a total order (Kani `next_key_total`), and no invariant depends on the tie-break
(D.10.6).

**The index** (CS-16, review TP-2, FS-9, RS-5). `ix.next` keeps every candidate that nothing holds
back in the partition of its `(needs, est bucket)`, sorted by `NextKey = (tier, group, fnv, id,
kind)`, where `group = ⌊since / HOUR⌋ − priority` orders like `−aged` because `⌊now / HOUR⌋` is
common to all. A session's best candidate is found without ranking the backlog:
1. The eligible partitions are those with `needs ⊆ caps(sess)` and an `est` bucket below the bit
   length of the session's horizon, or bucket 0, or any bucket without a horizon; the bucket equal
   to the horizon's bit length is eligible too, with `est > horizon` checked per entry. The needs
   sets with `needs ⊆ caps(sess)` are found in `ix.next.needs_trie` by descending only through the
   labels the caller has, so the cost is the eligible sets and their prefixes, not every partition:
   a company with 100 teams and skill labels has 10³ to 10⁴ needs sets. The other partitions are
   what `needs` and `horizon` count in `EmptyWhy`: `needs` is the number of candidates in
   partitions less those in the needs-eligible ones (a set's length is O(1)), and `horizon` the
   needs-eligible ones above the horizon's bucket.
2. In each eligible partition, the candidates of one `(tier, group)` are read in ring order from the
   session's point: the range from `(tier, group, fnv_session(sess))` upwards, then the range from
   the group's start below that point. This is exactly the order of `h = fnv − fnv_session` within
   the group (D.2.6).
3. A merge over the partitions' heads, smallest `(tier, stale, est, group, h, id, kind)` first,
   yields the candidates in `key` order (`stale` read from the group's band); each is skipped if a
   caller exclusion applies (`refused`, `own`, `query`, or `est > horizon` in the boundary bucket),
   and the first `k` that remain are the answer (1 for `next`, 3 for `hello.offers`). 1.10: for a
   caller with a horizon, a partition of `est` bucket 0 is read as two streams, its nodes to take,
   whose `est` is 1, and its other items (status, review, and routing items, whose `est` is 0), so
   that each stream's keys come in merge order; a stream passes over the other's keys, one visit
   each.

A pause moves the candidates under its scope into `held` when it is set, and back when it is lifted
or expires; a `depends_on` target's close or reopen moves its dependents (D.7.4). Both are rare. A
pause finds the candidates under its scope by the cheaper of two passes: a walk of the scope's
subtree, or, when the subtree (`ix.node[scope].sub`, exact) holds more nodes than there are
candidates, a pass over `ix.next.of` and `ix.next.held` with `is_under`, at O(candidates × depth);
so a pause of `/`, which anyone may set (FQ-3), costs O(candidates × depth), not O(the forum's
10⁶ to 10⁸ nodes). A `next` costs O((P + T + skipped + k) × log), where P is the number of
eligible partitions, T the trie nodes visited, and `skipped` is bounded by the class's live
refusals, the session's holds, the entries of the one boundary bucket whose `est` exceeds the
horizon, and, under a query, SCAN_MAX entries the query filter rejected, after which the scan stops
and `EmptyWhy.query_capped` says `≥k` (§18, A-20). Under a query the routing items' partition is not
read at all. Measured on the review's prototype: 0.4 to 0.6 µs per `next` at 10⁵ candidates, where
ranking the backlog took 29 to 39 ms (review TP-2). The brute-force ranking of every candidate by
`key` stays as `spec::ranked`, the oracle the proptests compare the index with (D.12.3).

**`hold next {query?, lease?}`.** Validation: `query.under` resolves (`not_found(Node)`) → the
session's live holds `>= hold.per_session` → `holds_limit` (§10.1, literal even though routing and
status items need no hold, A-50). Execution:
1. Find the best candidate in the index; emit `NextCalled { sess, outcome, open, class_window_end:
   now + refusal.window }`, where `open` is "the query is empty" (the session asked for any work it
   can do, which makes its class active for E1 with its caps, CS-7) and `outcome` is `Item`,
   `Nothing` (`why.candidates = 0`), or `NothingForYou` (CS-31).
2. Empty → reply `Next(Empty { why, leave_better: leave_better(s, None, Some(sess)) })` (D.8.7).
   `why.waiting` is `|ix.next.waiting|` (1.4, §10.4, R27): the nodes that wait for a question, a
   node, a time, or something outside, counted for every caller and query, so "no node is offered"
   is never said while offered work waits; the shell renders it as "<k> nodes wait and come back
   when their waits resolve". When pauses excluded candidates (`why.paused > 0`), the shell
   renders each scope of
   `why.pause_scopes` with its source, time, and reason, and the hint "read its reason, and lift it
   with `control unpause` if it no longer holds" (CS-9). It also renders the first reason of the
   cached health that is not green, yellow ones included, with its first item and what fixing it
   takes (D.8.22): an idle agent is the one with time to fix what no other rule moves.
3. Top is `Route(e)` → reply `Next(Route { entry: e, why })` (the agent then calls `talk route`).
4. Top is `Status(n)` → `Shown { sess, n, n.seq }` if it raises `shown[n]` (CS-14); reply
   `Next(Status { node: n, why })`. The agent records a `said` of kind `reply` in each conversation
   whose commitment raises the flag, which fulfils that conversation's commitments (§9.2, §10.4);
   rule 9 of the next calls names them (D.8.26).
5. Top is `Node(n)` → if `n` is closed, `was := n`'s outcome and `reopen(n)` (D.8.20, with K7 and
   its `duplicate_key` warning); `issue_hold(n, lease, was)`; `bind_holder_notes(n)`; `Shown { sess,
   n, n.seq }` if it raises `shown[n]`; reply
   `Next(Hold { node, token, lease_until, why, reopened: was })` (1.4: `{was}`, R4). Taking cannot
   fail here: every take precondition is part of the classification or of the exclusions.

`why_this = { tier, flags, aged, reason }`, where `reason` is the first that applies of
`ClosedFlagged`, `Routing`, `Status`, `Occurrence`, `Signal`, `Flagged`, `Offered`. `hello.offers`
is the top 3 of the same order, without `NextCalled` and without taking; when there are none, it
carries the `EmptyWhy` of the same read, as an empty `next` gives it (1.4, §20.3, R25).

**Cost.** Independent of the forum's size, and of the backlog apart from the skips above (§18). One
skip is not bounded by a constant: in the boundary bucket, the candidates whose `est` lies between
the horizon and the next power of two (a backlog of 65 to 127-minute tasks is skipped in full by
every `next` with a 64-minute horizon). The gates of D.12.8 check the cost with a `Meter` at 10⁵
candidates, that boundary case included (G-3); if it shows, the buckets are split finer (four per
power of two), which shrinks the boundary range to a quarter at four times the partitions.

**Tie-break under conformance.** The public `ranked` and `apply` always use FNV-1a-64 and the
index. The test-only `apply_with(.., TieBreak::Id)` of D.6.1 breaks the `h` component by id instead,
which is what the model's slices do with `USE_FNV = false` (D.10.6), and ranks with `spec::ranked`,
