reaches its quorum: nobody else asks for such work. Answering the refusal question, or its default,
clears the node's refusals (A-56), so the node returns to `next` for every class. After a drop, the
unsettled requests are on a closed node and carry `unanswered_request`, which makes the node a closed
candidate; the agent that takes it tells the requester (for a user request, a `to_user` of kind
`result` to the requester principal, which needs nobody present, CS-4, A-23), which settles them. A
refusal older than
`refusal.ttl` never excludes a node: `next` reads `expires_at > now`, and the expiry deadline
removes the entry (E1, second clause). This works with any number of classes, including one
(§10.3).

### D.8.15 People: requests, `said`, `ask`, `heard`, commitments (§9)

**`talk request {at, text, origin, where?, requester}`.** Validation: `at` resolves; `text`
non-empty (`invalid(EmptyText(Text))`); a `repeat:` origin or `where` is `invalid(ReservedKey)`
(A-90). If `ix.origins[origin.key] = r`: reply `Request { request: r, node: r.node, existing: true }` and
nothing else (Q1: "a repeat is the same request", that is, a repeat of the same message, A-61).
Otherwise `k := where`, else `origin`, and `c := conv_node(at, k)`, which must not be reserved
(`invalid(ReservedNode)`, D.8.8) (`KeyAdded` first if case 3); `Appended(Request { origin, conv: k,
from_user })` on `c` (text: the
request; extra: the requester), where `from_user` is the entry of a `user:e<n>` origin; if that entry
is unrouted, `EntryRouted { e, Request { node: c, request } }`. Recording needs no hold (§9.4). Reply
`Request { request, node: c, existing: false }`.

`where` defaults to the origin (A-61), not to `at`'s conversation as for `said`: a call without a
message id passes the conversation key as its origin and keeps 1.1's meaning, and a `user:e<n>`
origin stays its own routing key (D.8.11). An agent that passes a message id without `where` makes
that message a conversation key on `at` (case 3); a later `said` without `where` there then reports
`AmbiguousConversationKey` if `at` already carried one, and `node key {remove}` repairs it. Such a
request's conversation is the message id itself (`Request::conv`), so only a `said` with that id as
`where` answers it (§9.4, 1.3), even after the repair, which that `said` undoes (case 3 again); rule
6 fills that `where` (D.8.26). `create
{request}` defaults `where` to the call's own conversation key instead (D.8.9), because there the
conversation is among the keys being created or joined.

**`talk said {at, where?, text, kind, corrects?, seen?}`.** Validation: `at` resolves → `kind ≠
Question` (`invalid(SaidKindQuestion)`) → `corrects` names a `said` (`not_found(Said)`) → `k :=
conv_key(at, where)` (`invalid(NoConversationKey | AmbiguousConversationKey)`; a `repeat:` `where`
is `invalid(ReservedKey)`) → `c := conv_node(at, k)` is not reserved (`invalid(ReservedNode)`,
D.8.8). Warnings, computed on the pre-state:
- `moved`: with `seen := seen.unwrap_or(sessions[sess].shown[c], or 0)`, the entries on `c` with
  `seq > seen`, type in {Request, Said, Heard, Question, Answer}, and author not `sess`, read from
  `ix.people` newest first: at most MOVED_MAX of them, with a `total` that is exact when the range
  holds at most SCAN_MAX entries and `seen >= c.people_left` (no people entry after `seen` has left
  memory, D.4.12), and `≥k` otherwise (CS-17, spec-clarify of §9.2). 1.1 listed them all,
  and a new session has `seen = 0`, so a `said` on a conversation with 10⁴ entries carried 10⁴ eids
  (review TP-8, FS-16); the newest are the ones to read before speaking, and the agent pages older
  ones with `view feed`;
- `conversation_held`: another session has a live hold on `c` or a descendant, and the caller holds
  neither `c` nor a descendant of it (`conversation_holder(c, sess, k)`); 1.10: the `said` counts
  all the same, and the detail says so and that, by convention, the holder speaks (1.9 recorded it
  withheld, with `withheld: true`, a field 1.10 removes); 1.11 (§9.1, §9.2): it names the first
  holder whose caps include `k`'s scheme, else the first holder, and does not come when no holder
  has that cap and the caller has it (`voice(c, sess, k) = Caller`, D.8.26);
- `agreement`: the sources are `at` and its ancestors, plus `c` and its ancestors when `c` is not
  among them, that have non-empty agreements; `approvals := current_approvals(at)` (A-76, CS-34,
  D.8.17).

Also read on the pre-state (1.11, §9.1, §9.2): `voice := voice(c, sess, k) = Caller`, and `alone`,
whether the session holds no live hold. Events: `KeyAdded { c, k }` if `conv_node` is case 3;
`Appended(Said { conv: k, kind, corrects, voice })` on `c`, eid `a`; with `alone`, `SaidConfirmed {
a, via: Recorded, link: None }` (1.11: no release or close of the session will come to mark it, so
it is taken as sent with its reply at once, `with_reply`; in the lab's sixth round (l6) a chat
worker's two replies stayed pending in the holder's brief); then, whoever holds the conversation
(1.10, §9.2; 1.9 emitted `SaidWithheld { a }`
when `conversation_held` held, and nothing more, but in the lab's fifth round (l6) the holder of an
incident could not post in its chat, and the chat worker's answer was withheld until it held a child
made up only to speak):
- `Ack`: if `c` has open commitments with `conv = k` (in `items(c).open_commitments`, CS-20) →
  `CommitmentRefreshed { x, followup_at: now + commitment.followup }` for every such `x`, ascending
  (after a merge there may be several); else `CommitmentOpened { a, c, k, followup_at: now +
  commitment.followup }` (A-26: only an ack refreshes);
- `Reply`, `Result`, `Correction`: `CommitmentFulfilled { x, by: a }` for every `x` in
  `items(c).open_commitments` with `x.conv = k`, ascending, and for no other commitment (§9.2, 1.3,
  decided on 2026-10-02, D.14.3), then the people answers of D.8.8, for the requests of
  conversation `k` only (§9.4, 1.3), and `try_settle`.

Reply `Said { said: a, node: c, answered, settled, fulfilled }` (1.4, §20.7, R9): `answered` the
requests whose `RequestAnswered` the step emitted, `settled` those whose `RequestSettled` it
emitted, and `fulfilled` the commitments whose `CommitmentFulfilled` it emitted, each ascending and
empty for an `Ack` (`settled` is read by rule 8 of the next calls, D.8.26). In 1.3 only `settled`
was returned, and agents guessed which commitment a reply had fulfilled. 1.12 (§9.1, §9.2): `keyed`,
the key `k` when the conversation node is case 3 (`KeyAdded` emitted), as `heard` and `ask` to a
person have it, rendered as `conversation_node`; and a `Reply` or `Result` that answered nothing,
on a `c` none of whose resident requests is of conversation `k` (`has_request`, over
`items(c).requests`), warns `answered_nothing { node: c, conv: k }`; in the lab's seventh round
(it6 l3), a chat worker answered two questions in a thread with no request recorded, and its first
`said` made a node the thread's conversation node unsaid.

**`talk said {said_id, confirmed}`.** `not_found(Said)`; already `Confirmed` → reply
`SaidConfirmed { already: true }`, no event; otherwise `SaidConfirmed { said, Explicit, link:
Some(confirmed) }` (pending, unconfirmed, or withheld → confirmed, §25; a withheld one that its
author sent after all is marked sent, and answers nothing, 1.9).

**`talk ask {at, text, where?, again?, blocking?}` to a person** (`AskTo::Person { where_,
blocking }`; 1.4: `blocking` is this form's only, and `options`, `recommendation`, `default`, and
`due` are the human form's, D.11.5). Validation as for `said`. With
`c := conv_node(at, k)`: if `c` has a people question in state `Open` with `conv = k`
(`items(c).open_pq[k]`) and not `again`
→ reply `Asked { question, said: None, node: c, existing: true }`, no further event (§9.3, "asking
only once"; A-25). Otherwise: `KeyAdded` if case 3; `a := Appended(Said { conv: k, kind: Question,
corrects: None, voice })` (pending, so the next release or close confirms it; 1.11: with `alone`,
`SaidConfirmed { a, Recorded }` at once, as for `said`); `q :=
Appended(Question(People { conv: k, blocking, said: a, supersedes: old, recheck_at: now +
question.recheck }))` (A-24); with `again` and an open old question: `PqSuperseded { old, by: q }`
and `WaitSet { w, Some(Question { q, 0 }) }` for every node `w` whose wait on the old one is still
unresolved (`Question { old, rechecks_at_set = old.rechecks }`, read before `PqSuperseded`), so
that a node whose wait already resolved at a recheck, and which is offered work again, is not
suspended once more ("moves any waits", §9.3; A-109). Warnings as for `said`. Reply `Asked {
question: q, said: Some(a), node: c, existing: false }`.

**`talk heard {at, where?, from, text, answers?}`.** Validation: `at` resolves; `k`; `answers` names a
people question (`not_found(Question)`, `invalid(NotPeopleQuestion)`). Events: `KeyAdded` if case 3;
`h := Appended(Heard { conv: k, answers })` on `c`; with `answers: q`, if `q` is `Open`, `Expired`, or
`Escalated`: `answer_pq(q, h)` (§9.3: it answers the question it names). An answer to a question that
is already answered, or `superseded`, is recorded and changes no state: `superseded` is final for a
people question (§25), and the question that superseded it stays open, so its next recheck has
someone re-read the conversation, where the `heard` is. Reply `Heard { entry: h, node: c, answered }`,
with `answered = Some(q)` only when it changed `q`'s state.

```
answer_pq(q, by):
    PqAnswered { q, by }                                   // waits on q resolve by predicate
    MarkSet { w, m, q, off } for each w in ix.marked_by_question[q] and each mark m it carries
    if q is Escalated { uq } and uq is Pending: UqAnswered { uq, by }      // A-60
    if q is Escalated { uq } and uq is Lapsed:                             // CS-2
        MarkSet { w, Assume, uq, off } for each w in ix.marked_by_question[uq]
```

A person's late answer to an escalated question whose user question lapsed clears the lapse's
`proceed_on_assumption` marks: the missing answer is there now, and the brief shows it (§9.3).

**Commitments.** Opened by an ack, refreshed by an ack on the same conversation key, and fulfilled
by a reply, result, or correction on the same conversation node with the same conversation key `k`
(its `where`, given or by default): the key `CommitmentOpened` carries and `Commitment::conv` keeps
(§9.2, 1.3). A reply in another conversation on the node fulfils none of them, as it answers none of
that conversation's requests (D.8.8): two threads joined on one node by `node key {add}` or a merge
each get their own status. Both the refresh and the fulfilment filter `items(c).open_commitments` by
`conv`, without an index by conversation as `unanswered` and `open_pq` have: an ack refreshes the
open commitments of its conversation instead of opening another, so only a merge gives a node a
second open commitment of one conversation, and the filter is O(open commitments on `c`), a few. A
merge moves an open commitment with its `conv` and fulfils nothing (D.8.20); the next reply of its
conversation on `into` does. A status reply to a `{status: node}` item is a `said` of kind `reply`,
so it fulfils the commitments of the conversation its `where` names, and rule 9 suggests one per
conversation whose commitment raises the flag (§10.4, D.8.26). The flag is D.8.3's.

### D.8.16 Agent communication and the inbox (§13)

**Recipients**, computed by decide when a note is recorded (A-49) and stored in its body:

```
recipients(to, sender) -> (BTreeSet<SessionId>, pending_holder: bool):
    Session(x)  => ({x}, false)
    Holder(n)   => let hs = sessions other than sender with a live hold on n        // 1.4, R12
                   if hs is empty { ({}, true) } else { (hs, false) }   // "or takes it next"
    Holders(a)  => ({}, false)                         // read time: the branch's holders (D-6)
    Principal(p)=> ({}, false)                         // read time: p's sessions (A-18, CS-3)
```

**The sender is never a `holder:` or `holders:` recipient** (1.4, §13, R12). In 1.3 a holder that
wrote to `holder:` of its own node, or to `holders:` of a branch it held in, received its own
message, and rule 11 then suggested that it answer its own question. Now a `holder:` note goes to
the other holders, or, with none, to whoever other than the sender takes the node next
(`bind_holder_notes` skips a note whose author is the taker); and a session's inbox skips the
`holders:` notes it wrote. The author is the note's `EntryMeta::by`, which the core keeps for every
addressed note while the note lives (CS-17, D.4.12). `session:<self>` still reaches its sender: it
names the session explicitly.

**A note without `to`** (1.9, §13). `say`'s validation addresses it `Holder(at)` when a session
other than the sender holds `at` live (`others_hold`), so it is recorded and delivered as a
`holder:` note, with `Appended(Note { to: Some(Holder(at)), recipients, .. })`, and the shell's
reply names its `to` and `delivered_to`. In the lab's fourth round (l6), five notes without
`to` at the node the lead held reached no inbox. 1.10: it is addressed `Holder(at)` too when no
session holds `at` live and `at` can be held (not reserved, capacity above 0: `next_holder`), so
`recipients` leaves it `pending_holder` and the next taker other than the sender receives it
(`bind_holder_notes`); in the lab's fifth round (l7), 16 of a parallel run's 18 notes had no `to`,
and none reached anyone. 1.11: `next_holder` also requires `at` open, since a closed node is never
taken, and at a closed node the note is addressed `Session(x)` to the session `x` that closed it
(`closure.by`, D.4.3), while `x` is live (in `sessions`, not `silent`) and is not the sender
(`closer`); in the lab's sixth round (l5), 10 of a research run's 12 notes were at closed nodes and
reported "the next holder", and one, meant for the reviewer that had closed its node 4.5 s before,
reached nobody. Otherwise, at a node only the sender holds, a closed node whose closer is the sender,
silent, retired, or the server, or one nobody can hold, it stays a plain note (`Note { to: None }`,
no `EntryMeta`, CS-17). The shell's reply says whom it reached:
`delivered_to` lists the recipients, or reads "the next holder of <node>" for a pending `holder:`
note, or "nobody" for a plain note (1.10, §20.7). The decoder reads `to: "holder:"` with no path as
`holder:<at>`, in `say` and in `ask` to agents (D.11.5).

**Closed nodes and silent sessions** (1.12, §13). `recipients(Holder(n), sender)` of a closed `n`
is `closer(n, sender)` (now in `helpers::agents`), never pending, so `holder:<path>` and `holder:`
there reach what a note without `to` reaches; in the lab's seventh round (it6 l6), two notes to
`holder:` of an incident closed seconds before waited for a next holder while its closer was live.
`delivery_warnings` adds, after the note's or the agent question's entry, `no_recipient { node }`
when a note by `holder:` of a closed node, or without `to` at a closed `at`, reached nobody, and
`addressee_gone { session, since: last_seen }` for `session:` of a silent session. The shell's
`delivered_to` is now always the list of the recipients of a note with fixed recipients (`[]`
for none), with `pending: "the next holder of <node>"` for a pending `holder:` note; a
`principal:` or `holders:` note has none. The closure's words, 1.11's in `delivered_to`, are
`no_recipient`'s: its outcome, closer, time, and close entry (`Source::close_entry`), and the
closer to reach while it is silent and not retired.

A `to: principal:<key>` is `Principal(intern(key))`; a bare `to: user` is `Principal(chain(at,
None, false)[0])`, resolved when the note is recorded (A-49): the nearest requester of an unsettled user
request on `at` or above, else the owners, else `user` (CS-3, D.8.12). A note for Dave therefore
reaches the inbox of the sessions that serve Dave under any of his aliases, not every colleague's
agent; this is routing, not privacy: the note itself, like everything in the forum, is visible to
every agent (FQ-1).

**`holders:<a>` at read time** (D-6). A `holders:<a>` note records no recipients: it goes into
`ix.branch_notes[a]` until its `until`, and a session's inbox reads, for each node it holds, the live
`holders:` notes of that node and of each ancestor `m` that are newer than its cursor for `m`,
`branch_seen[m]`, at O(holds × depth × (log + such notes)). Recording costs O(1) at any size: fixing
the recipients when the note is recorded made `say {to: holders:/}` at 10,000 agents an event and a
`Note::recipients` of about
10,000 sessions and 10,000 `ix.inbox` entries that lived 24 hours, which one session could repeat
120 times an hour (and a looper that opens fresh sessions without limit, review C-12). The note also
reaches a session that takes work in the branch after the note, within `until`, as §13 requires. The
cursor keeps one `Eid` per scope the session has read from instead of a `read_by` set per broadcast.
It is per scope because notes of one scope are delivered together, all the live ones newer than its
cursor, so each live note of a scope reaches each session once; a single cursor per session would
hide an older live note of a branch the session enters only after it has read a newer note of
another branch, which §13 ("including sessions that take work there after the message was
recorded") does not allow. The map holds at most depth + 1 entries per node the session has held,
and the session's life is minutes. The writer wakes the parked
sessions that hold in the branch, found by descending `ix.attended_children` from `a`: O(the holds in
the branch), the recipients a broadcast has anyway (D.11.11). `holder:<n>` is the range of `n`'s
holds, fixed when recorded (A-49).

**`talk say {at, text, to?, expects?, reply_to?, until?}`.** Validation: `at` resolves; `to`: a
`session:` id exists (`not_found(Addressee)`, 1.4, R12: not the caller's own session, whose remedy
would be a new session), a `holder:` or `holders:` path resolves (`not_found(Node)`); `reply_to`
exists, that is `reply_to < next_eid` (`not_found(Entry)`, D.4.5). Events: `Appended(Note { to,
until: Some(until.map(|w| w.resolve(now)).unwrap_or(now + deliver.window)), recipients,
pending_holder, expects, reply_to })` on `at`; `to: None` records a plain note (A-17). Warning
`expects_ignored { expects }` when `expects` is `ack` or `reply` (1.4, §13, R17): `expects` is a
later release (§29) and nothing waits for the answer; the note is recorded as given, and the
warning points to `talk ask {to}`. Reply `Say { entry }`.

**`talk ask {at, text, to: agent}`** (`AskTo::Agent(AgentAddressee)`, validated like `say`'s `to`):
`Appended(Question(Agent { to, until: now + deliver.window, recipients, pending_holder }))` on `at`.
Reply `Asked { question, said: None, node: at, existing: false }`.

**`talk answer {question, text}`**: the shell reads the question's entry (its `entries` row and its
event) and adds its node and asker to the command, or answers `not_found(Question)`; an entry that is
not an agent question is `invalid(NotAgentQuestion)` (A-36), whether the question is resident or not.
Events: `Appended(Answer { question, recipient: asker, until: now + deliver.window })` on the
question's node; `AqAnswered { q, by }` if the question is resident and still `Open`. An agent
question leaves memory with its note at `until` (D.4.12), so an answer after that is recorded and
delivered like any other, and changes no state. Reply `Answered { entry }`.

```
bind_holder_notes(n):          // after every HoldIssued on n
    for x in ix.pending_holder[n] with notes[x].until > now and entries[x].by ≠ Session(sess):
        NoteBound { x, sess }                                  // 1.4: never to its sender

inbox(s, sess, now) -> Vec<NoteId>, ascending:
      { x ∈ ix.inbox[sess] : notes[x].until > now }
    ∪ ⋃ over p ∈ sessions[sess].principals, a ∈ aliases(p):
          { x : (until, x) ∈ ix.user_notes[a], until > now, sess ∉ notes[x].read_by }
    ∪ ⋃ over the nodes n the session holds, m ∈ n and its ancestors:
          { x ∈ ix.branch_notes[m] : notes[x].until > now, entries[x].by ≠ Session(sess),
                                     x > sessions[sess].branch_seen.get(m).unwrap_or(0) }
```

A `holder:` note that its sender takes the node over stays pending for the next other taker. A
`holders:` note its sender skips does not move its cursor: `InboxRead` advances `branch_seen[m]` over
the notes it delivers, and the sender's own are never delivered to it.

A note to a principal nobody serves before `until` expires unread; what a human must see goes in a
`to_user` report or a question (§13, CS-25).

`hello` emits `InboxRead { sess, first(inbox(...)) }` when the inbox is not empty, where `first` keeps
the INBOX_DELIVER_MAX (10) oldest items by eid (1.5, §13): only those are delivered and read, and the
rest wait for the next `hello` or `talk wait`, counted by the status line's `inbox`. Agent questions
and agent answers are delivered the same way.

**`talk wait {timeout, for?}`** is a long poll in the shell (D.11.11). The core command `Wait`
validates that `for` resolves, computes `delivered := first(inbox(s, sess, now))` and `news := Some((n,
n.seq))` if `n.seq > since` for `for: n`, where `since` is what the shell passes: the last `seq` of
`n` it reported to this session, kept in its memory, or else `sessions[sess].shown[n]`. It emits
`InboxRead` for the notes it delivers, and replies `Waited { delivered, news }`. News moves no `seen`:
`Shown` comes only from briefs and feed pages, which show the entries (A-85); news says only that
there are new ones. A woken waiter's `wait` is therefore a read that appends nothing unless notes are
delivered or presence is due (CS-14): with `Shown` on every news, 5,000 sessions parked on one hub
node with 10 appends a second made 50,000 writer jobs and as many events a second. Nothing to return
is `{timeout}` (A-19).

**`talk who {at?}`** — the `who` query (D.8.25): at most WHO_MAX sessions, with counts (CS-21).
**`session status {text}`** — `SessionStatus` (the text is shown by `who`).

### D.8.17 Decisions, agreements, review, retraction (§11, §15)

**`talk decide {at, text, settles?, supersedes?, basis?, evidence?}`.** Validation: `at` resolves;
`settles` ids are requests (`not_found(Request)`); `supersedes` is a decision (`not_found(Decision)`);
each basis reference resolves (CS-22): a node reference to a node (`not_found(Node)`), an entry
reference to an entry, `eid < next_eid` (`not_found(Entry)`, D.4.5); then `supersedes` is `Active`
(`invalid(DecisionNotActive)`), a node reference's version is at most the node's
(`invalid(VersionAhead)`, A-71), and an external reference's `checked_at` is at most `now`
(`invalid(CheckedAtAhead)`, 1.4, §15, re-run R27b: what was checked cannot have been checked in
the future). A node reference that names `at`, directly or through
`merged_into`, is not refused (1.4, §15, R14): it is dropped from the basis, with the warning
`self_basis_dropped { dropped }`, and the decision is recorded with the other references. A
decision does not rest on its own node: such a reference would flag the node itself with
`basis_changed` when it closes, for example as `failed`. 1.3 refused it with `invalid(SelfLink)`, a
refusal that protected no invariant (§21 mapped it to "—", against AGENTS.md's "every refusal maps
to an invariant"); the server notices rather than forbids. An entry reference to the decision
`supersedes` names is dropped likewise, with the warning `superseded_basis_dropped { decision,
dropped }` (1.4, §15, re-run R33): a decision that cited the one it supersedes became stale at
once. Events:
1. `d := Appended(Decision { settles, supersedes, assumes: at.assume_marks, evidence, basis })` on
   `at` (text: the decision; extra: the `what` of each external reference, as `TextField::Basis`),
   where each node reference is resolved through `merged_into` (A-88) and stores the node's outcome
   now (`life_at`, None while open), and each external reference its `checked_at` and `recheck`
   resolved against `now` (CS-22);
2. `DecisionSuperseded { old, by: d }` if `supersedes`;
3. for each `q` in `at.assume_marks`: `PqAssumed { q, decision: d }` if `q` is a people question
   still `Expired`, or `UqAssumed { q, decision: d }` if `q` is a user question still `Lapsed` with
   `assumed_by = None` (CS-2), and `MarkSet { at, Assume, q, off }` (A-15: any decision on a marked
   node records the assumption);
4. `try_settle(r)` for each `r` in `settles`;
5. if `at` is an open signal node: `close_node(at, Done, Session(sess), None, Close, …)`
   ("covered by a decision", §14, A-34).

Reply `Decided { decision: d, settled, not_settled }` (1.4, §20.7, R9): `settled` the requests step
4 settled; `not_settled` each other request of `settles`, ascending, with why: `SettledBefore` if it
was settled before this call; otherwise it is unanswered, and the answer it awaits is a `to_user`
of kind `result` to its requester (`AwaitsResult`, a user request) or a `said` of kind reply,
result, or correction on its node in its conversation (`AwaitsSaid { node, conv: r.conv }`, §9.4).
A listed request that is answered always settles here, so these are the only cases. In 1.3 an
unexplained `settled: []` led agents to decide again.

Every decision the server records (an assumption below, a refusal drop, D.8.14) and the decision a
`node close {settles}` records has an empty basis.

**The basis as references** (CS-22, review RS-9, RS-10). 1.1 stored `basis` as text with no
behaviour (A-48). A research programme that starts on the first release would then keep a year of
decisions whose basis is prose: events are immutable, so a later `basis_changed` could not read
them, and nothing could list what rests on a refuted lemma (links are outgoing only, `ix.dependents`
is internal, and a search for `#100` matches every number 100). Now the core stores each reference
with the decision and indexes the active ones in `ix.cited_by`, and `view node {view: full}` lists
what rests on a node (D.8.25). The shell parses the forms of §15 (`#12@4`, a path with `@4`, `e57`
or `entry:e57`, `{external: what, checked_at, recheck?}`) and builds `BasisArg`s (D.11.5).

**`basis_changed`, one hop** (D-4, review RS-11). A conclusion resting on a refuted lemma stays
closed `done` and keeps being cited: in a citation graph of 200,000 results grown by preferential
attachment, the top 0.1 % of results have at least 221 direct dependents, the largest 11,755, and
flagging them by hand at `write.per_hour` takes up to 98 session-hours while agents keep citing the
lemma. The flag is a predicate over the base state, with no time in it:

```
stale(s, b) := match b {
    Node { id: m, life_at, .. } => let f = resolve_merged(s, m) in      // the node m lives on in
        Node(m) ∈ s.retracted ∨ Node(f) ∈ s.retracted
        ∨ (f.life = Closed(c) ∧ c.outcome ≠ life_at.unwrap_or(Done)),   // f is never merged
    Entry(e)  => Entry(e) ∈ s.retracted ∨ (e ∈ s.decisions ∧ s.decisions[e].state ≠ Active),
    External { .. } => false,                     // external staleness is later (§29)
}
stale_decision(s, d) := s.decisions[d].state = Active ∧ ∃ b ∈ s.decisions[d].basis: stale(s, b)
items(n).stale_basis  = { d ∈ items(n).active_decisions : stale_decision(s, d) }   // R1
```

So a reference is stale when what it names was struck out (`talk retract`), when a cited decision
was superseded or retracted, or when a cited node is closed with another outcome than the one it had
when the decision was recorded (or, if it was open then, with an outcome other than `done`): a
lemma closed `done` and later closed `failed`, a failed approach that later closed `done`, an open
lemma the decision relied on that closed `dropped`. Three cases are deliberately not stale:
- **An edit.** Version changes are not compared, so a hub's typo fixes do not flood its dependents.
- **A reopen.** A cited node that is open again is under re-examination, not refuted: if a reopen
  made its citers stale, taking one flagged conclusion (which reopens it) would flag everything that
  rests on that conclusion at once, and the flag would cascade through the whole graph with no
  agent's judgement in between (199,193 nodes below the largest hub). The citers are flagged when
  the verdict is recorded: a close with another outcome, or a retraction.
- **A merge.** A node merged into another is closed `superseded` with `merged_into`; its content
  lives on in `into`, so its citers are not flagged by the merge. A reference is judged by the node
  it lives on in, `resolve_merged(m)`: a later refutation of `into` (closed `failed`, or retracted)
  flags the decisions that cited `from` before the merge, as it flags those that cite `into`. The
  merge re-files `ix.cited_by[Node(from)]` under `Node(into)`, an index change only (the stored
  references keep naming `from`), and the recount files every node reference under its
  `resolve_merged` target (D.4.10); a reopen of `from`, which clears `merged_into`, files its citers
  back, at O(the citers of `into`). Without this, citers of a refuted lemma's merged duplicates,
  which scenario 5 merges routinely (signals, CS-37), would keep relying on it silently.

The flag sits on the decision's node, whether it is open or closed (§15), and
is in `CLOSED_TAKE` and tier 0 (D.8.5): a closed conclusion whose basis went stale is offered, and
taking it reopens it. The next holder re-examines: a decision that supersedes the old one with a
basis as it stands now clears the flag; a retraction of the old decision clears it too, and closing
the node as `failed` then flags what rests on this node, which is the next hop, taken by an agent's
judgement (a theorem may survive through another proof). A merged node never carries it
(`¬merged(n)`), because `next` never offers a merged node (A-94), and its decisions stay behind as
history. A refresh costs O(the target's direct citers), one transaction even for the 11,755-citer
hub (D.7.4). External references, the transitive cascade, and §15's list of the `said` entries where
a retracted statement was told to people stay later (§29, D.13.4).

**Recording assumptions without an agent's decision** (A-104). `proceed_on_assumption` is cleared
only by a decision that records the assumption (§14), so the server records one where no agent will:

```
record_assumptions(n, by: Author, text):     // before a close of a node with assume marks
    if n.assume_marks = ∅: return
    d := Appended(Decision { settles: {}, supersedes: None, assumes: n.assume_marks,
                             evidence: None, basis: [] }) by `by` on n (text: the close's text)
    step 3 of talk decide: PqAssumed or UqAssumed for each q still Expired or Lapsed;
    MarkSet { n, Assume, q, off }

assume_now(q):                               // a question expires or lapses with no open node to mark
    home := q.node for a people question; for a user question, `about` if it is a node that is not
            reserved, else USER_DECISIONS (CS-2)
    d := Appended(Decision { settles: {}, supersedes: None, assumes: {q}, evidence: None,
                             basis: [] })
         by Server on home (text: "the node was closed before the question expired; the
         assumption stands", or "nobody answered by the last due; the assumption stands")
    PqAssumed { q, d }, or UqAssumed { q, d } for a user question
```

`close_node` runs `record_assumptions` first (D.8.18), so a closed node never carries an assume mark;
a merge moves the marks to `into` instead (D.8.20). The digest entry `Assumption { q }` or `Lapsed {
q }` is created at the expiry or lapse either way, so the user still sees the assumption (§8.5).

**Agreements.** A node's own and inherited agreements are the non-empty `agreements` of the node and
its ancestors, nearest first. `node close` and `talk said` (and `talk ask` to a person) always return
the `agreement` warning when the list is not empty, with the sources and the number of approvals of
the current content (§11.2 as amended by CS-34):

```
current_approvals(n) := Σ approvals[(n, v)] for n.content_version <= v <= n.version   // a range
```

`content_version` is the `version` at the last change of title, body, fields, or files (D.4.3), so an
approval survives a status change, a key, a link, a close, and a reopen, and lapses only when what
was reviewed changes (review RS-13: an `update {status: "reviewed"}` and a `key {add}` after an
approval used to leave the close warning with 0 approvals). O2 is unchanged. The server does not
interpret the texts, and the count is information, not a threshold: an agreement that asks for no
approval misses none, whatever the count, and the warning's rendered detail says both (1.4, §11.2,
R24, D.11.7).

**`talk approve {on: id@version, checked}`.** `on` resolves; `version > n.version` →
`invalid(VersionAhead)` (A-71). `Appended(Approve { version })` on `n` (text: checked); evolve counts
it at that version, which counts towards `current_approvals` while `version >= n.content_version`.
Reply `Approved { entry, approvals: current_approvals(n) }`.

**`talk object {on, note}`.** `Appended(Object)` on `n`: an open objection, and the `objection` flag.
Reply `Objected { objection }`.

**`talk resolve {objection, note, upheld?, defer?}`.** `not_found(Objection)`; a deferral (1.11) is
described below; already resolved (1.10,
§11.3): with the same verdict (resolved and `upheld` false, or upheld and `upheld` true) → reply
`ObjectionResolved { entry: None, already: Some({verdict, upheld}) }`, no event; with the opposite
verdict, a second verdict: `Appended(Object)` by the caller, with its note, on `resolve_merged(o.node)`
(a new open objection, which flags the node; a closed node is then a review item again, D.8.5),
and, when the earlier verdict was upheld and `o.node` is closed with `closure.upheld = Some(that
verdict)`, `CorrectionWithdrawn { o.node, outcome: corrected_from, or the outcome when it is None }`;
reply `ObjectionResolved { entry: Some(new objection), disputed: Some({objection, node, disputes,
earlier}), withdrawn }`, whose `why` the shell writes with the earlier verdict's author. In the
lab's fifth round (l5), two reviewers given one review reached opposite verdicts, and the later one
got a bare `{already: true}`; the dissent now stays visible, and a disputed claim reads as it was
closed, with an open objection, whichever verdict came first, until a third verdict decides it.
Otherwise `Appended(Resolve {
objection, upheld })` on its node and `ObjectionResolved { o, by, upheld }`. Anyone may resolve
(§11.3). 1.8: with `upheld` on a closed node, then `NodeCorrected { n, outcome, by, was }` with
`outcome := corrected_outcome(n.kind, was)`: `done` becomes `refuted` for kind `claim`
(`Outcome::Other`, the label `refuted`) and `failed` otherwise, any other outcome stays (the mark is
set all the same); 1.10: `was` is what a withdrawal restores, the outcome before the first
correction that still marks the node (`corrected_from` if marked, else the current outcome); the
reply names it, `corrected: {node, was, outcome}`. No counter moves (O2:
an outcome is neither content nor a close), and the citers of `n` are re-staled (D-4): a reference
that recorded `done`, or an open node, is now stale, so their nodes get `basis_changed`, one hop.
On an open node an upheld resolve records the verdict (`Upheld`) and nothing else; the holder closes
the node `failed` or `refuted`, as rule 10 says. Why a mark rather than a new life: a corrected
node must stay closed and out of `next` whatever flags it later carries, and the mark lives in the
closure, so a reopen, the only deliberate way back to work, drops it.

1.10 (§11.3, §21): a resolve that keeps the outcome (`upheld` false) of an open objection on a node
for which `query::no_basis(n)` is `Some(d)` (kind `claim`, closed `done`, no active decision, and
`d` its newest retracted decision, scanned as rule 10's `why` scans, D.8.26) warns `no_basis
{node, decision: d}`; the brief's header reads "closed done, decision dN retracted" from the same
function (D.8.6). In the lab's fifth round (l5), three reviewed lemmas whose deciding decisions the
objector had retracted read as plain `closed done` after verdicts that kept them. 1.11 (§11.3,
§24): `d` is `n.retracted_decision`, which `DecisionRetracted` sets on the node (D.4.3), or, for a
retraction recorded before 1.11, the scan of the resident decisions, the newer of the two; the
active decisions never leave memory (D.4.12), so "no active decision" reads the resident set. In the
lab's sixth round (l5), 1.10's scan found none: the retractions, 9 to 31 days old, had left memory.

**A deferral** (1.11, §10.3, §11.3). `talk resolve {objection, note, defer: true}`: after
`not_found(Objection)`, `defer` with `upheld` is `invalid(BadParams)` (the shell refuses it first,
naming both); of a resolved objection, `{already}` as for the same verdict, no event. Of an open
one: `Appended(Resolve { objection, upheld: false, deferred: true })` on `o.node`, by the caller,
its text the why, which marks the objection (`Objection::deferred`, which the brief's objection item
shows, D.11.7); and, when `o.node` is closed (the review), `Refused { o.node, class of the caller,
session, backoff_until: now + refusal.backoff, expires_at: now + refusal.ttl, quorum:
refusal.quorum }`, the record a `cannot` release makes (D.8.14), with no `e1_check`: `all_refused`
reads open nodes only, and a reopen runs `e1_check` (D.8.20). Reply `ObjectionResolved { entry:
Some(entry), deferred: Some({until: Some(backoff_until)}) }`, `until: None` on an open node, where
the holder decides the objection with its work and steps back, if it must, with a `cannot`
release. `next` and `hello`'s offers skip a candidate the caller's class is `excluded` from, status
and review items included (D.8.5), so the class is not given the review until the backoff ends, or,
at the quorum, until the refusals expire; `leave_better` leaves it out too (D.8.7). A verdict
recorded on a closed node, the `resolve` entry or a second verdict's `Appended(Object)`, ends with
`RefusalsCleared { node, by: that entry }` when the node has refusal records (`ix.refused`): the
review of a new objection, and the node's other flags, reach every class again. In the lab's sixth
round (l5), every reviewer found a review that neither held nor fell, and `next`, rule 13, and
`leave_better` gave it back, to the reviewer that had just declined it too.

**`talk retract {entry | path, text, reason}`.** The target exists (`not_found`): a node resolves,
or an entry has `eid < next_eid` and the node the shell added exists (D.4.5, D.5.2).
`Appended(Retract { target })` on the target's node, which puts the target into
`State::retracted`; if the target is an active decision, `DecisionRetracted { d, by, node: Some(the
decision's node) }`, which removes it from `ix.settling` and `ix.cited_by`, and (1.11) sets the
node's `retracted_decision`. A superseded decision cannot be retracted as a state change
(§25 has no superseded → retracted); the `retract` entry is still recorded, and the decision keeps
counting for the requests it lists (A-11). Every decision that cites the target directly gets
`basis_changed` (D-4, above); nothing propagates further by itself, and a settled request stays
settled (A-11). 1.12 (§9.3): if the target is an open question to a person, `withdraw_pq(q, by)`
(D.8.15): `PqWithdrawn { q, by }`, then `MarkSet { m, mark, q, off }` for the marks it set. A
withdrawn question is finished (D.4.12): `resolved` is true for every wait on it, its Recheck key
leaves the queue (`deadline_of` filters `Open`), so it never marks, expires, or escalates, and a
later `heard {answers}` is recorded and changes nothing (`answer_pq`). The reply names it,
`Retracted { entry, withdrawn: Some(q) }`. E1 (g) checks that no recheck of a withdrawn question is
queued and no wait on it is unresolved; its step clause that only a retract of it, while open,
withdraws it.

**Review view.** `view node {view: review}` is rendering only: the content (title, body, fields,
files, digest, status, closure) and the approve and object entries, without checkpoints, notes,
`said`, `heard`, and decisions (§11.3). `view node {view: full}` adds what rests on the node
(`query::backlinks`, D.8.25, CS-22), so a reviewer of a refuted result sees what depends on it.

### D.8.18 Recurring nodes, coverage, missed, overdue (§12, K6, R2)

**Slots** (`forum-cron`, D.11.10):

```rust
/// The first slot strictly after `after_ms`: the smallest UTC instant s > after_ms such that
/// s = earliest(local(d, h, m)) for a local date d and time h:m matching the cron, where
/// earliest() maps a local time to its first UTC instant, and a local time that does not exist
/// (a DST gap) has no instant. A local time that occurs twice (a fold) fires once, at its
/// earlier instant. Searches at most MAX_SEARCH_DAYS local days; None if there is no slot.
pub fn next_slot(cron: &CronSpec, tz: &TzTable, after_ms: u64) -> Option<u64>;
```

**Order.** Local time order is not UTC order in general, even taking the earliest instant of each
local time: where a fold reaches back past an earlier gap, a local time that the gap skipped first
happens after the fold, later in UTC than local times that follow it (the unit test
`a_fold_that_reaches_back_past_a_gap`: local 02:40 fires at 01:50Z, local 02:00 only at 03:40Z). So
`next_slot` does not walk local days. It walks the table's spans of constant offset in UTC order,
and within a span the local days and their matching minutes in ascending order, which are in UTC
order there. A candidate fires only when its instant is its local time's earliest
(`earliest_utc(tz, local) = Some(utc)`), so a local time that an earlier span already had, or that
lay before `after_ms`, does not fire again. The first candidate that fires is the smallest instant
after `after_ms` at which the schedule fires.

**Search window** (§12, 1.3). With `d0` the local day of `after_ms`, by the offset in force at
`after_ms`, the search covers every local time before local midnight at the start of day
`d0 + MAX_SEARCH_DAYS`, that is the local days `d0` to `d0 + 2,999`, in whichever span it occurs: a
span that starts in UTC after that midnight can still hold an earlier local time when its offset is
lower (the unit test `a_span_that_starts_after_the_limit_can_reach_back_before_it`). A span that
starts at or after that midnight read as UTC plus 26 hours is not entered, since no instant from
there on has a local time before it. With no slot in the window, `next_slot` returns `None`:
`create` and `update {repeat}` then refuse the schedule (`invalid(ScheduleNeverFires)`), and
`open_next_occurrence` closes the series as `failed` (below). The window covers 29 February across
a non-leap century year (2096 to 2104, 2,921 days), but not every expression that fires: under the
day rule of Vixie cron (D.11.10), `0 0 29 2 */7` is 29 February on a Sunday (2032, 2060, 2088, then
2128), so a series of it created in 2024 fires in 2032 and then closes as `failed`, and one created
from March 2032 to mid-December 2051 is refused.

**`open_next_occurrence(series, after)`:**

```
slot := next_slot(cron, tz, after)
if slot is None:                              // the schedule has no further slot (A-51)
    Appended(System(ScheduleEnded)) on series
    close_node(series, Failed, Server, None, Close, "the schedule has no further slot")
    return
name := slot_name(slot)                       // "YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ"; + "-<id>" if that name is live
NodeCreated { id, parent: series, name, origin: Occurrence, init: {
    title, body, needs, est: copied from the series (§12); capacity: 1; priority: 0; no tags;
    due: Some(slot + run_within) (A-57);
    keys: { repeat:<series>:<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ of slot> : NormVer(0) }, or {} if that key is
          already in ix.keys_open (defence in depth: agents cannot supply `repeat:` keys, A-90,
          so this never happens; omitting the key keeps K1 inside a firing that cannot fail);
    role: Occurrence { series, slot, window_end: slot + run_within, phase: Waiting,
                       window_fired: false } } }
```

The first slot is the first after creation; each next one is the first after `max(slot, close
time)`, so there is no catch-up. The close time is the closing event's `at`, a deadline's own time
when settling (§24: "cron slots are computed from the deadline's timestamp"). An occurrence is not a
candidate before its slot: its phase is `Waiting` until the OccurrenceSlot deadline fires.

**The copy at availability** (1.4, §12, §25, R10). When the OccurrenceSlot deadline fires, the
occurrence copies the series' `title`, `body`, `needs`, and `est` again, as they are then: the
firing emits `NodeUpdated { o, patch }` with the fields whose values differ from the occurrence's
(none: no event), then `OccurrenceAvailable { o }` (D.8.2), so the occurrence becomes a candidate
in the partition of its final `needs` and `est`. An edit of the series made while the occurrence
waited, such as the channel to post in, thus reaches the run whose slot has not come; in 1.3 it
reached only the run after next. An edit of those fields made to the waiting occurrence itself is
replaced by the copy, with no warning (§12, §20.2 say so: edits go on the series). O2 holds as for any update: `version` and `content_version` rise
when the title or body changes, and `needs` and `est` bump nothing. A series that was closed or lost
its `repeat` meanwhile has no waiting occurrence (it was dropped or detached), so the copy always
reads an open series. The cost is one node row per run, bounded by the open occurrences (K6); the
later option of occurrences that share their series' text (D.15.7) stays later.

**`close_node(n, outcome, by: Author, merged_into, cause: EndCause, text)`** is the one helper every
close goes through (agent close, merge, missed, refusal drop, series drop, signal resolution, a
schedule that ended):
0. `record_assumptions(n, by, text)` (D.8.17): a node with `proceed_on_assumption` records its
   assumptions in a decision before it closes, so no expired question is left without a mover on a
   closed node (A-104);
1. `Appended(System(Closed { outcome }))` on `n` (text: summary, verified, learnings);
2. `HoldEnded { t, EndedByClose(cause) }` for each live hold on `n`;
3. `IntentClosed { n, ResolvedByClose }` if `n`'s open intent belongs to the closing session (§5);
4. `MarkSet { n, Recheck, q, off }` for each recheck mark (§14: cleared by a close);
5. `NodeClosed { n, outcome, merged_into }` (evolve: wait cleared, `offer` removed, version + 1);
6. if `n` is a series: `close_node(o, Dropped, by, None, Close, …)` for its open occurrence, whatever
   its phase (A-14). `n` is already closed, so no next occurrence opens; `close_node` returns `o`,
   which `node close` and `node merge` report with the `series_stopped` warning (1.4, D.8.20);
7. if `n` is an occurrence whose series is open and is still a series: `SeriesOutcome { series,
   missed: outcome = Missed }`, then `open_next_occurrence(series, reslot.unwrap_or(max(slot,
   now)))`, where `reslot` is `Some(now)` only when `update {repeat}` drops a waiting occurrence;
8. if `n` is a signal node whose key is in `signals`: `SignalResolved { key }`.

The parent's `missed` flag follows `last_missed`, so it clears when a later occurrence closes with any
other outcome (§12).

**Missed** (`maybe_missed(o)`, at the window deadline and after every hold end on an occurrence that
leaves it open: lease expiry, release, and move; A-80):

```
if open(o) ∧ o.window_fired ∧ ix.node[o].live = 0 ∧ o.open_intent = None ∧ o.checkpoints = 0:
    close_node(o, Missed, Server, None, Close, "missed: no session took it within its window")
```

An occurrence with a checkpoint never closes as missed (R2); its `due` is its window end, so after
its window it carries `overdue` (A-57) until someone finishes it. A release always records a
checkpoint (A-9), so only a lease expiry or a move of a holder off it can lead to `missed` after a
hold. An occurrence with an open intent stays open with `open_intent` (and `overdue`).

**Coverage check** on `create` with `repeat` and on every `update` of `repeat` (§12):

```
coverage_at(s, repeat, now, next) -> Option<WarningDetail::UncoveredSlot>:
                                         // coverage(s, repeat, now): with next := next_slot(now)
    from  := now − coverage.window
    slots := next_slot from `from` repeatedly while < now, at most 50_000 slots
    covered(slot) := some minute m of stats.starts with slot ≤ m × 60_000 < slot + run_within
                     has a count > 0
    days  := the distinct local days (tz) of the slots; covered_days := days with a covered slot
    if days ≠ ∅ ∧ 2 × covered_days < days:           // "on most days no session started" (A-47)
        usual_hours := the three most frequent local hours (tz) of session starts in [from, now),
                       summed over the minutes of stats.starts, by count descending, then hour
                       ascending
        first_start := first_usual(tz, next, next + run_within, usual_hours)   // 1.4, R18
        return Some(UncoveredSlot { covered_days, days, usual_hours, first_start })

first_usual(tz, next, end, hours) -> Option<Time>:  // next: the slot of the series' next
                                                     // occurrence; end: its window's end
    (d, h) := forum_cron::local_day_hour(tz, next)
    if h ∈ hours: return Some(next)
    for i in 1..=72:                              // local hours after the slot's own, three days
        (d', h') := the local day and hour i hours after (d, h)
        if h' ∈ hours: if let Some(t) = forum_cron::earliest_utc(tz, local(d', h', 00)):
            return if t < end { Some(t) } else { None }   // a gap skips the hour (D.11.10);
                                                          // the first usual start is past the
                                                          // window: none falls inside
    None
```

The node is created either way; the warning says that something else must bring an agent then. Its
detail (1.4, §12, §21, R18) also says what to do, which the shell renders (D.11.7): set up an
outside trigger that brings an agent within the window, an external action recorded with an intent
(§10.2), or tell the requester when runs are likely to start; and it names that time, `first_start`,
the first usual start inside the next slot's window, as a local time in the series' zone, or, when
none falls inside, says that without an outside trigger that run will likely be missed. A usual hour
after the window's end is not named: the occurrence is `missed` by then, and a requester told that
time would be told wrong. `next` is the slot of the series' next occurrence: the waiting
occurrence's slot, else the schedule's first slot after `now` (on an open series whose occurrence is
available or held, which keeps the old schedule until its close, and on a closed series, which has
none).
The rule 3 item of the response then suggests the checkpoint with the intent at once (D.8.26). In
1.3 one agent ignored the warning, one could not tell whether a trigger would clear it, and one told
the requester 07:30 where the first run was likely about 08:05. The
check reads the per-minute counts of `stats.starts`, at most 40,320 of them over `coverage.window`,
so it costs the same at any number of sessions; over 1.1's list of starts it was 3.3 × 10⁷ entries
and about a second of writer time at 10,000 agents (CS-17, CS-21, review TP-15).

**Changing `repeat`** (A-75). Whether `repeat` changed is decided on its meaning, not on the stored
value: the parsed `cron`, `run_within`, the zone name, and the zone's offsets from `now` on (the
transitions at or after `now` and the offset in force at `now`). The shell rebuilds the `TzTable` on
every call with `from = now − coverage.window` (D.11.10), so comparing whole tables would treat every
re-sent, unchanged cron as a change. If none of those differs, `repeat` is left out of the
`NodePatch` (the stored text and table are kept); a change of zone rules alone (a tzdb update) is a
change.

On an open node:
- a new `repeat` on a series: `NodeUpdated` (the new repeat) first; then, if the open occurrence is
  still `Waiting`, `close_node(occ, Dropped, …)` with `reslot = Some(now)`, so the next occurrence
  follows the new schedule from now; an `Available` or held occurrence is kept and the new schedule
  applies from its close;
- removing `repeat` (`Change::Clear`): `NodeUpdated` makes the node plain; a `Waiting` occurrence is
  closed as `Dropped` (no next one opens); an `Available` or held one is `OccurrenceDetached` and
  becomes an ordinary node;
- adding `repeat` to a plain node opens its first occurrence after `now`.

On a closed node, a `repeat` change emits only `NodeUpdated` (the role and the repeat): a closed
series has no open occurrence (K6), and the first one opens when the node is reopened (`reopen` step
7, D.8.20). The coverage check still runs, since §12 asks for it on every update of `repeat`,
against the schedule's first slot after `now`, and may return `uncovered_slot`; it adds no event
(WP-D6). Skipping it until the series is reopened was the alternative; the literal §12 is kept.
Occurrence and signal nodes cannot get a `repeat` (`invalid(RoleConflict)`), nor can reserved nodes
(`invalid(ReservedNode)`).

**Reopening** (A-13, A-51): reopening a closed series opens a new occurrence after `now`. Reopening an
occurrence fails with `invalid(OccurrenceReopen)` while `occ_locked` holds (§12: the series always has
another open occurrence then). When the series is closed, or the node is no longer an occurrence of a
series, the reopen succeeds and `OccurrenceDetached` (emitted before `NodeReopened`, so no occurrence
deadline of a past slot is ever queued, D.4.8) makes it an ordinary node, so K6 counts it no longer.
The same holds for taking a flagged closed occurrence.

### D.8.19 Signals (§14, S1)

```
open_signal(kind, x, y) -> Option<NodeId>:
    if x = y: return None
    key := SignalKey { kind, a: min(x, y), b: max(x, y) }
    if signals[key] = id: return Some(id)                                   // S1
    NodeCreated { id, parent: SIGNALS, name: "<kind>-<a>-<b>-<id>", origin: Signal, init: {
        title: "<kind>: #<a> and #<b>", tags: {offer}, capacity: 1,
        links: {(Duplicate | ConflictsWith, a), (Duplicate | ConflictsWith, b)},
        role: Signal(key) } }
    SignalOpened { key, id }
    return Some(id)
```

The name contains the new node's own id, so it never collides. Signal nodes are server-made, so they
do not count against `tree.max_children` (A-28) and creating one never fails.

Creation sites: create-or-join (each other open carrier), `node key {add}` with a key another open
node carries, `reopen` (each dropped key), and `node link` with `duplicate` or `conflicts_with`.

A signal resolves when its node closes (`close_node` emits `SignalResolved`), which happens (A-34):
- when one node of the pair is merged into the other (`merge`, step 7; §14 "once its pair is
  merged"). A merge of one of them into a third node leaves the signal open: whoever takes it follows
  `merged_into`;
- when a `superseded_by` link is added between the pair, in either direction ("linked as resolved");
- when a decision is recorded on the signal node ("covered by a decision");
- when anyone closes the signal node.

Server-made resolutions close the signal node with outcome `Done` and author `Server`.

**Reopening a signal node** (`node reopen`, or `take`/`next` of a flagged closed signal node; A-89).
The node keeps role `Signal(key)` while closed, but its key has left `signals`. In `reopen`:
- if `signals` has no entry for `key`: `SignalOpened { key, n }` after `NodeReopened`, so the
  reopened node is the pair's open signal again (S1);
- otherwise (another signal for the pair was opened meanwhile): `SignalDetached { n }` before
  `NodeReopened`, so the node reopens as an ordinary node and the pair keeps one open signal.

S1's state check ("`signals` equals the set of open signal nodes with their keys") covers both
branches.

### D.8.20 Update, link, close, reopen, move, merge, hide (§5, §16)

**`node update {path, version, digest_version?, token?, …}`.** Validation: `at` resolves → a given
token is a live hold on `n` (`stale_token`) → shape: `title` present and empty
(`invalid(EmptyText(Title))`), `digest` too long (`invalid(DigestTooLong)`), `digest` present
without `digest_version` (`invalid(MissingDigestVersion)`, CS-11), a `repeat` with `run_within = 0`
or a bad tz table → `depends_on` and `owners` resolve (`not_found(Node)`) → `version ≠ n.version`, or
`digest_version` given and `≠ n.digest_version` (`stale_version`; O2: "an edit with a stale version
or digest version changes nothing"; A-4, CS-11) → `capacity` or `repeat` on a reserved node
(`invalid(ReservedNode)`), `repeat` on an occurrence or signal (`invalid(RoleConflict)`), a `repeat`
with no slot (`invalid(ScheduleNeverFires)`), a new `depends_on` edge closing a cycle (`cycle`, T5) →
`capacity < ix.node[n].live` (`full`, H1) → L1 for a new occurrence, when `n` is open
(`limit(Depth)`). Execution: `NodeUpdated { n, patch }` with only the fields whose value differs
(`repeat` by A-75's comparison; `tags` and `needs` as the sets that result from removing
`tags_remove` and then adding `tags_add`, and likewise for needs, CS-34; none: no event); then the
coverage warning for a changed `repeat` (§12: "on every update of `repeat`"), on an open node only,
the occurrence consequences of D.8.18 (on a closed node the occurrence opens at reopen, K6), and, when
`needs` changed on a node in `ix.refused`, `e1_check(n)` (an added need can shrink the active classes,
D.8.14, CS-7). Counter rules (O2, A-3): `version` increases iff title, body, fields, files, or status
changed, and `content_version` follows it iff title, body, fields, or files changed (CS-34);
`digest_version` iff the digest changed; kind, tags (including `offer`, A-2), capacity, priority,
est, needs, due, depends_on, owners, repeat, and agreements change neither. `owners` may be set on a
reserved node too: ROOT's owners are the forum's (D.2.2). Reply `Updated { version,
digest_version }`.

**Why `digest_version` is required with a digest** (CS-11, review RS-15). The digest bumps only
`digest_version` (A-3), and 1.1's `update` carries only `version`, so two agents that read the same
node and each rewrite its digest both succeed, and the first summary is lost without a warning: on a
hot node with one digest edit a minute, 63 % of edits race. A patch that sets `digest` must now carry
`digest_version`, and a stale one is `stale_version` like a stale `version`, which is §0's protection
against lost updates for the field a stranger reads first.

**Why tags and needs are added and removed** (CS-34, review FS-12). Tags and needs bump no counter
(A-2, A-3), so a patch that replaced the whole set lost concurrent edits silently: two agents that
read a node without tags, one adding `offer` and one adding `needs-review`, left it without `offer`,
not a candidate and without a flag, so nothing would ever move it and M1b could not see it. Additions
and removals of single labels commute, so the order of two such patches does not matter, and no
version is needed for them. The scalar settings (kind, capacity, priority, est, due) stay last writer
wins, as 1.1 has them.

**`node link {path, rel, to}`.** Both resolve; `at = to` → `invalid(SelfLink)`. An identical link →
reply `Linked { existing: true, signal: None }`. Otherwise `LinkAdded` (version + 1); then
`duplicate` → `open_signal(Duplicate, at, to)`; `conflicts_with` → `open_signal(Conflict, at, to)`;
`superseded_by` → resolve the open signals of the pair (both kinds). Reply `Linked`.

**`node close {path, outcome, summary, verified?, settles?, learnings?, token?, unsent?}`.**
Validation: `at` resolves → a given token is a live hold on `n` (`stale_token`) → `outcome = Missed`
(`invalid(ServerOutcome)`) → empty summary (`invalid(EmptyText(Summary))`) → `settles` are requests
(`not_found(Request)`) → `unsent` are `said` entries (`not_found(Said)`) → reserved
(`invalid(ReservedNode)`) → already closed (`invalid(AlreadyClosed)`, A-66) → an occurrence in phase
`Waiting` with an outcome other than `dropped` (`invalid(OccurrenceNotYetAvailable)`: §25 allows
only waiting → dropped, A-91). Execution:
1. if `settles` is non-empty: steps 1, 3, and 4 of `talk decide` on `n` with the summary as the
   decision's text and no basis (§5: "the summary is recorded as a decision that settles them");
   that decision also records `n`'s assumptions (A-15);
2. for each pending `said` of the session, ascending: `SaidConfirmed { x, Close, link: None }` when
   it is not in `unsent`, and `SaidUnconfirmed { x }` when it is, or `SaidWithheld { x }` when a
   later `said` replaced it (§9.2, 1.5, 1.9; as a release's step 7);
3. warnings, evaluated now: `unsettled_requests`, `open_commitments`, `open_objections` (the flags
   stay); `agreement` for `n` (`current_approvals(n)`, CS-34); `held_by_other` (live holds of other
   sessions on `n`, and, when `n` is a series, on the open occurrence that `close_node` step 6 drops,
   A-14);
4. `close_node(n, outcome, Session(sess), None, Close, summary + verified + learnings)`;
5. if `n` was a series and step 6 of `close_node` dropped its open occurrence `o`: warning
   `series_stopped { occurrence: o }` (1.4, §12, R2). It is a warning only: the close is applied,
   and no further occurrence opens until the series is reopened. In 1.3 agents that had set up a
   reminder closed its series as finished, which stopped it silently; the instructions' "(series:
   release)" (§22, R1) and rule 8's release of a container are the other guards.

Reply `Closed { node, decision, settled, dropped: o or None, leave_better: leave_better(s, Some(n),
None) }` (1.4: `dropped`, R9).

**`node reopen {path, reason}`.** Validation: `at` resolves → open (`invalid(NotClosed)`) →
`occ_locked(n)` (`invalid(OccurrenceReopen)`). `reopen(n, reason)`, shared with `take` and `next` of
a flagged closed node (reason "taken"):
1. `dropped := { (k, o) : k ∈ n.keys, ix.keys_open[k] = o ≠ n }`; `KeyRemoved { n, k }` for each (K7);
2. role fix-ups while `n` is still closed: if `n` is an occurrence, `OccurrenceDetached { n }`
   (A-13); if `n` is a signal node whose key another node now holds in `signals`,
   `SignalDetached { n }` (A-89). Both come before `NodeReopened`, so no deadline of a past slot is
   ever queued (D.4.8) and no second open signal exists for one key;
3. `NodeReopened { n }` (life open, `merged_into` gone, version + 1; it may take the parent past
   `tree.max_children`, which only `create` and `move` check, CS-10);
4. if `n` is still a signal node (its key is free): `SignalOpened { key, n }` (A-89, S1);
5. `open_signal(Duplicate, n, o)` for each dropped key; `Appended(System(KeysDropped { keys }))` if
   any;
6. `Appended(System(Reopened))` on `n` (text: the reason);
7. if `n` is a series: `open_next_occurrence(n, now)`;
8. `e1_check(n)`;
9. (`node reopen` only, 1.12, §16) `OfferSet { n, on }` unless `n` carries `offer` already or is a
   container, as at a hold's end (D.8.10 step 5): in the lab's seventh round (it6 l5), four
   reopened claims carried neither a flag nor the tag, and nothing offered them; a take that
   reopens a node holds it, and adds none;
10. warning `duplicate_key` listing the dropped `(k, o)`.

Reply `Reopened { node, dropped_keys, offered }` (1.12: `offered`, step 9).

**`node move {path, to}`.** Validation: `at` resolves → reserved (`invalid(ReservedNode)`) → the new
parent (its missing steps become ancestors) is `n` or inside `n`'s subtree (`cycle`, K4) → the final
name is live at the new parent (`invalid(NameTaken)`) → L1 (`limit(Depth | Children)`; no child
limit when the new parent is PEOPLE or TEAMS, A-113). Moving onto the node's own current place is a
no-op success. Execution: `NodeCreated` for missing ancestors; `NodeMoved { n, parent, name }` (the
old name becomes an alias; a path is not content, so version is unchanged, A-3; the live holds
still on `n` carry its attendance to the new parent, D.7.4); `HoldEnded { t, EndedByClose(Move) }`
for every live hold of another session on `n` (A-6: "that holder's later writes become late";
evolve counts an attempt for a hold without a checkpoint, A-9, and tags `offer` unless `n` is a
container, judged at its new place, §10.3, A-113); `Appended(System(Moved { from }))` on `n`; if
holds ended and `n` is an occurrence, `maybe_missed(n)` (A-80). Warning `held_by_other` naming
those sessions. Reply `Moved { node }`.

`NodeMoved` comes before the `HoldEnded` events so that `is_container` reads the node's new parent
(D.14.2, confirmed on 2026-10-02). With the old order, a work node created by mistake under
`@people`, held by one session and moved to `/work` by another, lost that hold without an `offer`
tag and became an ordinary node with no flag, which `next` would never offer again: the case A-6's
offer-on-move exists for. A node moved into `@people` gets no tag, which is harmless either way.

**`node merge {from, into}`.** Validation: both resolve → `from = into` (`invalid(SelfMerge)`) →
either reserved (`invalid(ReservedNode)`) → `into` closed, merged ones included (`closed`, K5) →
`from` closed (`invalid(MergeFromClosed)`, A-33) → `from` an occurrence in phase `Waiting`
(`invalid(OccurrenceNotYetAvailable)`: closing it as superseded is not a §25 transition, A-91) →
`into` the open occurrence of `from`, a series (`invalid(MergeIntoOwnOccurrence)`, 1.5: closing
`from` would drop it, and with it the keys and marks the merge moved there, against N5) → with `E'`
the edges after replacing `from` by `into` and dropping self-edges, `E'` must be acyclic
(`cycle`, N5, T5). Execution:
1. for each key of `from`: `KeyRemoved { from, k }`, then `KeyAdded { into, k }` (N5);
2. what is still open moves to `into`, keeping its id, with `moved_from` set (§16, N5, A-94):
   `RequestMoved { r, into }` for each unsettled request; `PqMoved { q, into }` for each people
   question that is `Open`, `Expired`, or `Escalated` (N5's "open questions": not yet answered or
   superseded); `CommitmentMoved { c, into }` for each open commitment; `ObjectionMoved { o, into }`
   for each open objection; `SaidMoved { x, into }` for each `Pending` or `Unconfirmed` `said` (the
   conversation's key has just moved to `into`); for each assume or recheck mark `(m, q)` on `from`,
   `MarkSet { from, m, q, off }` and `MarkSet { into, m, q, on }`; and, if `from` has an open intent
   that is not the merging session's and `into` has none, `IntentMoved { from, into }`. Settled and
   closed items, confirmed `said` entries, agent questions (addressed messages, already delivered),
   and an intent that cannot move stay on `from` (an intent left there is reported by `health` as
   M1b; `node reopen` of `from` reaches it);
3. for each moved request `r` still unanswered that is not a user request: if `into` has a `said` of
   kind reply, result, or correction with `conv = r.conv` and eid `a > r`, `RequestAnswered { r, by:
   min such a }`, then `try_settle(r)` (A-95; a `said` of another conversation answers nothing,
   §9.4, 1.3);
4. `Appended(System(MergedFrom { from, last_checkpoint }))` on `into` (text: `from`'s digest);
5. for each `w ∈ waiters[Node(from)]`: `WaitSet { w, Some(Node(into)) }`, or `WaitSet { w, None }`
   when `w = into` (self-edge dropped); for each `d ∈ dependents[from]`: `DependsRedirected { d, from,
   Some(into) }`, or `None` when `d = into`;
6. `close_node(from, Superseded, Session(sess), Some(into), Merge, "merged into #<into>")` (its live
   holds end; `held_by_other` for other sessions' holds; a series `from` drops its open occurrence,
   with the `series_stopped` warning, as a close does, 1.4, R2);
7. resolve the open signals of the pair `{from, into}` (both kinds).

After the merge `from` carries nothing that needs a mover except an intent that could not move, and
`next` never offers it (D.8.5), so no agent reopens a merge by accident. Links pointing at `from` are
not rewritten; readers follow `merged_into` (§16). Reply `Merged { from, into }`.

**`node hide {entry | file, reason}`.** The entry exists (`eid < next_eid`, `not_found(Entry)`, with
its node added by the shell, D.4.5), or the node exists and has that name in `Node::files`
(`not_found(Node)`); `reason` non-empty. A file named in a
checkpoint's `files` is part of that entry's text, so it is hidden with `hide {entry}` (A-97).
Events: `Hidden { target, reason }`;
`Appended(System(Hidden(target)))` on the target's node (text: the reason). The core never reads
hidden status (O3); the shell renders `[hidden: reason]` (§16). Reply `Hidden`.

### D.8.21 Pause (§19, P1, P2)

```
paused(n, now) := ∃ a ∈ ancestors_or_self(n): pauses[a].until > now
```

**`control pause {scope, reason}`.** `scope` resolves (`not_found(Node)`); `reason` non-empty.
`Paused { scope, until: now + pause.ttl, ttl: pause.ttl, by: sess, class: class(sess), renewed:
pauses contains scope }` (pausing again renews, §19, and the renewer becomes the pause's source);
`Appended(System(Paused { until }))` on the scope (text: the reason). Reply `Paused { scope, until,
renewed }`. The scope is a node id, so it follows moves (A-72).

**`control unpause {scope}`.** `scope` resolves; an active pause exists there (`not_found(Pause)`).
`Unpaused { scope }`; `Appended(System(Unpaused))` on the scope. Anyone may lift it. Reply
`Unpaused { scope }`.

Expiry is the Pause deadline (`PauseExpired`). A pause stops new holds only: `take` fails with
`paused`, `create` issues no hold (`no_hold(Paused)` and the `offer` tag), `next` skips the subtree;
checkpoints, renewals, releases, and every deadline continue (P2). `next` skips it without testing
each candidate: setting a pause moves the candidates under its scope into `ix.next.held`, and lifting
or expiring it moves back those no other pause covers (CS-16, D.8.5); on a settled state the active
pauses are exactly those in `pauses`, so this agrees with `paused(n, now)`.

**A pause is seen** (CS-9, FQ-3, review FS-7). At 10⁸ to 4 × 10⁸ sessions a year, a mistaken pause
of `/` once in a million sessions is 88 to 438 such pauses a year, each stopping every team for up to
`pause.ttl` while 1.1's `health` stays green (an idle swarm with a backlog trips neither
`Overloaded` nor `Underused`), the status line says `PAUSED` with no source or reason, and a renewal
every 110 minutes keeps one in place for ever. The rule stays as §19 has it: anyone can stop work,
and it was decided to keep it so (FQ-3). What changes is that every pause is seen:
- `control health` reports `Paused`, red when the scope is ROOT or excludes at least
  `PAUSE_RED_PERMILLE` of the candidates (D.8.22), so it also heads the status line's health;
- the status line names the ROOT pause and every pause covering the session's holds with its source
  (class and session), its end, and its reason (D.11.7);
- an empty `next` that pauses caused names them and says to lift a pause whose reason no longer
  holds (`EmptyWhy::pause_scopes`, D.8.5).

The alternative the review offered was declined (FQ-3, D.14): a pause of `/`, or of a scope
that excludes more than 10 % of the candidates, lasting `pause.broad_ttl` (15 min) unless a second,
distinct session renews it.

### D.8.22 Health and capacity (§17)

```rust
pub struct Health { pub level: Level, pub reasons: Vec<HealthReason>, pub capacity: CapacityReport }
pub enum Level { Green, Yellow, Red }
/// Every reason that holds, each with its own level (`HealthReason::level()`: the stored `level`
/// of the three counted reasons and of `Overloaded` (1.5), computed as below; otherwise the fixed
/// one, red for `FlagsPilingUp`, yellow for `WriteSurge` and `Underused`), sorted red first and
/// then in declaration order: the status line shows the first (CS-9). A reason about many objects
/// carries their count and at most HEALTH_TOP of them, never one item per object (CS-9, FS-8).
pub enum HealthReason {
    /// Active pauses, those that exclude the most candidates first (CS-9, FQ-3).
    Paused { level: Level, count: u32, top: Vec<PauseExclusion> },
    /// Objects whose mover is unreachable (M1b, D.9.3, A-54).
    NoMover { level: Level, count: u32, top: Vec<MoverGap> },
    /// Candidates no session profile seen within capacity.window could take (CS-9, RS-18).
    Unreachable { level: Level, count: u32, by_needs: u32, by_horizon: u32,
                  top: Vec<(NodeId, UnreachableBy)> },
    /// Flagged nodes that are not waiting keep growing (CS-31): the count at the window's start,
    /// and now.
    FlagsPilingUp { start: u32, now: u32 },
    /// `oldest` (1.6): the oldest candidate for `next` that nothing holds back, whose age makes
    /// the level, ties by `Cand`; the status line names it.
    Overloaded { level: Level, demand_min: u64, supply_min: u64, idle_permille: u32,
                 oldest: Option<Cand> },  // 1.5, 1.6
    /// Added by the shell, which alone counts writes per class (CS-29, D.11.2).
    WriteSurge { class: ClassName, last_hour: u32, baseline: u32 },
    Underused { idle_permille: u32 },
}
pub struct PauseExclusion { pub pause: PauseView, pub excluded: u32 }      // PauseView: D.8.25
pub enum UnreachableBy { Needs, Horizon }
pub struct CapacityReport {
    pub demand_min: u64, pub supply_min: u64, pub lost_min: u64, pub next_calls: u32,
    pub next_empty: u32, pub next_empty_for_you: u32,
    pub idle_permille: Option<u32>,            // None: no `next` call in the window (1.5)
    pub backlog: u32, pub flagged_active: u32, pub median_done_min: u64,
}
/// An object with no mover that the server cannot prevent (M1b, D.9.3).
pub enum MoverGap {
    NodeWait { node: NodeId, target: NodeId },      // a {node} wait whose target has no mover
    Dependency { node: NodeId, target: NodeId },    // the same for depends_on
    FlaggedUnreachable { node: NodeId, flags: FlagSet },  // a mover flag on a node no one can take
}
```

**Counts and shares, not red when any** (CS-9, review FS-8). §17's "some `needs` cannot be met" and
"some object has no mover" are red as soon as one object anywhere is affected. With 10⁵ objects and
one in 10⁴ affected, `health` is then red with certainty, and a `health` that is always red says
nothing. `NoMover` is red only when its count reaches `RED_SHARE_PERMILLE` (1 %) of its population,
or by age (below), and yellow otherwise:

```
age_level(oldest) :=
    Red    if oldest ≤ now − capacity.window
    Yellow otherwise, or with no oldest time
share_level(count, population, oldest) :=
    Red    if count ≥ 1 ∧ 1000 × count ≥ RED_SHARE_PERMILLE × population
    age_level(oldest) if count ≥ 1
```

A share alone would let up to 1 % of the population wait for ever below red: 10³ candidates at 10⁵
that no profile can take, `{node}` waits on targets that never close, dependencies on them. So a
counted reason is also red once its oldest item has been in it for `capacity.window`, where the item
carries a time: for `Unreachable`, `oldest_in` of each unreachable partition, the `since` of its
first node or status entry of each tier (a partition is ordered by tier, then hour group, D.8.5, so
this is its oldest up to priority, and a young candidate of a higher tier hides no older one); for
`NoMover`, the waiting node's `wait.set_at`, or a dependent's `since` (a `FlaggedUnreachable` gap
carries none and counts by share only). Below red, an empty `next` names the first yellow reason and
its first item (D.8.5), so idle agents read it; and the no-user profile of the year simulation
reports the objects that waited longer than `capacity.window` (D.15.4).

**Red by age alone** (1.5, the final usability round). With the share, a small forum (one bad
object among fewer than 100) was red exactly as in 1.1, and so was a young one: in the final round,
117 of the 119 sessions that used the forum saw `health red`, from `Unreachable` at one node of a
few candidates and from `Overloaded` once a first `next` found work before any hold had made
progress, while constitution line 9 told agents to fix the first red reason before other work.
`Unreachable` and `Overloaded` therefore have no share: `Unreachable`'s level is
`age_level(oldest)`, and `Overloaded`'s is `age_level` of the oldest candidate for `next` that
nothing holds back, `oldest_in` over every partition with its routing items, one range query per
tier and partition. A candidate held back for every caller (a pause, a dependency) is not
`Overloaded`'s item: `Paused` and `NoMover` report it. At scale, an `Unreachable` that matters
turns red within `capacity.window` of its first item, and so does the backlog of a swarm that is
really overloaded; until then both are yellow, which the status line and an empty `next` show. `NoMover` keeps its share: the
final round showed no red from it.

The reasons, over the days of `stats.days` within `capacity.window` before `now`, with backlog = the
number of `Cand::Node` and `Cand::Status` candidates (`ix.next.nodes`, CS-21):
- **`Paused`** (CS-9): every active pause with `excluded`, the candidates `ix.next.held` attributes to
  its scope (CS-16); red if a pause is at ROOT, or excludes at
  least one candidate with `1000 × excluded ≥ PAUSE_RED_PERMILLE × backlog`, else yellow. The shell
  renders each pause's reason (D.4.6);
- **`NoMover`**: `m1b_gaps(s, now)` (D.9.3); `share_level(count, |ix.flagged|, oldest)`;
- **`Unreachable`** (CS-9, review RS-18): a candidate is unreachable when no profile of
  `stats.profiles` has `n.needs ⊆ caps` and (`est` or the profile's largest horizon absent, or
  `n.est <= ` that horizon); `by: Needs` when no profile meets the needs, else `Horizon`;
  `age_level(oldest since)` (1.5; before, `share_level` over the backlog). It replaces 1.1's `UnmetNeeds` (needs only) and adds
  horizons: work longer than every session's horizon, which `next` excludes for every caller,
  otherwise starves while `health` stays green. It is computed per partition of `ix.next`, and per
  candidate only in a partition whose `est` bucket straddles the largest fitting horizon (CS-21).
  The profiles are first reduced to one per caps set, with the largest horizon seen for it, and
  indexed by label: a partition's needs are met by the caps sets in the intersection of its labels'
  lists, shortest list first, so a partition costs O(the shortest list), and the whole reason
  O(partitions × the shortest list) at most once per `HEALTH_REFRESH`; with 10⁶ distinct horizons
  and 10⁴ caps sets, testing every partition against every profile was 10³ × 10⁶ tests on the
  writer every 10 s. 1.1's `UnmetNeeds` tested every candidate against every session started within
  `capacity.window`, 10⁴ × 8 × 10⁶ tests at 10,000 agents, so `control health` never returned
  (review TP-15);
- **`FlagsPilingUp`** (red, CS-31): with `f(d)` the `flagged_end` of day `d` (carried forward over
  days without an entry; a day's entry holds the count it began with when no flag changed that day,
  so a recorded 0 is a value, D.4.9; the earliest day kept stands for the window's start) and
  `f(now) = |ix.flagged_active|`: `f(now) > f(start) + max(FLAGS_GROWTH_MIN, f(start) ×
  FLAGS_GROWTH_PERMILLE / 1000)`, and `f` grew on each of the last `FLAGS_GROWTH_DAYS` days. 1.1's
  "raised exceeds cleared" is the change of the count over the window, which a healthy, stationary
  swarm shows on half of its days (FS-8);
- demand `= Σ demand_min` (each candidate's `est`, or the median of `stats.done_minutes`, or
