| H2 | S + St | S: for each session: count its live holds (by `Hold::session`, the taker); at most `params.hold_per_session`; every hold's taker is in `sessions`, with `retire_at > taken_at + terms.ceiling` (CS-8: a retired session holds nothing), and is not `silent` (1.4, §3, §26 H2, R27: a silent session holds no live hold, so a holder never sees `STALE SESSION`; every hold in the map is live on a settled state, T3). St: `SessionRetired` only for a session with no hold, and every `HoldIssued` in a command step is preceded in that step by a `Touched` or by the `SessionOpened` of its session (D.8.23) | `inv_H2`, `step_H2` (the `holds` slice with retirement, and, 1.4, a checkpoint within a tick of the take) | `hold_cmds_preserve_h`, `session_retire`, `silence_after_leases` (1.4) |
| H3 | S + St | S: every hold's `token.fence <= nodes[token.node].fence`. St: every `HoldIssued` has `fence = before.fence + 1` for its node, so no token repeats | `inv_H3`, `step_H3` | `hold_cmds_preserve_h` |
| H4 | St | Preconditions (A-105, A-114): `cmd.longest_text() <= before.params.text_max`, `ctx.op` is not in `before.ops`, the session resolves (or is new), and the target exists. Then, if a write (`checkpoint`, `renew`, `release`, `update {token}`, `close {token}`) carries a token that is not a live hold on its target in `before`: the outcome is `stale_token`, the events are exactly one `Appended(Late)` on the target (plus `PrincipalSeen`, `SessionOpened`, and `OpRecorded` if present), and the base state of `after` equals that of `before` except that entry, the node's `seq`, the counters, `last_now`, `ops` and `notes` (what expired by the event's time leaves them, CS-8, CS-17), and, on a first call, the new session and its interned principal (`sessions`, `principal_ids`; opening a session no longer touches `classes`, CS-7): holds, versions, digest versions, fences, content, and every entity map are equal. `ix` and `stats` are derived and not compared. A stale write with a text over `text.max` (answered by L1's text half, before O1), a retried stale write (answered by O1), an unknown session, and an unknown target append no late entry; `step_H4` has a case for each | `step_H4` | `stale_token_only_late` |
| H5 | S + St | S: for each hold, with its own `terms` (the lease parameters in force at issue, A-102): `taken_at < lease_until <= min(taken_at + ceiling, last_extended + max)`; `¬checkpointed ⇒ lease_until <= taken_at + first`; `renews <= renew_max`. St: every `HoldIssued` carries the terms of the params in force | `inv_H5` | `lease_issue_h5`, `lease_extend_h5`, `renew_limit` |
| H6 | S | No hold is on a closed node | `inv_H6` | `close_ends_holds` |
| O1 | S + St | St, for a command with `cmd.longest_text() <= before.params.text_max` (a longer one is answered before the retry store, and L1's text half checks it, A-114): with `ctx.op` and a live record `r = before.ops[(class, op)]` (`r.expires_at > now`): the same digest from no session or from `r.session` ⇒ no events, `after = before`, reply `Replay`; another digest, or another session ⇒ no events, `op_id_conflict` (CS-8). Without a live record: with events, `after.ops[(class, op)] = {digest, session, expires_at: now + op.retain}`, and `OpRecorded`, carrying exactly the returned outcome, is the last event; with no events, `after.ops = before.ops` (no record, A-106). Under `SessionCtx::System` there is never an `OpRecorded`. S: every stored record has `expires_at > last_now` (evolve drops the others, CS-8) | `step_O1`, `inv_O1` (with expiry) | `op_retry_no_effect`, `op_expiry` |
| O2 | S + St | S: per node, every kept entry's `seq <= node.seq`, and `ix.people` holds exactly its kept people entries (the full feed's gapless seqs are the shell's: `UNIQUE (node, seq)` of the `entries` table and the history-replay test, CS-17); `fence >=` every fence of its holds; `version >= 1`. St, per node and per event: `version` rises by 1 exactly for `KeyAdded`, `KeyRemoved`, `LinkAdded`, `NodeClosed`, `NodeReopened`, and a `NodeUpdated` that changes title, body, fields, files, or status (whose values then differ between `before` and `after`), and stays put otherwise; `digest_version` rises by 1 exactly for a `NodeUpdated` that changes the digest, and only in a command whose `digest_version` equals the node's in `before` (an `update` that sets `digest` without one is `invalid(MissingDigestVersion)` and changes nothing, CS-11); `seq` by 1 per `Appended`; `fence` by 1 per `HoldIssued`; `content_version` (not a §5 counter) becomes the new `version` exactly at a `NodeUpdated` that changes title, body, fields, or files, and stays put otherwise (CS-34); a `stale_version` outcome has no events except `PrincipalSeen`, `SessionOpened`, and `OpRecorded` | `inv_O2`, `step_O2` | `version_bumps_o2` |
| O3 | St | Every entry of `before.entries` is in `after.entries` unchanged, except metadata that left memory by the prune of D.4.12 (its leaving time plus FINISHED_RETAIN at or before an event of the step), and every entry of `after.entries` not in `before.entries` was appended or restored (`Restored`) by the step; `before.retracted ⊆ after.retracted` (D-4); `after.counters.events = before.counters.events + events.len()`. The history's prefix property is the shell's: it only inserts into the history tables, whose triggers abort any update or delete (D.11.6, FQ-2). The core stores no hidden status, so nothing in `decide`, `settle`, or `evolve` can read it (structural) | `step_O3` (in every slice) | *structural: the core has no hidden status to read, and the prefix property is the shell's append-only history; the step check runs in every test* |
| R1 | S | `s.ix == recount(s, now)` over the resident state (D.4.12) for every index except `flags` (F) and `deadlines` (T4): the open subsets of `items` (CS-20) with `stale_basis` (D-4) and `requesters_by_age`, `people` (CS-17), `ix.next` with its needs trie (CS-16) and its `waiting` set (1.4, §10.4), `backlinks` and `cited_by` (CS-22, filed through `resolve_merged`), each node's `sub` (CS-32), `attended_children`, the `unheld_flagged` sets, `flagged_occurrences` (WP-D6), `person_of` and `aliases_of`, `branch_notes`, `profiles_by_time`, `class_ends`, and `leaving_by_time` included; the key set of `ix.next.of` equals that of `State::since`, each `CandAt.since` is `since[c]`, and every `since <= now` | *the model has no indices* | `evolve_no_panic_*` (each ends with "indices equal the recount"), `subtree_rollup_move`, `basis_stale_refresh` |
| Total | S | `anomalies == 0` | *the model applies transitions directly and has no `evolve` preconditions* | `evolve_counts_anomalies` |
| K1 | S | For each key: the open nodes carrying it (over `nodes[*].keys`, not `ix.keys_open`) number at most 1 | `inv_K1` | `keys_open_unique` |
| K2 | S | Over every stored key and every resident request's origin (§26 K2: "and so does every request's origin"; an origin is a `Key` with its version, D.2.4). Core part: every `NormVer(0)` key or origin is a canonical `user:e<n>` with `e < counters.next_eid`, or a key `repeat:<id>:<slot>` naming a series; no key or origin of another version has the `repeat` scheme (A-90). The user entry itself is not required to be resident: a routed entry whose request settled leaves memory while its node keeps the `user:e<n>` key for good (D.4.12), and every state invariant ranges over the resident state. Shell part: `check_keys` (on replay, with `--check`, and in `forum-server check`) asserts `forum_keys::normalise_v(nv, k) == k` for every other key and resident origin, and `forum-server check` also runs it over the `origins` table, the origins that left memory, and confirms that every `NormVer(0)` `user:e<n>` key or origin has a `from_user` row for `e` in its `entries` table | *keys are model atoms (D.10.6)* | *a shell property: the proptests of `forum-keys`* |
| K3 | S | `names` and `aliases` have disjoint key sets; every non-root node's `place` is in `names` and maps to it; every `names` value has that place; every alias target exists | `inv_K3` | `move_keeps_tree` |
| K4 | S | From every node, the parent walk reaches ROOT within `nodes.len()` steps | `inv_K4` | `move_keeps_tree` |
| K5 | S | `merged_into = Some(m)` only on closed nodes with outcome `Superseded`; following `merged_into` from any node ends within `nodes.len()` steps at a node with `merged_into = None` | `inv_K5` | `merge_redirects` |
| K6 | S | Count the nodes with role `Occurrence { series: x }` that are open: an open series has exactly one; a closed series has none (A-13: a detached occurrence has role `Plain`) | `inv_K6` | `occurrence_close_reopen` |
| K7 | St | For every node reopened by the step (`reopen`, or `take`/`next` of a closed node): `keys(after) = { k ∈ keys(before) : no other node carries k openly in before }` | `step_K7` | `reopen_keys_k7` |
| K8 | S | For each reserved id 0..=7 (D.2.2): the node exists with origin `Reserved`, is open, its `place` equals its Genesis place (ROOT none; `@user`, `sys`, `@people`, and `@teams` under ROOT; `decisions` and `digest` under `@user`; `signals` under `sys`; D.7.4), its capacity is 0, its role is `Plain` (no `repeat`), and its `keys` are empty; no other node has origin `Reserved` (§4, §26 K8, A-29). O(1), so `check_startup` runs it at every startup (§24, A-118). §21 maps every reserved-node refusal but the conversation and request cases (C1) to it: a move, a merge of either side, a close, a capacity or `repeat` change, a key, and a routing to a reserved node are `invalid(ReservedNode)` | `inv_K8` (in every slice; the `keys`, `holds`, `recurring`, and `user` slices aim their move, merge, close, key, update, and route actions at reserved nodes too) | `reserved_k8` |
| C1 | St | Every `Appended` of a request from a conversation (an origin other than a `user:` entry), a people question, a `said`, or a `heard`, and every `CommitmentOpened`, lies on `spec::conv_node(S_e, at, k)`, with `k` the body's `conv` (for a request, its `where`, or its origin without one, A-61), where `S_e` is the state just before that event (after a case-3 `KeyAdded`) (A-12), and that node is not reserved (A-29). 1.3 (§9.2): every `CommitmentFulfilled { x, by: a }` follows, in the same step, the `Appended(Said)` of `a`, of kind `Reply`, `Result`, or `Correction`, on `x`'s node in `before`, with `saids[a].conv = commitments[x].conv`, and no `SaidWithheld { a }` (1.9); and after a step that appends such a `said` of conversation `k` on node `c`, not withheld, no commitment on `c` with `conv = k` that was `Open` in `before` is still `Open`. So a reply in another conversation on the node fulfils nothing, and a reply leaves no commitment of its own conversation open | `step_C1` (the `people` slice: an ack in each of two conversations on one node, then `act_said` of each kind with each `where`) | `conv_node_c1`, `settle_conversation` (its commitment half, 1.3) |
| Q1 | S | Request origins, the messages they came in (A-61), are pairwise distinct | `inv_Q1` | `record_request_q1` |
| S1 | S | Per `SignalKey` at most one open signal node; `signals` equals the set of open nodes with role `Signal`, with their keys (after a reopen too, A-89) | `inv_S1` | `open_signal_s1` |
| N1 | S | Every user entry has one `Routing` state (by type); `unrouted ∈ flags(USER) ⇔ ∃ e: Unrouted` | `inv_N1` | `route_n1` |
| Settled | S + St | S, over resident requests (D.4.12): `settled = Some((d, a)) ⇒ r ∈ d.settles`, `a = answered_by`, `a > r`, and `entries[a]` is a `said` of kind reply, result, or correction with `saids[a].conv = r.conv` (for a request with `requester = External`: a reply in another conversation on the same node answers nothing, §9.4, 1.3), or a `to_user` (`entries[a].ty = ToUser` with `entries[a].principal = Some(_)`) for a user request (CS-4); `settled = None ⇒ ¬(answered_by ≠ None ∧ ∃ d with state ≠ Retracted and r ∈ d.settles)`, scanning `decisions` (a superseded decision counts, §9.4). St: no `settled` becomes `None` (monotone, A-11); a `RequestAnswered { r, by: a }` with `a` a `to_user` follows, in the same step, the `Appended(ToUser)` of `a`, whose kind is `Result` (A-23), and has `entries[a].principal` and `r.requester` of the same person in `before` (`same_person`, D.8.11): a report to Alice never answers Bob's request, and an `ack` or a `question` to Bob never answers his. The person half is a step check because aliases may change after the answer; the kind half because `EntryMeta` keeps no `to_user` kind, and a `to_user` answers only in the step that records it. St (1.12, `release_decision`, §10.3): a `hold release` that records its checkpoint entry records a decision that lists requests only when its `settles` is non-empty, and then exactly one, on its node, after that entry, listing exactly its `settles` | `inv_Settled`, `step_Settled` (the `user` slice has two principals and `user`, and `to_user` of each kind; the `people` slice has `act_said` with each `where`, on a node that carries both conversation keys); *1.12's step clause: its executable check and tests (D.0.3)* | `try_settle_monotone`, `settle_requester`, `settle_conversation` (1.3) |
| F | S | **F1**: `ix.node[n].flags == spec::flags(s, n, now)` for every node, the fourteen flags with `basis_changed` (D-4) and `stale` (1.8). **F2**: with `t` the time of the first queued key, or `Time(u64::MAX)` when the queue is empty, `spec::flags(s, n, now) == spec::flags(s, n, t − 1 ms)` for every node: no flag changes before the next deadline, and none changes by time alone when nothing is queued (D.8.3). ### D.9.3 M1: what the server guarantees, and what `health` reports

M1 as written cannot be a pure state invariant: agents can legitimately create objects with no
server-guaranteed mover (a `{node}` wait on a node created with `take: false` and no `offer`, flags on
a node with capacity 0), and §17 already lists "some object has no mover" as a `health` condition. The
design splits it (A-54).

**M1a** (state invariant, `check_invariants`): every waiting object has its server-guaranteed mover.
A mover is a queued deadline or a flag that makes some node a `next` candidate. A question for the
user and the digest are how a human hears of things, not movers: with no human they move nothing, so
the rows below never count a person (CS-6). A digest entry is a record, not a waiting object (D1
keeps it until shown, and nothing waits on it).

| Waiting object | Asserted mover |
|---|---|
| wait `{time}`, `{external}`, unresolved | its Wait deadline is queued |
| wait `{question q}` (people), unresolved | `q` is `Open` and its Recheck deadline is queued |
| wait `{question q}` (user), unresolved | `q` is `Pending` and its UserQuestion deadline is queued (CS-2) |
| wait `{node t}`, unresolved | `t` is open (M1b checks `t`'s own mover) |
| people question `Open` | its Recheck deadline (A-24) |
| people question `Expired`, not answered, `assumed_by = None` | its assume mark on an open node (`proceed_on_assumption`: a candidate, or held, or waiting with its own mover); closed nodes carry no assume mark (A-104) |
| people question `Escalated`, not answered | its user question, by the user-question rows: `Pending` with its deadline queued, or `Lapsed` with its own mover; the nodes that waited on it wait on that user question (A-93) |
| commitment `Open` | its Commitment deadline, or `open_commitment` on its node, or its node attended (a lease deadline), or an `Open` people question with the same `conv` on its node (a Recheck deadline) |
| `said` `Pending` | its session's Silence deadline |
| `said` `Unconfirmed` | `unconfirmed_said` on its node, or its node attended |
| open intent | `open_intent` on its node, or a live hold on the node, or the node waiting |
| open occurrence | its OccurrenceSlot or OccurrenceWindow deadline, or a live hold, or `overdue` or `open_intent` |
| user question `Pending` | its UserQuestion deadline is queued, which defaults, re-addresses, or lapses it (CS-2) |
| user question `Lapsed`, `assumed_by = None`, not answered after all (for an `Escalation { q }` source, `q` is not `Answered` and has not left memory, which it does only once answered, D.4.12, D.8.15) | its assume mark on an open node (`proceed_on_assumption`), as for an expired people question (CS-2) |
| refusal | its RefusalExpiry deadline |
| pause | its Pause deadline |

**M1b** (`query::m1b_gaps`, reported by `control health` as `NoMover`, with the count and the first
`HEALTH_TOP` gaps, red from 1 % of the flagged nodes, CS-9): every node whose flags are
its objects' mover is reachable: it is in `ix.next.of` (any kind) or held; and every chain of
unresolved `{node}` waits and `depends_on` edges ends at a node that is held, a candidate, closed, or
has a deadline-based mover. Each failure is a `MoverGap`. The gaps the server cannot prevent include
flags on capacity-0 nodes, `{node}` waits on nodes nobody offers, and an open intent that a merge
could not move because `into` had its own (D.8.20, A-94).

A *deadline-based mover* (WP-D6, `health::chain_ok`) is one of: an unresolved wait on time or on
something external (its Wait deadline), or on a question to a person or for the user (its Recheck
or UserQuestion deadline, M1a's rows); an occurrence still `Waiting` for its slot (its
OccurrenceSlot deadline); or, for a node that is not yet a candidate, a queued Due deadline on it
(capacity above 0, not reserved): once due the node carries `overdue` and becomes a candidate, so
the chain ends there, or, while the node depends on an open node, goes on through that dependency.
A commitment's follow-up, a `said`'s Silence deadline, and a question's Recheck also raise flags on
a node, but they are not counted as the mover of a node that does not wait: such a node must be
held, a candidate, or moved by one of the deadlines above.

### D.9.4 The invariant registry and `docs/verification.md`

`forum_core::invariants::registry`:

```rust
pub enum InvKind { State, Step, Property }
pub enum VerusStatus { Todo, InProgress, Proved }

/// Serialize only under the `serde` feature (D.2): it holds &'static data.
pub struct InvariantInfo {
    pub id: Inv,
    pub kinds: &'static [InvKind],       // H2, H3, H5, O1, O2, Settled, D1, U1, R2, T1, T4, L1:
                                         // State and Step
    pub quint: &'static [&'static str],  // names in model/*.qnt
    pub quint_reason: Option<&'static str>, // why there is no Quint check (D.9.2, italics)
    pub kani: &'static [&'static str],   // #[kani::proof] functions
    pub kani_reason: Option<&'static str>,  // why there is no Kani harness
    pub verus: VerusStatus,
    pub verus_todo: &'static str,        // the tracked TODO, id "V-<Inv>"
}

/// One row per Inv, the table of D.9.2. Every row starts with VerusStatus::Todo.
pub const INVARIANTS: &[InvariantInfo] = &[ /* … */ ];
```

Tests in `forum-core/tests/registry.rs`:
- every `Inv` variant has exactly one row;
- every row has a Quint name or a `quint_reason`, and a Kani harness or a `kani_reason`, never both
  empty, so a gap cannot be silent (AGENTS.md "every invariant gets checked at each level that
  exists");
- every row has a non-empty `verus_todo`;
- every Quint name occurs as `val <name>`, `def <name>`, or `run <name>` in `model/**/*.qnt`;
- every Kani name is a `#[kani::proof]` function under `crates/*/src`;
- `docs/verification.md` contains the table generated from `INVARIANTS` between the markers
  `<!-- registry:begin -->` and `<!-- registry:end -->`; the test fails if it differs, and
  `UPDATE_VERIFICATION=1 cargo test -p forum-core --test registry` rewrites it.

The rest of `docs/verification.md` is maintained by hand: the traceability tables of Appendices A, B,
and C of this document (the coverage check that nothing in the specification is lost), the Verus TODO
list, and the record of which Kani harnesses were narrowed (D.12.5).

**Verus TODOs** (each a registry row's `verus_todo`): for every state invariant, K8 (V-K8, new in
1.2) included, "`evolve` of each event `apply` and `settle` emit preserves it"; for every step invariant and every step half (H2, H3,
H4, H5, O1, O2, O3, K7, C1, N5, Settled, D1, U1, R2, T1, T4, L1, P2), "every `(s, ctx, cmd)` with `decide`'s
events, and every `(s, key)` with `fire`'s events, satisfies the step predicate"; `settle`
idempotence and T2 through the lemmas L1 and L2 of D.8.2 (V-T2); T3 ("every reply equals the reply on the settled
state"); exactly-once `op_id` (O1); flag monotonicity between events (the lemma behind F2);
`recount ∘ evolve = evolve_index ∘ recount` (R1, T4); for G1 (V-G1, new in 1.3), "every item of
`guide` on a settled state satisfies `validate`'s precondition, and a `Close` item's plan raises
none of the four warnings"; a termination measure for every loop. Verus needs specifications of
the `BTreeMap` and `BTreeSet` operations the core uses; if `vstd`'s are insufficient, the proofs target an abstract map model and the concrete maps stay in the
trusted base, decided when the proofs start.

## D.10 Quint model

> **Scope (D.0.3).** The model checks the key invariants only (holds, retries, keys and the tree,
> and time). Parts below that serve other invariants are not required.

### D.10.1 Files

```
model/
  package.json             @informalsystems/quint 0.33.0 (exists); scripts below
  types.qnt                ids, sum types (keys and names included, D.10.3), records of the
                           abstract state (no text)
  params.qnt               scaled parameters (D.10.5) and the bounds of D.10.7 as pure vals
  basics.qnt               ancestors, resolve, conv_node, live, waiting, paused, tie_hash, p90
  flags.qnt                the flag predicates of D.8.3, one to one
  deadlines.qnt            deadline_of, the computed queue, fire (D.8.2), and the bounded settle
                           with its saturation flag
  commands.qnt             one pure function per command: validate, then execute; returns
                           (State, Outcome) and allocates ids in the same order as Rust
  invariants.qnt           every item of D.9.2 as a val over (prev, mid, s, clock, last_action)
  guide.qnt                1.3: `def guide(s, sess, last_action)` for the rules of §20.9 whose
                           call is a model action, and `inv_G1`, `inv_G1_close` (D.10.4, WP-A5)
  forum.qnt                module forum: consts, vars, init (genesis and the seed, D.10.7), the
                           named actions, step, inv_all
  instances/two_class.qnt  import forum(CLASSES = Set("a", "b"), USE_FNV = true, QUORUM = 2).*
  instances/one_class.qnt  import forum(CLASSES = Set("w"), USE_FNV = false, QUORUM = 1).*  (§28)
  instances/no_user.qnt    import forum(CLASSES = Set("w"), USE_FNV = false, QUORUM = 1,
                           PRINCIPALS = Set("user"), HAS_USER = false).*: no from_user or to_user
                           action at all, for simulation (CS-2, CS-6, ZU-9)
  slices/holds.qnt         step restricted to the hold actions (D.10.7), USE_FNV = false; one
                           module per class configuration (holds_two, holds_one)
  slices/keys.qnt
  slices/people.qnt
  slices/user.qnt          one module per configuration: user_two, user_one, and user_none
                           (HAS_USER = false, PRINCIPALS = Set("user"))
  slices/recurring.qnt
  slices/basis.qnt         decisions with basis references, retraction, supersession, closes with
                           each outcome, reopen, take, next (D-4, CS-22)
  tests/forum_test.qnt     run tests: one per command family, scenario_32, test_T2, O1, H4, K6, E1
traces/                    (git-ignored) ITF traces and counterexamples
```

`commands.qnt` mirrors `validate` and the execution of D.8 step by step, including the order of
entries and therefore of `Eid` allocation, so that a model state and a projected Rust state can be
compared field by field. Actions in `forum.qnt` are thin: check that the state is settled at `now`,
call the pure function, settle at `now` as D.8.1's post-settle does, and set `prev`, `mid`, and
`last_action` (D.10.4). Every action ends with a settle: a command's post-settle at its `now`, or a
time action's settle to the new clock.

`forum.qnt` is parameterised by `const CLASSES: Set[str]`, `const USE_FNV: bool`, `const QUORUM:
int` (`refusal.quorum`, CS-7: 2 with two classes of two sessions, so that a class can reach it, and 1
with one class, where it keeps 1.1's single refusal reachable), `const PRINCIPALS: Set[str]` (the
principal keys `act_from_user`, `act_to_user`, and `act_ask_user` pick from; `user` is always in
it), and `const HAS_USER: bool` (false disables `act_from_user` and `act_to_user`); instances and
slices instantiate it, for example `module one_class { import forum(CLASSES = Set("w"), USE_FNV =
false, QUORUM = 1, PRINCIPALS = Set("user", "p1", "p2"), HAS_USER = true).* from "../forum" }`, so
every configuration shares one definition. Slices take `QUORUM` from their class configuration.
Instances that do not name the last two use `PRINCIPALS = Set("user", "p1", "p2")` and `HAS_USER =
true`; `no_user` uses `Set("user")`.

`package.json` scripts: `typecheck` (every file), `test` (`quint test tests/forum_test.qnt`),
`simulate` (`quint run instances/two_class.qnt --max-steps 40 --max-samples 20000
--invariant inv_all`), `traces` (the `--mbt` run of D.10.7), `verify:<slice>` (Apalache),
`tlc:<slice>` (TLC), and `liveness:holds`, `liveness:recurring`, `liveness:user` (with its
`user_none` module) (TLC with `--temporal`), as listed in D.10.7. Apalache and TLC need a JDK 17 or
newer; `scripts/verify.sh` checks for `java` and says which checks it skipped.

### D.10.2 State variables

```quint
var s: State               // the abstract base state (D.10.3)
var clock: int             // model-only time in ticks: where the shell's clock has got to
var prev: State            // the state before the last action (step invariants)
var mid: State             // the state after the last action's command, before its post-settle
                           // (D.8.1); prev for init and the time actions (step invariants)
var last_action: Action    // the last action: name, parameters, op, outcome, and the flags of its
                           // settle (D.10.8)
```

`mid` lets the step invariants see an action as D.9.1 sees a call: `check_step` from `prev` to `mid`,
and `check_fire` on each firing of the settle that ends the action, from `mid` to `s`. It is a
function of `prev`, `clock`, and `last_action`, so it adds no distinct state, and the replay never
reads it. `last_action.settle` holds that settle's flags (`saturated`, `stuck`), which
`inv_settle_bound` and `inv_T4` read; the time actions' outcome is `OutNone`.

`clock` is separate from `s.last_now` for the same reason as in Rust: settling does not record the
`now` it was called with, and `last_now` moves only with events (D.8.2, T2). A model that kept time
only in `last_now` could not run a tick that fires nothing, and its `last_now` would differ from the
projected Rust state after every such tick. Invariants over `(S, now)` take `now = clock`.

The quint-connect projection is `Config { state: &["s", "clock"], nondet: &[] }`: the driver keeps
its own clock (the sum of the `dt` it has replayed) and projects it into `clock`; `last_now` is
compared as an ordinary field of `s`.

### D.10.3 Abstract state

```quint
/// Quint strings are opaque: there is no concatenation and no integer-to-string conversion, so
/// every key and name the server builds from ids is a sum type, not a string.
type Key  = Conv(str) | Msg(str, int) | User(int) | Repeat(int, int) | Person(str)
          // atom; message n of conversation c, a request's origin (A-61); user:e<eid>;
          // repeat:<series>:<slot>; person:<principal key> (D.2.2)
type Name = Lit(str) | Slot(int) | SlotDup(int, int) | Signal(SignalKind, int, int, int)
          // an agent's name; YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ of a slot; that name with "-<id>"; <kind>-<a>-<b>-<id>

type State = {
  last_now: int,
  next_node: int, next_eid: int, next_session: int, next_principal: int, anomalies: int,
  principal_ids: str -> int,                   // "user" -> 0 from genesis (CS-1)
  user_msgs: int -> List[int],                 // per principal, pruned as in evolve (CS-2; history,
                                               // D.4.2)
  nodes: int -> Node,                          // Node mirrors D.4.3 with the abstractions below
  names: (int, Name) -> int,
  aliases: (int, Name) -> int,
  entries: int -> { node: int, seq: int, at: int, by: int, ty: EntryType, principal: int },
                                               // keeps_meta (CS-17); principal −1 unless from_user
                                               // or to_user (D.4.5)
  holds: (int, int) -> Hold,                   // keyed by token (node, fence)
  requests: int -> Request,                    // origin: Key, a Msg, a Conv, or a User (A-61);
                                               // conv: Key, its conversation key (§9.4, 1.3)
  pquestions: int -> PQuestion,
  aquestions: int -> AQuestion,                // dropped with their note at `until` (D.4.12)
  uquestions: int -> UQuestion,
  commitments: int -> Commitment,
  saids: int -> Said,
  decisions: int -> Decision,                  // with `basis: List[BasisRef]` (CS-22)
  retracted: Set[BasisTarget],                 // what `retract` struck out (D-4)
  objections: int -> Objection,
  user_entries: int -> UserEntry,
  digest: int -> DigestEntry,
  notes: int -> Note,                          // dropped at `until` as in evolve (CS-17)
  approvals: (int, int) -> int,
  refusals: (int, str) -> Refusal,             // a quorum and per-session entries (CS-7)
  classes: str -> ClassActivity,               // caps profiles: Set[str] -> window end (CS-7)
  signals: (SignalKind, int, int) -> int,
  pauses: int -> Pause,
  sessions: int -> Session,                    // with `retire_at`; retired ones leave (CS-8)
  ops: (str, str) -> { digest: Cmd, session: int, expires_at: int },   // CS-8
}
```

Every Rust base field (D.4) has a field here, with these abstractions:
- node content (title, body, fields, files, status) is one integer `content` from a small domain,
  the digest another, and agreements a boolean, so O2's "iff content changes" is still checkable;
  `Text` is otherwise absent, and of a command's free texts only their length relative to
  `text.max` remains, as the action flag `long` (D.10.4), which is all that L1's text half reads;
- labels are small string sets;
- keys and names are the sum types above: `Conv("c1")` for an agent's conversation key,
  `Msg("c1", n)` for message `n` of that conversation as a request's origin (A-61), `User(e)`
  for `user:e<e>`, `Repeat(series, slot)` for `repeat:<series>:<slot>`, `Lit("w1")` for an agent's
  name, `Slot(t)` and `SlotDup(t, id)` for occurrence names, `Signal(kind, a, b, id)` for signal
  names; `project()` (D.10.8) parses Rust's strings into them;
- a `Repeat` is a period and an offset (D.10.6); the tz table is absent (UTC);
- `Stats`, `since`, `held_ms`, `counters.events`, and `params` are absent: health and the coverage
  warning are not modelled, and the parameters are model constants (D.10.5);
- the `op_id` digest is the command record without `sess` and `op` (`ops` stores the abstract
  command, so "same digest" is record equality), matching Rust's digest, which excludes `session`
  and `op_id` (D.11.5);
- every kept entry has its `at`, so `inv_T1` ("every entry's `at <= last_now`") is expressible; the
  model keeps the same entries as Rust (`keeps_meta`, CS-17), so states compare field by field;
- the retry store keeps the digest, the session, and the expiry, as Rust's does (CS-8): the outcome is
  in `last_action`, not in the state, and expired records and notes leave at the next event as in
  `evolve`;
- there is no candidate `since`: `aged` equals `priority` within the model's time bound (D.10.5);
- a basis reference is `BNode(id, life_at)` or `BEntry(eid)`, with `life_at` an outcome or `-1`
  for open; the cited version and external references are absent, because no decision reads them
  (CS-22, D-4);
- the user side keeps every field that a decision reads (CS-1 to CS-5): `UserEntry.principal`,
  `Request.requester`, `UQuestion.{to, stage, due, assumed_by}`, `DigestEntry.to`,
  `Session.principals`, the entries' `principal`, and the per-principal message times
  (`user_msgs`, history in Rust too); principal keys are model strings from `PRINCIPALS`;
- the directory is ordinary state (D-3): the reserved nodes `@people` (6) and `@teams` (7), `Person`
  keys on their children, the `gone` tag, and `Node.owners: Set[int]`; `chain`, `same_person`, and
  `absent` are defs over it, as in D.8.11 and D.8.12, a team's members are its own `owners` only
  (A-116), and `is_container` and the child limit read the parent as in D.4.3 and D.8.4 (A-113);
- a `holders:` note has no recipients, and `Session.branch_seen` is the per-scope cursor its readers
  advance (D-6), so the `people` slice's `say` and `wait` exercise delivery at read time;
- nothing leaves memory except notes and agent questions at `until` and `op_id` records at expiry:
  FINISHED_RETAIN and DIGEST_RETAIN are real-time constants (7 and 28 days) that no model run
  reaches (D.10.5), so the replay compares every entity;
- 1.4's two base fields are modelled as Rust keeps them (D.14.4): `Hold.reopened`, the outcome the
  node had when this hold's take reopened it, or `-1`; and `Session.told: Set[int]`, the principals
  the session has recorded a `to_user` to, empty when the session opens.

### D.10.4 Actions

One named action per command that changes the base state, plus time:

```
act_hello(c, caps, principal) act_create(sess, parent, name, keys, take, capacity, owners, repeat)
act_update(sess, n, ver, dver, content, digest, capacity, needs_add, needs_remove, tags_add,
           tags_remove, due, depends, owners, repeat)        act_link(sess, n, rel, m)
act_key_add(sess, n, k)       act_key_remove(sess, n, k)     act_close(sess, n, outcome, settles, tok)
act_reopen(sess, n)           act_move(sess, n, parent, name) act_merge(sess, from, into)
act_take(sess, n, lease)      act_next(sess)                 act_checkpoint(sess, tok, intent, done)
act_renew(sess, tok)          act_release(sess, tok, reason, wait)
act_from_user(sess, principal, answers, node)   act_to_user(sess, principal, kind, re)
act_route(sess, e, to)
act_request(sess, at, origin, where) act_said(sess, at, kind, where) act_confirm(sess, said)
act_heard(sess, at, answers)         act_ask_person(sess, at, blocking, again)
act_ask_user(sess, at, has_default, to)  act_ask_agent(sess, at, to)    act_answer(sess, q)
act_decide(sess, at, settles, supersedes, basis)              act_retract(sess, target)
act_approve(sess, n, ver)     act_object(sess, n)            act_resolve(sess, o, upheld, defer)
act_check_intent(sess, n)     // 1.8: hold check {target, intent_done}
act_say(sess, at, to)         act_wait(sess, for)            act_hide(sess, entry)
act_pause(sess, n)            act_unpause(sess, n)           act_view(sess, n)   // Touched? + Shown?
act_tick(dt)                  // dt ∈ 1..3, clock + dt ≤ MAX_TIME: the clock moves, then
                              // everything due fires
act_tick_next                 // the clock jumps to the first queued key (≤ MAX_TIME), which fires
```

`act_next` has no query in the model, so every call is an open `next`: it records the caller's caps
as a profile of its class (CS-7). `act_create` gives a node without its own `needs` its parent's
(CS-26). `act_update` picks `dver` as "absent" too, so that `MissingDigestVersion` is reachable
(CS-11), and changes needs only by additions and removals (CS-34). `act_create` under `@people`
picks `Person` keys from `PRINCIPALS` (aliases), under `@teams` picks owners among the person nodes,
and anywhere may pick owners (persons or teams, ROOT included); `act_update` adds and removes the
`gone` tag and replaces owners (D-3). Every command emits `Touched` only
when presence is due (`clock >= last_seen + 1` tick, the scaled `presence.resolution`), the session is
silent, or it issues a hold, and `Shown` only when it raises `seen` (CS-14), exactly as Rust does, so
`act_view` of an unchanged node within the same tick changes nothing. The time actions fire `Retire`
(a session retires 10 ticks after its last touch, CS-8), and every event drops the expired `op_id`
records and notes, with their agent questions, as `evolve` does. `act_decide` picks `basis` from at most two references to
existing nodes (including closed and merged ones, and `at` itself, so that the drop of a
self-reference, 1.4's in place of 1.3's `SelfLink` refusal, is reachable)
and existing decisions, and `act_retract` picks a decision, another entry, or a node, so that every
case of `stale` is reachable (D-4). `act_request` picks its origin among `Msg("c1", 1)`,
`Msg("c1", 2)`, `Conv("c1")`, and `Conv("c2")`, and `where` among none, `Conv("c1")`, and
`Conv("c2")`, so that a repeat of one message, a second request in one conversation, and a request
without a message id (the origin is the conversation, as in 1.1) are all reachable (A-61).
`act_said` picks `where` among none, `Conv("c1")`, and `Conv("c2")`, so that a node carrying both
conversation keys, with a request of each, is reachable, and a reply in one of them must leave the
other's request unanswered (§9.4, 1.3); `inv_Settled` and `step_Settled` compare the `said`'s
`conv` with the request's, and `Request` carries `conv` as Rust's does (D.4.5). A reply likewise
fulfils only the open commitments whose `conv` is its own and leaves the other conversation's
open, and `step_C1` compares the two (§9.2, 1.3). `act_to_user` picks `kind` among `ack`,
`question`, and `result`, and only `result` answers a request (A-23).

1.8: `act_resolve` picks `upheld`; on a closed node an upheld resolve corrects it, `done` to
`failed` (the model's nodes have no kind, so never `refuted`, which Rust's `Outcome::Other` alone
can hold), and marks the closure `upheld`, which `classify` and `v_take` read. `act_check_intent`
is `hold check {target, intent_done}`, in the `holds` slice and its conformance variants; a `check`
without `intent_done` reads and is not modelled. `append_entry` (but for a `late` entry),
`ev_node_created`, `add_key`, `remove_key`, the link, update, and reopen executions, and the Wait
firing touch their node (D.4.3), and the queue has the Stale kind, 12, last in §17's order
(`K_STALE`, `stale_key_at`); `flags.qnt` has `f_stale`, `best_candidate` the key `(tier, stale,
recheck, …)`, `inv_F` the open-only `stale`, and `inv_T3` its marker.

1.9: `act_say` with `SayNone` at a node another session holds records a `holder:` note to those
holders (`say_ex`, `other_holders`), and `act_said` by a session that holds neither the
conversation node nor a node below it, while another does (`conv_held`), records the `said` as
`SdWithheld`, answering, fulfilling, and opening nothing; `step_C1`, `step_Settled`, and the merge's
credit skip it, and `step_N5` moves only pending and unconfirmed entries. `unsent`, whose replaced
entries 1.9 withholds, and the forum's tidy items, which are next calls, are not modelled.

1.10: `act_said` by such a session records the `said` pending, as any other (`conv_held` stays as
the warning's condition, which the model does not render); `act_say` with `SayNone` at a node no
session holds, which can be held, records a `holder:` note pending its next holder, and
`bind_holder_notes` and `holder_recipients` leave the sender out, as the core does since 1.4;
`checkpoint_ex` ends the node's wait; `resolve_ex` of a resolved objection records nothing for the
same verdict, and for the opposite one a new open objection on `resolve_merged` of its node
(`dispute_ex`), withdrawing the correction when the earlier verdict upheld it and still marks the
node: the closure's `from_done` (Rust's `corrected_from == Some(Done)`, the only outcome a
correction changes) says whether `done` comes back. The `keys` slice takes and checkpoints (T5 and
M1 over a `{node}` wait that a checkpoint ends: before, nothing held a node again once its release
had set a wait) and the `people` slice checkpoints and says without `to` (W1 and M1).
`no_basis` and `paused` are warnings, and the `waiting` warning's author a text: not modelled. The
conformance group `review_two` (D.10.8) replays the review and the notes; building it found two
older differences of the model from the core, both fixed in the model: the expiry prune kept a
note's entry metadata, which the core drops with the note (`at_event`), and a `session:` addressee
that does not exist was `not_found(Session)`, where the core says `not_found(Addressee)` (1.4, R12;
`WhatAddressee`).

1.11: `act_resolve` picks a verdict or a deferral (`defer`, never with `upheld`, which
`v_resolve` refuses with `WhyBadParams`): a deferral of an open objection appends its `resolve`
entry and, on a closed node, the caller's refusal (`refuse`, shared with `release_ex`'s `cannot`),
so `best_candidate` skips the review for the caller's class while it is `excluded`; a verdict on a
closed node with refusal records clears them (`verdict_clears`, `clear_refusals`), and a deferral
of a resolved objection records nothing. `said_ex` and `ask_person_ex` record the `said` confirmed
when its session holds no live hold (`said_start`, `holds_nothing`). The closure carries `by`, the
closing session or -1 for the server (`ev_node_closed_by`, set by `close_steps`), which the
projection compares with Rust's `closure.by`, and `say_ex` with `SayNone` at a closed node records a
note to its live closer (`closer`), and at an open node only does it wait for a next holder. The
voice by its cap is a warning's condition and the next calls', and the kept retracted decision and
an objection's deferral feed the brief and `no_basis`: not modelled, as `conv_held` and
`no_basis` are not. Run tests: `deferTest`, `saidAloneTest`, `closerNoteTest`; the `people` slice
resolves with each verdict and defers (E1 and M1 over refusals of closed nodes), and the conformance
group `review_two` replays the deferrals and the notes at closed nodes.

1.12: `CRelease` carries `settles`, and `release_ex` ends with `record_decision`, the events of
`decide_ex` (which now calls it too), with the reply ids `[decision]`; `retract_ex` of an open
people question sets `PqWithdrawn(entry)` and removes its marks; `holder_recipients` of a closed node
is its live closer (`closer`), never pending; `reopen_ex` puts `offer` on a node that is not a
container. `inv_E1` gains (g), a withdrawn question with no recheck queued and no unresolved wait
on it; 1.12's step clauses of Settled (a release's decision) and E1 are executable checks only
(D.0.3), while `step_Settled` keeps Settled's older ones. `step_O3` now lets
the entry of a note whose `until` has come leave, as `at_event` and the core's `may_leave` do:
1.12's conformance group `finish_two`, generated with the slice's invariants checked, found it.
Run tests: `releaseSettlesTest`, `withdrawTest`, `holderClosedTest`, `reopenOfferTest`; the `people`
and `user` slices release with `settles`, and `people` retracts questions; the conformance group
`finish_two` replays all four.

**Next calls (1.3, WP-A5): not modelled.** D.0.3 dropped WP-A5, and `guide.qnt` was never
written: the model has no `guide`, no `inv_G1`, and no `inv_G1_close`, no slice imports them, and
the conformance replay compares no next calls (D.10.8). G1 is not a key invariant; `check_guide`
checks it in Rust after every call in every test, in the property test, and in the §32 scenario
(D.9.1, D.9.2's G1 row), and the registry records it at the level *tests* (D.9.4, WP-D9). The rest
of this paragraph is the plan, kept for a later model of G1. `guide.qnt` would define
`guide(s, sess, last_action)`, the next calls of §20.9 as model actions with their parameters, for
the rules whose call is one: 2 (`act_confirm`), 3
(`act_checkpoint`, with and without `intent_done`), 5 (`act_create` with the entry's key, and
`act_route` to none), 6 (`act_to_user` of kind `result`, `act_said` of kind `result` with the
requests' conversation as `where`), 7 (`act_decide`), 8 (`act_close`, and `act_release` of a
container), 9 (`act_release` with a wait, `act_wait`, `act_heard` on the question's conversation,
`act_update` adding `offer`, `act_from_user` with `answers`, `act_said` of kind `reply` with each
conversation whose commitment raises the flag as `where`, `act_route`), 10 (`act_confirm`,
`act_decide`, `act_release` with a wait, `act_create` of a child without its fresh name,
`act_merge`, `act_resolve`), 11 (`act_wait`, `act_answer`), 12 (`act_to_user` of kind `question`, or
`ack` with only digest entries pending), 13 (`act_take`, `act_next`), and E's `act_take` and
`act_checkpoint`. `inv_G1` says that every action `guide` suggests after the last action is enabled
in `s`, and `inv_G1_close` that a suggested `act_close` raises none of the four warnings on a node
with no open child and no other session's open intent, and that none names a container or a reserved
node. `guide` returns the whole list of the modelled rules, before the cut of §20.9, so `inv_G1`
checks every item, and conformance compares it with Rust's (D.10.8). Rule 4's `view node`, rule 1's
`talk from_user` without `answers`, E's `session hello`, texts, and rendering are left out: a read,
a new message, and a new session are enabled whenever their session is, so no guard could refuse
them, and G1's row carries their `quint_reason` (D.9.2). The checkpoint cadence and margin are the
constants of D.10.5.

**1.4 in the model** (the usability round, D.14.4). Of the items, those that change the base
state, an event, a firing, or a refusal reach the model; replies, warnings, texts, rendering, and
the shell's schemas do not (the model compares outcomes by code and allocated ids, and drops
warnings, D.10.8). In order of the files:
- `types.qnt`: `Hold.reopened` and `Session.told` (D.10.3), and the `NotFound` subject
  `Addressee` (D.6.3).
- `deadlines.qnt`: the Silence key of a session lies at `max(silence_at, the largest lease_until
  of its holds, last_now)`, in both the computed queue and its minimum (R27, D.4.8: the floor
  keeps the key out of the past when the last hold ends after `silence_at`); `Hold`'s rank 0 before
  `Session`'s rank 5 keeps an equal-time lease end first. The OccurrenceSlot firing copies the
  series' `content` (which stands for title and body), `needs`, and `est` into the occurrence where
  they differ, as a `NodeUpdated` that bumps `version` as O2 says, before `OccurrenceAvailable`
  (R10).
- `commands.qnt`: `act_take` and `act_next` set `reopened` to the outcome the closed node had
  (R4); `act_release` takes `intent_done` and closes the node's open intent, `Invalid(NoIntent)`
  with none open, checked after the wait target's `NotFound` and before `Cycle` (D.8.24) (R15); `act_decide` drops a basis reference to `at`, directly or through
  `merged_into`, instead of refusing it with `Invalid(SelfLink)` (R14); `act_to_user` adds its
  principal to the session's `told` (R13); a `holder:` note's recipients and `bind_holder_notes`
  skip the sender, and a session's inbox skips the `holders:` notes it wrote (R12); `act_say` to
  `session:<retired>` is `NotFound(Addressee)` (R12); `act_ask_person` keeps `blocking`, and
  `act_ask_user` takes none, as 1.3's model already did.
- `forum.qnt` and the slices: `act_release` picks `intent_done` where an intent can be open (the
  `holds` and `recurring` slices); `act_decide` still picks `at` among its basis references, now so
  that the drop is reachable; `act_say` picks `holder:` and `holders:` of a node the sender holds,
  so that the skip is reachable; the `recurring` slice updates the series' content and needs while
  an occurrence waits, so that the copy is reachable.
- `invariants.qnt`: H2's state half gains "a silent session holds no live hold" (§26 H2, 1.4), and
  `inv_T3`'s session marker becomes `silent ⇔ silence_at <= now ∧ no hold has session = x`
  (D.9.2); no other invariant changes, and none is added: the refusal of a self-citing basis,
  which §21 mapped to none, is gone.
- `guide.qnt` (WP-A5, not written: D.0.3 dropped it; the plan for 1.4 was this): rule E keeps
  rules 6 and 7 (R19); rule 4 loses its `STALE SESSION` branch
  (R27); rule 7 suggests `act_decide` for a request the action recorded on a node nobody holds
  (R3); rule 8 suggests `act_close`, later, after an `act_checkpoint` with `intent_done` and no new
  `intent` on a node with no unsettled request (R11), and, with the hold's `reopened` outcome, after an action that
  cleared the last flag a close would leave on a node the take reopened (R4); rule 11 never offers
  the session's own agent question (R12); rule 12 stands until the session's `told` holds that
  person (R13). Rule 3's `uncovered_slot` branch (R18) is not modelled, because the coverage
  warning is not (D.10.6); G1's row gives the reason.

Not modelled: `session status` (its only base effect is the `Touched` that `act_view` already
exercises; its text is not in the core), `hold check`, `talk who`, `view` other than `node`,
`control health`, `constitution`, and `export` (they append nothing but `Touched`, or nothing), and
`admin set_params` (the parameters are model constants; A-103 makes the parameter E1 reads a stored
snapshot, so a change could not break an invariant the model checks).

Every command action takes an optional `op` (`"o1"`, `"o2"`, or none) and picks its parameters with
`nondet` from small domains, so that quint-connect sees named actions with named nondeterministic
picks (quint-connect cannot drive anonymous actions). Every command action whose Rust command
carries a `Text` also takes `long: bool`, which says that one of its free-text arguments is over
`text.max` (L1, A-114). With `long`, `run_cmd` returns the state unchanged and the outcome
`Limit(TextTooLong)` before it reads the retry store or the session, as `apply`'s step 1 does
(D.8.1); the record of a recorded command therefore never has `long`, and a repeat of its `op` with
`long` is still `Limit(TextTooLong)`, not a replay. `long` is picked in the `holds` slice and in
simulation, where O1 and H4 meet it; the other slices fix it at `false`, because a long text
changes nothing whatever the command. A command action is

```
all {
  settled(s, now),                       // now = max(clock, s.last_now); every action leaves the
                                         // state settled at its time
  val r = run_cmd(s, now, …),
  within_bounds(s, r.state),
  val p = settle(r.state, now, MAX_FIRINGS),   // D.8.1's post-settle
  s' = p.state, clock' = clock, prev' = s, mid' = r.state,
  last_action' = { name, params, op, outcome: r.outcome, settle: { p.saturated, p.stuck } },
}
```

A command action ends with D.8.1's post-settle at its `now`, the same bounded `settle` as the time
actions. Its pre-settle is the guard `settled(s, now)`: every action leaves the state settled at its
time, and only the time actions move the clock. No modelled command creates a deadline before its
`now`: a `{time}` or `{external}` wait at or before `now` resolves at once through its marker, and
`act_ask_user` has no explicit `due`. But a command that ends another session's last hold after
that session's `silence_at` (a release with its token, or a close, move, or merge of its node) leaves
that session's Silence key at exactly `now` (1.4, R27, D.4.8), and the post-settle fires it in the
same call, as the core's does. The step checks see the command and its settle apart (D.9.1), and
`step_T4` allows the command that one key at `now` (D.9.2). In Apalache's encoding every command
action unrolls one settle fold. (Until 2026-10-03 the model's commands did not settle, which WP-F1's
replay and the simulation caught as R27's case: D.14.7.)

`act_tick(dt)` is `all { clock + dt <= MAX_TIME, val r = settle(s, clock + dt), s' = r.state, clock'
= clock + dt, prev' = s, mid' = s, last_action' = { …, outcome: OutNone, settle: { r.saturated,
r.stuck } } }`. `act_tick_next` is the same with `clock'` the time of the first queued key, when
there is one at or before `MAX_TIME`; it lets a bounded run reach a second recheck, an expiry, and an
escalation's re-addressing or lapse (8 + 8 + 5 ticks after setup with an absent addressee, 8 + 8 +
11 with a present one; an asked question with a default defaults 11 ticks after it is asked),
without spending its depth on
empty ticks.

Settling is a bounded deterministic fold, `range(0, MAX_FIRINGS).foldl(…, fire_min_due)`, returning
the state and a `saturated` flag (a key at or before `now` remained after `MAX_FIRINGS` firings).
`MAX_FIRINGS` is set per slice to the number of firings the slice's bounds allow, counting each
`Session` owner twice, once for its Silence and once for its Retire, and in the `user` slices every
re-addressing and lapse of each user question (for example two leases, four sessions' silences and
four retirements, one pause, and one wait in `holds`), and `inv_settle_bound`
fails when the last settle (a time action's, or a command's post-settle) is `saturated`, separately from `inv_T4`, so a truncated fold is never mistaken for a
protocol violation, nor passes one. Owners are encoded so that the Quint queue order equals the Rust
order: `rank × 10^6 + payload`, with ranks in `Owner`'s declaration order (`Hold` 0, `Node` 1, `Entry`
2, `Refusal` 3, `Class` 4, `Session` 5) and payloads `node × 100 + fence`, `id`, `eid`, `node × 10 +
class index`, `class index`, `session`, where the class index is the position in the sorted class
names.

### D.10.5 Time scaling

One tick is one minute when a trace is replayed against Rust (`Time = T0 + tick × 60_000`, with
`T0 = 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`). Durations are scaled with their order and their equalities preserved,
with the one exception that §28 records (LEASE_MARGIN, below):

| Parameter | Real | Ticks |
|---|---|---|
| `presence.resolution` (CS-14) | 3 min | 1 |
| LEASE_MARGIN of the next calls (1.3, D.8.26) | 1 min | 1 |
| CHECKPOINT_EVERY of the next calls (1.3, D.8.26) | 5 min | 2 |
| `lease.first`, `presence.silence` | 15 min | 3 |
| `lease.default` | 20 min | 4 |
| `user_question.due_absent` (CS-2), `refusal.backoff` (CS-7) | 1 h | 5 |
| `commitment.followup` | 90 min | 6 |
| `lease.max`, `pause.ttl` | 2 h | 7 |
| `question.recheck` | 4 h | 8 |
| `lease.ceiling` | 8 h | 9 |
| `deliver.window`, `session.retain`, `op.retain` (CS-8) | 24 h | 10 |
| `user_question.due` | 72 h | 11 |
| `refusal.ttl`, `refusal.window`, `archive.after`, `capacity.window` | 7 days | 12 |
| `user_gap.window`, `coverage.window` | 28 days | 13 |
| `offer.stale` (1.8, §14) | 90 days | 14: within `MAX_TIME`, so the model's offers go stale |
| the hour of `aged` (§10.4) | 1 h | 60 (not scaled: the replay's real hour) |
| `renew.max`, `hold.per_session`, `question.max_rechecks`, `too_big.attempts` | 3, 2, 2, 3 | 2, 2, 2, 2 |
| `refusal.quorum` (CS-7) | 3 | `QUORUM`: 2 with two classes, 1 with one (D.10.1) |
| `tree.max_depth`, `tree.max_children` | 16, 500 | 4, 3 |

Counts are scaled down where the bound would otherwise be unreachable within the model's depth. The
Rust params used for replay are the scaled ones (any params that pass `Params::valid` are accepted;
`tree.max_depth = 4` keeps `/sys/signals/<signal>` legal). Every real duration of §22 has its own
tick value, so the scaling adds no equality: every order of the real values holds strictly between
the scaled ones, as §28 requires, with the one exception §28 records. Of the next calls' constants
(1.3), LEASE_MARGIN shares 1 tick with `presence.resolution`, because no tick is smaller, where the
real values are 1 < 3 minutes: no rule compares the two, and a checkpoint is enabled whenever it
falls due, so G1 does not depend on the margin; CHECKPOINT_EVERY keeps its order between them and
`lease.first` (1 < 2 < 3). Conformance compares the next calls of the modelled rules too (D.10.8),
so under the `conformance` feature both constants take these ticks as minutes (D.8.26), as the
replay's params are the scaled ones. The orders
`Params::valid` checks hold scaled: `lease.first <=
lease.default <= lease.max <= lease.ceiling` (3 ≤ 4 ≤ 7 ≤ 9), `user_question.due_absent <=
user_question.due` (5 ≤ 11), `refusal.backoff <= refusal.ttl` (5 ≤ 12), `3 × presence.resolution <=
presence.silence` (3 ≤ 3), and `session.retain` above `lease.ceiling` and `presence.silence` (10 > 9,
10 > 3), so a session retires within `MAX_TIME` of its last touch, holding nothing (CS-8). The two
memory constants of D.4.12, FINISHED_RETAIN (7 days) and DIGEST_RETAIN (28 days), are not
parameters and are not scaled: in a replay they are 10,080 and 40,320 ticks, far beyond `MAX_TIME`,
so nothing leaves memory in a model run but notes, agent questions, and `op_id` records. The forum's
owners are data, not a parameter (D-3): the seeds set none, and the `user` slice's actions add person
nodes, teams, owners, and `gone` marks; `user_question.max_pending` only drives a warning, which
conformance drops (D.10.8).

`aged = priority + ⌊now / 1 h⌋ − ⌊since / 1 h⌋` (CS-12, D-1) keeps the real hour, which is 60 ticks.
`T0` lies on an hour boundary, `MAX_TIME = 40`, and `params.qnt` asserts `MAX_TIME < 60`, so within
any model run every time lies in the first hour bucket and `aged = priority`; the model's commands
never set a priority, so `aged = 0` and `next` orders by `(tier, h, id)`. The Rust side computes
`aged` in full and gets the same value, because every replayed run ends within its first hour. The
model therefore needs no candidate `since`.

The series of the `recurring` slice and of the seeds has period 10 ticks, offset 0, and `run_within`
4 ticks; the replay driver maps it to `repeat: {cron: "*/10 * * * *", tz: "UTC", run_within: "4m"}`.

### D.10.6 What is abstracted

- **Text** of every kind, masking, text search, rendering, and budgets. L1's text half (`text.max`,
  A-114) keeps one bit of it: an action's `long` flag (D.10.4), over which `step_L1` checks that a
  long command changes nothing and is answered `Limit(TextTooLong)`, and `step_O1` and `step_H4`
  take `not(long)` as a precondition, as their Rust rows do (D.9.2). Byte lengths, masking before
  measuring, and `Cmd::longest_text` are left to `step_L1` in Rust, the Kani harness `limits_l1`,
  and the unit and shell tests.
- **Normalisation**: keys are the sum type `Key` (D.10.3); K2 is a shell property.
- **Cron and time zones**: a series has a `period` and an `offset` in ticks; `next_slot(t)` is the
  smallest `offset + k × period > t`. The replay driver maps it to the cron `*/period * * * *` in UTC,
  with `period` dividing 60 (the model uses 10, offset 0, D.10.5). DST gaps and folds are covered by
  `forum-cron`'s tests and Kani harnesses, not by the model.
- **Coverage warning, health, statistics**: not modelled (they never change the base state).
- **`aged` and candidate `since`**: not stored; `aged = priority = 0` within `MAX_TIME` (D.10.5).
- **FNV tie-break**: with `USE_FNV = true` (simulation and trace generation), `tie_hash` computes
  `fnv_id` and `fnv_session` over the two 9-byte inputs of D.2.6 and their difference modulo 2^64
  (CS-12, D-1), with integer arithmetic (little-endian bytes by `/` and `%`, the XOR of two bytes by
  an 8-step bit fold, multiplication modulo 2^64), so `next` picks the same candidate as Rust and
  conformance compares exact choices. With `USE_FNV = false` (Apalache, TLC) the tie is broken by
  id, and the driver replays those traces with `TieBreak::Id` (D.6.1, D.10.8); no invariant depends
  on the tie-break.
- **Commands without base effect** and `admin set_params` (D.10.4).

### D.10.7 Instances, bounds, and checks (§28)

**Bounds** (§28; their reading is A-108): 2 classes × 2 sessions each (session ids 1..4, each opened
at most once); 4 agent-made nodes besides the eight reserved ones, plus the server-made nodes, at most 3
occurrences of the one series and 2 signal nodes; 2 `op_id`s; 2 requests in all, user requests
included (origins `Msg("c1", 1)`, `Msg("c1", 2)`, `Conv("c1")`, `Conv("c2")`, or a user entry, so
that both requests can come from one conversation, A-61), and at most 2 user entries; capacity
in `{0, 1, 2}`; principals `user`, `p1`, and `p2` (CS-1; chains of at most 3 stages, one per
person), with at most one person node of two aliases and one team node among the four agent-made
nodes of the `user` slice (D-3); at most 3
decisions, each with at most 2 basis references (CS-22). The
single-worker-class configuration of §28 is `instances/one_class.qnt`; every slice is checked in
both class configurations. The forum with no human (one class, no `from_user` or `to_user`) is
`instances/no_user.qnt` for simulation and the `user_none` module of the `user` slice for Apalache,
TLC, and liveness, so that a question nobody answers is seen to end (CS-2, CS-6).

**Guards.** Every action carries explicit guards, so that the reachable state space is finite and TLC
terminates: `clock + dt <= MAX_TIME` (40); `next_eid <= MAX_EID` (16); every `version`, `fence`, and
`seq` `<= MAX_VER` (6); `attempts`, `checkpoints`, and approvals `<= 3`; at most 2 user entries. At a
bound the action is disabled. TLC runs without deadlock checking, so a run that reaches the bounds
stutters there, and the liveness properties are stated within the bounds.

**Seeds.** Every slice's `init` is genesis followed by a fixed seed of commands, which the driver
replays the same way: one `act_hello` per class, then two work nodes `/w1` (key `Conv("c1")`) and
`/w2` (key `Conv("c2")`), capacity 1, created with `take: false` and tagged `offer`; the `recurring`
seed also creates the series `/s` (D.10.5). The `people` and `user` slices, which have no `create`,
therefore still have nodes to take, ask on, and route to.

| Check | Command | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Types | `npx quint typecheck <file>` for every file | all |
| Unit and scenario runs | `npx quint test tests/forum_test.qnt` | each command family, `scenario_32`, `test_T2` |
| Simulation | `npx quint run instances/two_class.qnt --max-steps 40 --max-samples 20000 --invariant inv_all` | everything, random, within `MAX_TIME` |
| Traces for conformance | `npx quint run instances/two_class.qnt --mbt --max-steps 40 --n-traces 300 --out-itf traces/t{}.itf.json` | D.10.8 |
| Bounded model checking | `npx quint verify slices/<x>.qnt --max-steps 12 --invariant inv_<x> --out-itf traces/cex_<x>.itf.json` | Apalache, per slice |
| Exhaustive | `npx quint verify --backend=tlc slices/<x>.qnt --invariant inv_<x>` | TLC, per slice (finite through the guards) |
| Liveness (§27) | `npx quint verify --backend=tlc slices/<x>.qnt --temporal liveness_<x>` for `<x>` in `holds`, `recurring`, `user` | each property on the slice that produces its objects, under weak fairness of `act_tick`, `act_tick_next`, and of some call; both class configurations, and for `user` also `user_none` |

**Liveness, per slice.** `deadline_fires` ("every queued key with `at <= MAX_TIME` eventually fires")
in all three; `lease_ends` and `pause_ends` in `holds`; `occurrence_resolves` (every occurrence
closes or is flagged) in `recurring`; `uq_resolves` (every user question leaves `Pending`: answered,
defaulted, or lapsed, with or without a default, CS-2; it replaces 1.1's `default_resolves`) and
`wait_on_uq_resolves` (every wait on a user question resolves) in `user`, including `user_none`,
where nobody ever answers. Each property names only objects whose deadlines lie within `MAX_TIME`; a
deadline beyond it is outside the model's bounds (§28: "results hold only within the model bounds").

Slices restrict `step` to the actions their invariants need, so that Apalache stays tractable and TLC
terminates. `inv_<x>` is the conjunction of the slice's invariants; `step_O3`, `step_T4`, `inv_T3`,
`inv_T4`, `inv_K8`, and `inv_settle_bound` are in every slice, `inv_G1` and `inv_G1_close` (1.3,
`guide.qnt`) in `holds`, `people`, and `user` (`user_none` included), in both class configurations
and in simulation, and every slice's move, merge, close,
key, update (capacity, `repeat`), and route actions may name a reserved node, so that K8's refusals
are exercised wherever those actions exist:

| Slice | Actions | Invariants (besides the six above) |
|---|---|---|
| `holds` | hello, create (no keys), take, next, checkpoint, renew, release (no wait; with and without `intent_done`, 1.4), close, update (capacity; a digest with and without `digest_version`, CS-11), pause, unpause, view, tick, tick_next (so that sessions retire and `op_id` records expire, CS-8); every action with a text picks `long` (D.10.4) | H1–H6 (H2 with `step_H2`: a retired session holds nothing; 1.4: a silent session holds no live hold, with a checkpoint within a tick of the take extending the lease past `presence.silence`; H4 with a long stale write, which saves no `late` entry), O1 (`step_O1` and `inv_O1`, with expiry, the session check, and a long repeat of a recorded `op`), O2, P1, P2, T1, T2, L1 (`inv_L1`, `step_L1`, both halves), M1 |
| `keys` | create with keys, key add and remove, link, move, merge, reopen, close, release with a `{node}` wait, update (depends_on), request, said, ask person, heard (two conversation keys, so C1 and N5 see requests, `said` entries, questions, and commitments), hide, tick | K1, K3, K4, K5, K7, S1, N5, T5, C1, O2, L1 (a reopen past `tree.max_children`, and a `create` or `move` refused at it, CS-10; a `create` or `move` under `@people` or `@teams`, which the limit never refuses, A-113), M1 (its waits, `said` entries, questions, and commitments are M1a objects) |
| `people` | request (with message origins and `where`, A-61), said (of each kind, with `where`, on a node that carries two conversation keys with a request and an ack in each, §9.2, §9.4, 1.3), confirm, ask person (with `again`), heard, release with a `{question}` wait, decide (with `supersedes`), retract, approve, object, resolve, merge, key remove, ask agent, answer, say (1.4: to `holder:` and `holders:` of a node the sender holds, so that the skip of the sender is reachable), wait, take, next, close, tick, tick_next | Q1 (a repeat of one message is one request, and two messages of one conversation are two, A-61), C1 (on `where`, and a reply fulfils only the open commitments of its own conversation, §9.2, 1.3), Settled (superseded and retracted decisions, restructuring, A-12, and a reply that answers only its own conversation, 1.3), F, W1, E1 (questions), D1, M1, N5, T2 (rechecks, expiry, and escalation) |
| `user` | hello (with a principal), from_user, to_user (each with a principal of `PRINCIPALS`, and to_user of each kind, A-23; neither in `user_none`), route, ask user (to `user` or a principal), ask person (blocking, so that escalations arise), next (open, so that classes become active with their caps, CS-7), release `cannot`, release with a `{question}` wait on a people or a user question, update (needs, CS-7; owners and the `gone` tag, D-3), create under `@people` (person keys as aliases) and `@teams`, with capacity 0 or 1 and with or without a hold, so that a released person or team gets no `offer` tag and `next` takes it only by a flag (A-113), decide, retract, take, close, tick, tick_next | N1, E1 (with (e) and (f), the quorum, and needs-aware active classes), D1, Settled (a report to `p1` never answers `p2`'s request unless they are aliases of one person, and only a `result` answers, A-23), M1, U1 (with `step_U1` and `hello_exact`, over aliases and owners), T2 (re-addressing and lapses, with their marks and `assume_now`) |
| `recurring` | create series, take, next, checkpoint (intent), release (with and without `intent_done`, 1.4), close, update repeat (on open and closed series), update of the series' content and needs while an occurrence waits (1.4, the copy at its slot), reopen, move, tick, tick_next | K6, R2, F (overdue, missed), T2, M1, O2 (1.4: the copy at the slot bumps the occurrence's `version` exactly when its content changes) |
| `basis` (D-4, CS-22) | create, take, next, close (outcomes `done`, `failed`, `dropped`), reopen, merge, decide (with `supersedes` and a basis of node and entry references, `at` itself among them, which 1.4 drops, R14), retract (a decision, another entry, a node), object, resolve, tick | F (`basis_changed`: one hop, set by a close with another outcome, a retraction, or a supersession, never by a reopen or a merge; cleared by a supersession or a retraction of the citing decision), W1, M1, O3 (`retracted` only grows) |

**T2 as a state invariant.** Settling is a pure function in the model, so T2 is checked over every
reachable state, not only in one `run` test:

```quint
val inv_T2 = tuples(0.to(K), 0.to(K)).forall(((a, b)) =>
  a <= b implies run(run(s, clock + a), clock + b) == run(s, clock + b))
```

with `run` the settle of D.10.4 and `K = 12` in simulation and TLC, `K = 4` in Apalache (`K = 2` in
the `user` and `people` slices if Apalache needs it). A saturated fold fails `inv_settle_bound` on its
own, so truncation cannot make T2 pass or fail. `inv_T2` is in `holds` and `recurring`, where
deadlines are densest, and in `user`, `user_none` included, and `people`, where the firings of
CS-2 (re-addressing, lapses with their marks and `assume_now`) and of rechecks, expiry, and
escalation occur.

Swarm liveness (§27, strong fairness of taking each flagged node) is an assumption about the
environment; it is stated in a comment and run only as a TLC experiment. Results hold only within
these bounds (§28).

### D.10.8 Replaying model traces and counterexamples against the core

`crates/forum-conformance` holds a quint-connect driver for `quint run --mbt` traces:

```rust
#[quint_run(spec = "../../model/instances/two_class.qnt", max_samples = 300, max_steps = 40)]
fn simulation() -> impl Driver { ForumDriver::default() }

#[quint_test(spec = "../../model/tests/forum_test.qnt", test = "scenario_32")]
fn scenario_32() -> impl Driver { ForumDriver::default() }

#[derive(Default)]
struct ForumDriver { s: forum_core::State, clock: u64, ops: BTreeMap<(String, String), QCmd>,
                     tie: TieBreak }

impl Driver for ForumDriver {
    type State = QState;                     // mirrors D.10.3; Deserialize from ITF
    fn config() -> Config { Config { state: &["s", "clock"], nondet: &[] } }
    fn step(&mut self, step: &Step) -> Result {
        switch!(step {
            init => self.init(),             // genesis and the seed of D.10.7
            act_tick(dt) => self.tick(dt),
            act_tick_next => self.tick_next(),
            act_take(sess, n, lease, op?) => self.cmd(sess, op, take_cmd(n, lease)),
            // one arm per action of D.10.4, including retract, approve, ask_agent, answer,
            // wait, and hide
        })
    }
}
impl State<ForumDriver> for QState {
    fn from_driver(d: &ForumDriver) -> Result<Self> { Ok(project(&d.s, d.clock, &d.ops)) }
}
```

- **Pipeline.** The driver runs the shell's pipeline (`settle`, `apply_with`, `settle`) with
  `now = T0 + clock × 60_000` and the scaled params, and compares states after every step. A time
  action settles to the new clock. Ids match without translation, because both sides allocate node
  ids, eids, session ids, and fences in the same order. Content integers map to node content as
  `title = "c<v>"` with the other content fields held constant; node references are always sent to
  Rust as `#id`, so path resolution is not part of the comparison (K3 and K4 check it). An action
  with `long` sends its first free text (a title, a checkpoint's `done`, a reason, or a summary) as
  `text.max + 1` bytes of the replay params, and its outcome must be `limit(TextTooLong)` with no
  events (D.10.4).
- **Next calls** (1.3). After every step that names a session, the driver compares that session's
  next calls: Rust's `query::guide_items` (feature `conformance`: the items of D.8.26 before the
  cut, after the dedupe), restricted to the rules `guide.qnt` models, against the model's
  `guide(s, sess, last_action)` with the same dedupe, item by item by rule, `when`, tool, action,
  and the ids, tokens, and versions the skeleton carries (texts and `why` are not compared). Rule
  3's due items compare because both sides use the ticks of D.10.5. So `guide.qnt` and
  `query::guide` cannot drift apart, and `inv_G1` checks the rules the code runs.
- **Projection.** `project(&State, clock, ops) -> QState` drops what the model abstracts (indices,
  `stats`, `since`, `held_ms`, `counters.events`, `params`, tz tables, text, the cited version and
  the external references of a basis, `leaving`, history the model does not keep, and
  `digest_left`, `people_left`, and `left`, which change only when something leaves memory after
  FINISHED_RETAIN or DIGEST_RETAIN, which no model run reaches) and parses keys and
  names into the model's sum types (the inverses of `KeyStr::of_user_entry`, `KeyStr::of_occurrence`,
  `forum_cron::slot_name`, and the signal-name format of D.8.19). A `Msg(c, n)` origin is sent to Rust
  as the message form of `Conv(c)`'s chat key, with `/<n>` appended (D.11.14), and parsed back the
  same way (A-61). Principal keys are model strings
  as they are (`user`, `p1`, `p2`, sent to Rust as `test:p1`, `test:p2`; a `Person` key as
  `person:<key>`), and the projection compares `State::user_msgs`, history in Rust, with the model's
  `user_msgs` field (D.10.3).
- **The retry store.** Rust stores a SHA-256 digest, the session, and the expiry (CS-8); the model
  stores the abstract command in place of the digest, and the same session and expiry. The driver
  keeps the map from `(class, op)` to the model command it sent, and compares `ops` by key set,
  command, session, and expiry. Outcomes are compared through `last_action` against the `OpRecorded`
  event and the reply: `Ok` or the error code, the ids the outcome allocated, and the `Replay` marker.
  Warnings are dropped, because the model does not compute some of them (`uncovered_slot`,
  `user_saturated`).
- **Tie-break.** Traces from the slices (`USE_FNV = false`) replay through `apply_with(..,
  TieBreak::Id)` (D.6.1, feature `conformance`); simulation traces replay with `TieBreak::Fnv`. A
  tied `next` in an Apalache or TLC counterexample therefore does not diverge falsely.
- quint-connect runs `quint` from `PATH`; `scripts/verify.sh` prepends `model/node_modules/.bin`.
- **Counterexamples and the ITF path.** In Quint 0.33.0 only `quint run --mbt` (experimental) writes
  `mbt::actionTaken` and `mbt::nondetPicks`, which quint-connect's `switch!` reads; `quint verify
  --out-itf` has no such option, so Apalache and TLC counterexamples carry no action names. Replay of
  any ITF file therefore reads the model's own `last_action` variable (action name, parameters, op,
  outcome, and the flags of its settle), which every ITF state carries from every backend. A hand-written driver (about 300
  lines over the `itf` 0.4 crate) does this for counterexamples and for any trace quint-connect
  cannot express; quint-connect drives only the `--mbt` traces. WP-F1 tests the hand-written driver
  on a counterexample that the `holds` slice produces for a deliberately false invariant. If the core
  reproduces the violating state, the bug is in the core (or the invariant); if it does not, the
  model and the core disagree, which is itself a conformance failure to resolve. This tells model
  bugs from core bugs.
- The reverse direction is history replay: in CI, histories are folded through `evolve`, compared
  with the state tables they came with, and checked with `check_invariants` (D.12.6, FQ-2).
  tla-connect's post-hoc validation (§28) is not used in the first release; it may be evaluated
  later.

## D.11 The shell (`forum-server`)

### D.11.1 Libraries

Checked on crates.io for this design (2026-10-01), with the features confirmed in each crate's
manifest:

| Need | Choice | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| MCP | `rmcp = "3.5"`, features `server`, `transport-streamable-http-server` | The official SDK (`modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk`). `StreamableHttpService` is a tower service; `StreamableHttpServerConfig` has `legacy_session_mode` and `allowed_hosts`. The handler implements `ServerHandler` by hand (`get_info`, `list_tools`, `call_tool`): six tools with hand-written schemas keep decoding, and the digest, under our control |
| HTTP | `axum = "0.8"` | `Router::new().nest_service("/mcp", service)` plus the bearer layer, and `/healthz` outside it |
| Runtime | `tokio = "1"` (`rt-multi-thread`, `macros`, `sync`, `time`, `signal`) | The core never sees it |
| SQLite | `rusqlite = "0.40"`, features `bundled`, `hooks`, `backup` | Pins SQLite (`libsqlite3-sys` 0.38), with FTS5, into the binary (WP-E1 confirms FTS5 and `contentless_delete` with `PRAGMA compile_options` and a probe); `hooks` gives the progress handler that bounds a search (D.11.12), `backup` the online backup of D.11.8 |
| Time zones | `jiff = "0.2"` (`default-features = false`, `std`, `tzdb-bundle-always`) and `jiff-tzdb = "0.1"` | Bundled database: the system zoneinfo is never read; `jiff_tzdb::VERSION` (currently `2026c`) is the provenance recorded in each `TzTable` |
| Hashing | `sha2 = "0.11"` | `op_id` digests and bearer-token hashes |
| JSON | `serde`, `serde_json` | Tool I/O, events, canonical digests |
| Compression | `zstd = "0.14"` (over `zstd-safe` 8) | The history's event bodies (D.11.6): each text is stored once, compressed |
| Masking | `regex = "1"` | Linear-time matching |
| Config | `toml = "1"` | The server settings and parameters; bearer tokens come from the environment or a `.env` file, read by a small parser of the shell's own (D.11.3, no crate) |
| Logging | `tracing`, `tracing-subscriber` | |
| Tests | `rmcp` feature `transport-streamable-http-client-reqwest` (dev), `proptest = "1.11"` (dev) | |

### D.11.2 Process structure

```
main
 ├─ config::resolve(environment, flags)      TOML, the environment, and `.env`, once (the only
 │                                           std::env and fs reads, D.11.3, D.11.9)
 ├─ store::open(db)                          schema creation, migrations (D.7.6), PRAGMAs
 ├─ engine::start(store, config)             load the state tables (D.11.8), then the threads
 └─ axum server
      /mcp   rmcp StreamableHttpService<ForumServer, LocalSessionManager>
      layer  auth::bearer                    Authorization → class and default caps, or HTTP 401
      /healthz                               200 `ok`, outside the layer (no token, no Host check)
threads: the writer; the checkpointer; the search feeder; a pool of read-only search connections
```

- **Writer thread.** One OS thread owns the read-write `rusqlite::Connection` and the in-memory
  `forum_core::State`. Tool handlers send `Job { class, mcp_session, tool, cmd, op, hits,
  queued_at, reply: oneshot }` (`hits`: the search results of D.11.12, for rendering only) into a
  bounded queue per class and lane (QUEUE_MAX, 20,000 jobs, about what the writer runs within
  `queue.max_wait` at its lowest measured rate of 2,200 calls a second; QUEUE_TOTAL_MAX, 80,000, in
  all; a call that does not fit is answered `limit(Busy)` before it is queued); the thread takes jobs from the classes that have some by deficit
  round-robin (one job per class per round, arrival order within a class) and runs D.8.1 for each.
  This is the single writer of §24: one call at a time, no locks around the state. The order of jobs
  is the shell's; the history records the order the writer chose.
- **Group commit** (CS-13, review TP-4, RS-1, FS-2). The thread runs the jobs it takes in groups:
  one transaction for at most COMMIT_GROUP_MAX (64) jobs, or for those that arrive within
