### D.15.6 Fixed decisions and the answers

The review asked six questions about the fixed decisions of AGENTS.md. All six were answered; none
is open, and none reopens a decision. The rows of D.14 give the wording for 1.2.

| Fixed decision | The review's question | The answer | Design |
|---|---|---|---|
| All agents are trusted (FQ-1) | One company forum shows every employee's agent conversations to every other employee's agents: acceptable? | Yes, and intended: everything in a forum is visible to every agent, colleagues' conversations included, and 1.2 says so. No read filter, and no principal filter in automatic search; per-principal delivery of questions, digest entries, and notes is routing to the right person, not privacy | D.11.12, D.14 |
| A single writer with SQLite (FQ-2) | A restart replays 6 to 61 hours per year of log, and a state hash saturates the writer: who writes snapshots? | The SQLite state tables are the source of truth, written in the transaction of the events that change them and loaded at startup, where `check_invariants` runs (the linear subset at every startup, the full check where it is cheap enough: debug builds, `--check`, CI; the split was confirmed at G0, G0-a); the event log is append-only history for views, export, debugging, and CI replay; no state hash, hash chain, snapshot, or log segment; nothing is deleted; SQLite's file limit is a known limit, with rotation into archive files a later operational item (D.15.2) | D.4.2, D.6.1, D.7.6, D.9.1, D.11.6, D.11.8 |
| Anyone can stop work (FQ-3) | Should a pause of `/` last 15 minutes unless a second session renews it? | No: the rule stays, and only its visibility is added | D.8.21, D.8.22, D.11.7 |
| Nothing is deleted (FQ-4) | May feed texts be crypto-shredded? | No: nothing is deleted and nothing is shredded; masking before anything is stored is the protection | D.11.13, D.11.15 |
| MCP-only (FQ-5) | Where do bulk artefacts and directories of people live? | The forum holds coordination state and references; artefacts (code, proofs, data) live outside, referenced by URL or path with an optional content hash the server does not enforce; the directories of people (principals), teams, owners, aliases, and `gone` marks are maintained by agents through MCP, not by server configuration, preferably as ordinary forum nodes and fields under reserved paths (`@people/<principal>`, `@teams/<team>`) with an inherited owners field, handled by the existing node commands, and a command only if a concrete failure requires it; agent bearer tokens (token to class, optional default caps) are configuration from environment variables or a `.env` file and never enter the forum. The design follows it with three stated departures of detail: a person's node name is free and its keys are `person:<principal key>` keys (a key may contain `/`, and one human has several); owners are a structured setting (the core parses no text); a team's members are its `owners` (links cannot be removed). The forum's default addressee is ROOT's owners, not a parameter (D-3, D.11.9) | D.2.2, D.4.3, D.8.11, D.8.12, D.11.3, D.11.9 |
| Pull-only (FQ-6) | May the writer fire due deadlines while it is idle? | Yes: it contacts nobody, and by T2 the events are the same as at the next call | D.8.2, D.11.2 |

With them it was decided that O1 stays exact with the simplest mechanism: the request digest is a
plain SHA-256 of the masked request, not a keyed one (D.11.5); the `st_ops` row keeps the masking
version, so a retry across an upgrade of the masker is still exact.

### D.15.7 Could and later items of the review

Not in the first release, each with the failure it would prevent and what would make it needed:

| Item | The failure it would prevent | Why not now | Needed when |
|---|---|---|---|
| RS-12, a `checked` evidence kind | A proof that a machine checked cannot be told apart from an observation | Evidence is stored only (§29), and a variant can be appended to `Evidence` later without breaking an event (D.7.6); decisions recorded before it keep their kind | reviewers or a later check must tell machine-checked results apart |
| RS-14, reviewer independence | Results relied on after self-approval | Review routing works with offered review nodes (`needs: [review]`) | the year simulation or the history shows self-approved results relied on |
| RS-19, effort sinks | A lemma that absorbs hundreds of agent-hours unseen, because checkpoints reset `attempts` | The data exist (`held_ms`, `fence`) | such sinks show up in the capacity report |
| RS-25, an `outcome` filter on `view list` | "What has failed under lemma L?" cannot be listed | CS-32's counts and the search's rendering of closed results cover the common case | agents repeat failed approaches that search does not surface |
| FS-13, holds without progress as attempts | Tier-0 items re-taken for ever during an outage | D-8 | D-8 |
| FS-14, occurrences that share their series' text | A text copy per occurrence | Bounded by the occurrences open at once (K6); the `continues` half is in the first release, as A-111, because the links grew as O(n²) in state and events, not only in the brief's rendering | a gate shows the cost |
| TP-17, cheaper moves of large subtrees | A move of 10⁵ descendants takes about 0.1 s of writer time | Rare, and the rollups move at O(depth) (CS-32) | moves of that size become common |
| RS-26, artefacts by content hash | — | Adopted as FQ-5's clarification: references with an optional, unchecked hash | — |

MU-6 and MU-16, a directory with `gone` marks and aliases, left this list: with MU-8 and MU-9's owners
and teams they are in the first release, as forum data (D-3, FQ-5).

## D.16 Next calls in the examples (1.3)

The evidence behind 1.3 (§20.9, D.14.3), and the expected values of its scenario tests (D.12.2).
1.4's rules (D.14.4) change four rows of §32 below, each marked: step 1's create, which returns
`uncovered_slot` (rule 3, R18); step 6's two calls of `s-6` (rule 3's why, R6, and rule 8's
`later` close after `intent_done`, R11); and step 7's decision on audit, whose close item now names
the alternative in its `why` (R11). The other rules of 1.4 do not fire in §32; rule 8's `why`
changes wherever it suggests a close, and the rows below show it only where they quote a `why`.
The re-run's rule 7 on a held node (R28, D.14.5) adds a `later` decision to two more rows, each
marked: the series' create in step 1 and `s-1`'s create in step 2, each of which records a request
on the node it holds. Step 1's clarification, of a request the `to_user` just settled, is a new
request that follows it (D.14.5), and has a row of its own.

**The walkthrough.** Three scenarios were played as an agent that knows only the instructions (§22)
and the tool descriptions (§20.2) and reads each response. At every response the walkthrough
recorded the call the protocol expects next, and whether the response of 1.2 names it (an error's
hint, `leave_better`, `{existing}` with its holder) or leaves it to the agent's memory of the
specification:

| Scenario | Responses | With a protocol step due | Named by the response in 1.2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| §32, steps 1 to 8 | 34 | 27 | 3 (an `{existing}` with its holder, two `leave_better` lists) |
| A company session: Alice's IDE agent, and a worker that answers Bob | 11 | 9 | 0 |
| An autonomous worker with no human | 7 | 6 | 0 |
| All | 52 | 42 | 3 |

The 39 others fall into six families, which the rules of §20.9 cover: arrival (the human's words
just logged, or the event the session came for); pairs that must close (`said` and its confirmation,
an intent and `intent_done`, an `ask` and the release that waits on it, a question to the human and
the answer's `from_user {answers}`, a `from_user` and its routing); finishing in order (decide, a
`result` to the requester, close, or a release for a series); what a flag on a held node asks; the
human's pending questions and digest; and idle work. Every family is a function of the state after
the call, the caller, and the call; none needs the text of an entry.

**§32 with next calls.** `→` marks a call the example then makes from a next call, and `→ (guided)`
one that only the guided run of D.12.2 makes. Items are listed in the order they are rendered;
"later:" marks a `later` item.

| Step | Call | `next_calls` of its response |
|---|---|---|

Fifteen calls are made from a next call, two of them only in the guided run (the series' release in
step 1 and `s-3`'s `view node` in step 4); the fifteenth, the close of rerun-test after its
`intent_done`, is suggested since 1.4 (R11). 1.2's responses name none of them as a call: they state
the facts (a flag in the brief, `open_question` in a join, a node in `leave_better`) from which an
agent that knows the specification could derive it. Every other call after a session's first is a
judgement only the agent can make: what to split, when the work is done, what to say, which node to
take next.

**Two traces that §32 does not exercise** (the company scenario of D.12.2):
- **A worker answers Bob.** A worker that serves no principal takes Bob's node through `next` and
  records `talk decide {settles: [r61]}`. Rule 6 suggests `talk to_user {principal:
  mail:bob@example.org, kind: result, re: [r61]}`. Without the filled principal, its `to_user`
  resolves to `user` (§8.1), `r61` stays unsettled, the closed node keeps `unanswered_request`, and a
  second agent reports to Bob again.
- **Alice arrives.** `session hello {principal: alice, from_user}` with two questions and one digest
  entry pending for her: rule 5 suggests creating the work for her message, and rule 12 one
  `to_user {principal: alice, kind: question, re: [d3]}` that asks both questions and summarises
  `d3`. That call's response carries `answers_next` (later: `talk from_user {answers: q7}`, "when
  alice answers q7"). Since 1.4 (R13) the rule 12 item stands on every response of the session
  until that `to_user`, so an agent that first does other work still sees it.

## Appendix A. Traceability: specification to design

One row per requirement-bearing statement. "Where" names types (D.2–D.7), functions and algorithms
(D.8), checks (D.9), the model (D.10), or the shell (D.11). WP-F3 keeps this table in
`docs/verification.md` as the check that nothing in the specification is lost.

### A.1 Part 1 (§0–§6)

| Spec | Statement | Where |
|---|---|---|
| §0 | One shared MCP server; a tree of nodes with feeds, holds with leases and fencing tokens, checkpoints | `State::nodes`, `entries`, `holds`, `Token`, `Ev::HoldExtended`, `EntryBody::Checkpoint` |
| §0 | One log of all communication with the user | `USER`, `EntryBody::FromUser`, `EntryBody::ToUser`, each with its principal (CS-1) |
| §0, §1 | Pull only | No outbound IO in the shell; `talk wait` is a long poll the agent starts (D.11.11) |
| §0, §2 | Trusted agents; no permission model | `Ctx::class` is read only for history, `op_id` scope, refusals, and session ownership (A-69); principals are addressing and views, never permissions; everything in a forum is visible to every agent, with no read filter (CS-1, FQ-1) |
| §0 | Notices rather than forbids; refusals only for corruption or safety valves | `Warning` (D.6.4); `Error` limited to §21 (D.6.3) |

## Appendix B. Entity states (§25) to events

| Entity | Transition | Event |
|---|---|---|
| Node | creation (open) | `NodeCreated` |
| Node | open → closed(outcome) | `NodeClosed` |
| Node | closed → open (reopen, or taking a flagged closed node that is not merged, A-94, A-96, nor marked upheld, 1.8) | `NodeReopened` |
| Node | closed(o) → closed(o′) marked upheld (1.8, §11.3) | `NodeCorrected` |
| Node | closed(o′) marked upheld → closed(o) unmarked, by a second verdict (1.10, §11.3) | `CorrectionWithdrawn` |
| Hold | creation (live) | `HoldIssued` |
| Hold | live → live (checkpoint) | `HoldExtended { by: Checkpoint }` |
| Hold | live → live (renew) | `HoldExtended { by: Renew }` |
| Hold | live → released | `HoldEnded { Released }` |
| Hold | live → expired | `Fired { Lease }`, then `HoldEnded { Expired }` |
| Hold | live → ended_by_close | `HoldEnded { EndedByClose(Close \| Merge \| Move) }` (A-6) |
| Intent | creation (open) | `IntentOpened` |
| Intent | open → done, by `intent_done` in a checkpoint or, 1.4, a release (R15), or, 1.8, a check | `IntentClosed { Done }` |
| Intent | open → resolved_by_close | `IntentClosed { ResolvedByClose }` |
| Intent, request, question (people), commitment, objection, `said` | moved by a merge, same state (N5, A-94) | `IntentMoved`, `RequestMoved`, `PqMoved`, `CommitmentMoved`, `ObjectionMoved`, `SaidMoved` |
| Request | creation (open) | `Appended(Request)` |
| Request | open → settled | `RequestSettled` (after `RequestAnswered` and a decision) |
| Question (people) | creation, open(0) | `Appended(Question(People))` |
| Question (people) | open(k) → open(k+1) | `Fired { Recheck }`, then `PqRechecked` |
| Question (people) | open → answered | `PqAnswered` |
| Question (people) | open → superseded | `PqSuperseded` |
| Question (people) | open → expired (last recheck, non-blocking) | `PqExpired` |
| Question (people) | open → escalated (last recheck, blocking) | `PqEscalated` |
| Question (people) | expired, escalated → answered | `PqAnswered` (the lapse is kept) |
| Question (user) | creation, pending(0), with its chain (CS-2) | `Appended(Question(User))` |
| Question (user) | pending → answered | `UqAnswered` |
| Question (user) | pending → defaulted | `Fired { UserQuestion }`, then `UqDefaulted` |
| Question (user) | pending(k) → pending(k+1), re-addressed (CS-2) | `Fired { UserQuestion }`, then `UqReaddressed` |
| Question (user) | pending → lapsed, at the last stage's due (CS-2) | `Fired { UserQuestion }`, then `UqLapsed` (and `MarkSet`, or `assume_now`) |
| Question (user) | lapsed: its assumption recorded (CS-2) | `UqAssumed` |
| Commitment | creation (open) | `CommitmentOpened` |
| Commitment | open → open (refreshed by an `ack` in its conversation) | `CommitmentRefreshed` |
| Commitment | open → fulfilled (by a reply, result, or correction in its conversation, 1.3) | `CommitmentFulfilled` |
| `said` | creation (pending) | `Appended(Said)` |
| `said` | pending → confirmed; unconfirmed → confirmed | `SaidConfirmed` |
| `said` | pending → unconfirmed | `SaidUnconfirmed` (at the session's silence, or for an entry listed in `unsent` at a release or close, 1.5) |
| `said` | pending → withheld; withheld → confirmed | `SaidWithheld` (1.9: listed in `unsent` after a later `said` replaced it; 1.9's withholding of a `said` recorded by a session that holds neither its conversation node nor work inside it while another does is gone since 1.10); `SaidConfirmed` (its author's confirm) |
| `from_user` entry | creation (unrouted), with its principal (CS-1) | `Appended(FromUser { principal })` |
| `from_user` entry | unrouted → routed | `EntryRouted { Request \| Clarifies }` |
| `from_user` entry | unrouted → answered | `EntryRouted { Answers }` |
| `from_user` entry | unrouted → no_action | `EntryRouted { NoAction }` |
| Objection | creation (open) | `Appended(Object)` |
| Objection | open → resolved \| upheld (1.8) | `ObjectionResolved { upheld }` |
| Objection | a second, opposite verdict on a resolved one: a new open objection (1.10) | `Appended(Object)` by `resolve_exec` |
| Decision | creation (active), with its basis references (CS-22) | `Appended(Decision { basis })`; its node's `basis_changed` (a flag, not a §25 state, D-4) then follows the targets' `NodeClosed`, `NodeReopened`, `DecisionSuperseded`, `DecisionRetracted`, and `Appended(Retract)` |
| Decision | active → superseded | `DecisionSuperseded` |
| Decision | active → retracted | `DecisionRetracted` (a superseded decision still settles, A-11) |
| Retracted target (added, D-4; not a §25 entity) | a node or an entry struck out, for good | `Appended(Retract { target })` |
| Wait | creation (unresolved) | `WaitSet { Some(_) }` |
| Wait | unresolved → resolved | a predicate (T3): `Fired { Wait }` for time waits, `Pq*`/`Uq*` for question waits, the target's `NodeClosed` for node waits re-materialise the flags; `WaitSet { None }` and `NodeClosed` remove the wait |
| Wait | resolved → unresolved (a `{node}` wait whose target reopens, A-55) | the target's `NodeReopened` (through `waiters`) |
| Wait | replaced by a wait on the user question at an escalation (A-93) | `WaitSet { Some(UserQuestion(uq)) }` |
| Wait | ended by a checkpoint of a live hold on its node (1.10, §10.2) | `WaitSet { None }`, emitted by `checkpoint_exec` |
| Signal | creation (open) | `NodeCreated` (role `Signal`), `SignalOpened` |
| Signal | open → resolved | `NodeClosed` of the signal node, `SignalResolved` |
| Signal | resolved → open (reopen with the key free, A-89) | `NodeReopened`, `SignalOpened` |
| Signal | detached (reopen with the key taken, A-89) | `SignalDetached`, `NodeReopened` |
| Occurrence | creation (waiting) | `NodeCreated` (role `Occurrence`, phase `Waiting`) |
| Occurrence | waiting → available, copying the series' title, body, needs, and est (1.4, R10) | `Fired { OccurrenceSlot }`, then `NodeUpdated` with the fields that differ, if any, then `OccurrenceAvailable` |
| Occurrence | available ⇄ held | `HoldIssued` / `HoldEnded` on the occurrence |
| Occurrence | available → closed; held → closed | `NodeClosed { outcome ≠ Missed }` |
| Occurrence | available → missed | `NodeClosed { Missed }` (via `maybe_missed`) |
| Occurrence | waiting → dropped | `NodeClosed { Dropped }` (series close, `repeat` change, or an agent's close as `dropped`, A-91); no other transition leaves `waiting` except to `available` |
| Occurrence | detached (A-13, A-75) | `OccurrenceDetached` |
| Refusal | creation (live), one entry per refusing session; the class has refused at its quorum (CS-7) | `Refused` |
| Refusal | live → expired, per entry; the record goes with its last (CS-7) | `Fired { RefusalExpiry }`, then `RefusalExpired` |
| Refusal | live → cleared (A-56) | `RefusalsCleared` |
| Digest entry | creation (pending), one per audience principal (CS-5) | `Appended(System(Digest { item, to }))` |
| Digest entry | pending → shown, by a `to_user` to its principal or an alias of it | `DigestShown` |
| Digest entry | pending → left unshown after DIGEST_RETAIN (added, CS-5, D.4.12; not a §25 state change: it stays in `@user/digest`) | dropped by `evolve` at the first event at or after it, counted in `digest_left` |
| Pause | creation, active(until) | `Paused { renewed: false }` |
| Pause | active(until) → active(until′) | `Paused { renewed: true }` |
| Pause | active → lifted | `Unpaused` |
| Pause | active → expired | `Fired { Pause }`, then `PauseExpired` |
| Session | creation (live) | `SessionOpened` |
| Session | a principal bound (CS-1; not a §25 state, a field) | `SessionOpened { principal }`, `SessionHello { principal }`, `Appended(FromUser)` |
| Principal (added, CS-1) | creation (interned; never removed) | `PrincipalSeen` (`user` by `Genesis`) |
| Session | live → silent, once `presence.silence` has passed since its last refresh and it holds no live hold (1.4, R27) | `Fired { Silence }`, at the later of `silence_at` and its last lease's end (D.4.8) |
| Session | silent → live | `Touched` |
| Session | silent → retired, `session.retain` after its last touch, holding nothing (CS-8) | `Fired { Retire }`, then `SessionRetired` |
| `op_id` record (added, CS-8; not a §25 entity) | live → expired at `expires_at` | dropped by `evolve` at the first event at or after it |
| Note (added, CS-17; not a §25 entity) | delivered until `until` → expired | dropped by `evolve` at the first event at or after `until`, with an agent question's `AQuestion` (D.4.12) |
| Any finished entity (added, D-5; not a §25 transition) | resident → left memory, `FINISHED_RETAIN` after it finished and nothing held it back; left memory → resident, when a command names it | dropped by `evolve` at the first event at or after that time; `Restored` |
| Class caps profile (added, A-27, CS-7) | in window → out of window | `Fired { RefusalExpiry, Class(c) }`; into the window, or renewed, by `NextCalled { open: true }` |

The board states of §8.3 are a function of these states (`query::board`).
